# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic Basic HTTP authentication. Allowed headers-- Authorization: Basic <api_key> | Authorization: Basic <base64 hash of `api_key:`>

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Bearer HTTP authentication. Allowed headers-- Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

<h1 id="stripe-api-default">Default</h1>

## Retrieve account

<a id="opIdGetAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/account \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/account`

<p>Retrieves the details of an account.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create an account link

<a id="opIdPostAccountLinks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/account_links \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account=string&collect=currently_due&collection_options=%7B%22fields%22%3A%22currently_due%22%2C%22future_requirements%22%3A%22include%22%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&refresh_url=string&return_url=string&type=account_onboarding'
```

`POST /v1/account_links`

<p>Creates an AccountLink object that includes a single-use Stripe URL that the platform can redirect their user to in order to take them through the Connect Onboarding flow.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account: string
collect: currently_due
collection_options:
  fields: currently_due
  future_requirements: include
expand:
  - string
refresh_url: string
return_url: string
type: account_onboarding
```

<h3 id="create-an-account-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account|body|string|true|The identifier of the account to create an account link for.|
|» collect|body|string|false|The collect parameter is deprecated. Use `collection_options` instead.|
|» collection_options|body|object|false|Specifies the requirements that Stripe collects from connected accounts in the Connect Onboarding flow.|
|» » fields|body|string|false|none|
|» » future_requirements|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» refresh_url|body|string|false|The URL the user will be redirected to if the account link is expired, has been previously-visited, or is otherwise invalid. The URL you specify should attempt to generate a new account link with the same parameters used to create the original account link, then redirect the user to the new account link's URL so they can continue with Connect Onboarding. If a new account link cannot be generated or the redirect fails you should display a useful error to the user.|
|» return_url|body|string|false|The URL that the user will be redirected to upon leaving or completing the linked flow.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of account link the user is requesting.<br><br>You can create Account Links of type `account_update` only for connected accounts where your platform is responsible for collecting requirements, including Custom accounts. You can't create them for accounts that have access to a Stripe-hosted Dashboard. If you use [Connect embedded components](/connect/get-started-connect-embedded-components), you can include components that allow your connected accounts to update their own information. For an account without Stripe-hosted Dashboard access where Stripe is liable for negative balances, you must use embedded components.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» collect|currently_due|
|» collect|eventually_due|
|» » fields|currently_due|
|» » fields|eventually_due|
|» » future_requirements|include|
|» » future_requirements|omit|
|» type|account_onboarding|
|» type|account_update|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "object": "account_link",
  "url": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "advice_code": "string",
    "charge": "string",
    "code": "string",
    "decline_code": "string",
    "doc_url": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "network_advice_code": "string",
    "network_decline_code": "string",
    "param": "string",
    "payment_intent": {},
    "payment_method": {},
    "payment_method_type": "string",
    "request_log_url": "string",
    "setup_intent": {},
    "source": {},
    "type": "api_error"
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[account_link](#schemaaccount_link)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Create an Account Session

<a id="opIdPostAccountSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
```

`POST /v1/account_sessions`

<p>Creates an AccountSession object that includes a single-use token that the platform can use on their front-end to grant client-side API access.</p>

## List all connected accounts

<a id="opIdGetAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts`

<p>Returns a list of accounts connected to your platform via <a href="/docs/connect">Connect</a>. If you’re not a platform, the list is empty.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-connected-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return connected accounts that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="list-all-connected-accounts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-all-connected-accounts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[account](#schemaaccount)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

`POST /v1/accounts`

<p>With <a href="/docs/connect">Connect</a>, you can create Stripe accounts for your users.
To do this, you’ll first need to <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/applications/settings">register your platform</a>.</p>

<p>If you’ve already collected information for your connected accounts, you <a href="/connect/marketplace/tasks/create#prefill-account-information">can prefill that information</a> when
creating the account. Connect Onboarding won’t ask for the prefilled information during account onboarding.
You can prefill any information on the account.</p>

## Retrieve account

<a id="opIdGetAccountsAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account}`

<p>Retrieves the details of an account.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-account-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}`

<p>Updates a <a href="/connect/accounts">connected account</a> by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided are
left unchanged.</p>

<p>For accounts where <a href="/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection">controller.requirement_collection</a>
is <code>application</code>, which includes Custom accounts, you can update any information on the account.</p>

<p>For accounts where <a href="/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection">controller.requirement_collection</a>
is <code>stripe</code>, which includes Standard and Express accounts, you can update all information until you create
an <a href="/api/account_links">Account Link</a> or <a href="/api/account_sessions">Account Session</a> to start Connect onboarding,
after which some properties can no longer be updated.</p>

<p>To update your own account, use the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/account">Dashboard</a>. Refer to our
<a href="/docs/connect/updating-accounts">Connect</a> documentation to learn more about updating accounts.</p>

## Update a bank account

<a id="opIdPostAccountsAccountBankAccountsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/bank_accounts/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account_holder_name=string&account_holder_type=&account_type=checking&address_city=string&address_country=string&address_line1=string&address_line2=string&address_state=string&address_zip=string&default_for_currency=true&documents=%7B%22bank_account_ownership_verification%22%3A%7B%22files%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D%7D&exp_month=string&exp_year=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/bank_accounts/{id}`

<p>Updates the metadata, account holder name, account holder type of a bank account belonging to
a connected account and optionally sets it as the default for its currency. Other bank account
details are not editable by design.</p>

<p>You can only update bank accounts when <a href="/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection">account.controller.requirement_collection</a> is <code>application</code>, which includes <a href="/connect/custom-accounts">Custom accounts</a>.</p>

<p>You can re-enable a disabled bank account by performing an update call without providing any
arguments or changes.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_holder_name: string
account_holder_type: ""
account_type: checking
address_city: string
address_country: string
address_line1: string
address_line2: string
address_state: string
address_zip: string
default_for_currency: true
documents:
  bank_account_ownership_verification:
    files:
      - string
exp_month: string
exp_year: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
```

<h3 id="update-a-bank-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» account_holder_name|body|string|false|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|
|» account_holder_type|body|string|false|The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`.|
|» account_type|body|string|false|The bank account type. This can only be `checking` or `savings` in most countries. In Japan, this can only be `futsu` or `toza`.|
|» address_city|body|string|false|City/District/Suburb/Town/Village.|
|» address_country|body|string|false|Billing address country, if provided when creating card.|
|» address_line1|body|string|false|Address line 1 (Street address/PO Box/Company name).|
|» address_line2|body|string|false|Address line 2 (Apartment/Suite/Unit/Building).|
|» address_state|body|string|false|State/County/Province/Region.|
|» address_zip|body|string|false|ZIP or postal code.|
|» default_for_currency|body|boolean|false|When set to true, this becomes the default external account for its currency.|
|» documents|body|object|false|Documents that may be submitted to satisfy various informational requests.|
|» » bank_account_ownership_verification|body|object|false|none|
|» » » files|body|[string]|false|none|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit number representing the card’s expiration month.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit number representing the card’s expiration year.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Cardholder name.|

|» account_type|savings|
|» account_type|toza|

## Create an external account

<a id="opIdPostAccountsAccountExternalAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/external_accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'bank_account=%7B%22account_holder_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_type%22%3A%22checking%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22documents%22%3A%7B%22bank_account_ownership_verification%22%3A%7B%22files%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D%7D%2C%22object%22%3A%22bank_account%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&default_for_currency=true&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&external_account=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/external_accounts`

<p>Create an external account for a given account.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
bank_account:
  account_holder_name: string
  account_holder_type: company
  account_number: string
  account_type: checking
  country: string
  currency: string
  documents:
    bank_account_ownership_verification:
      files:
        - string
  object: bank_account
  routing_number: string
default_for_currency: true
expand:
  - string
external_account: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

## Update a bank account

<a id="opIdPostAccountsAccountExternalAccountsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/external_accounts/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account_holder_name=string&account_holder_type=&account_type=checking&address_city=string&address_country=string&address_line1=string&address_line2=string&address_state=string&address_zip=string&default_for_currency=true&documents=%7B%22bank_account_ownership_verification%22%3A%7B%22files%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D%7D&exp_month=string&exp_year=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/external_accounts/{id}`

<p>Updates the metadata, account holder name, account holder type of a bank account belonging to
a connected account and optionally sets it as the default for its currency. Other bank account
details are not editable by design.</p>

<p>You can only update bank accounts when <a href="/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection">account.controller.requirement_collection</a> is <code>application</code>, which includes <a href="/connect/custom-accounts">Custom accounts</a>.</p>

<p>You can re-enable a disabled bank account by performing an update call without providing any
arguments or changes.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_holder_name: string
account_holder_type: ""
account_type: checking
address_city: string
address_country: string
address_line1: string
address_line2: string
address_state: string
address_zip: string
default_for_currency: true
documents:
  bank_account_ownership_verification:
    files:
      - string
exp_month: string
exp_year: string
```

## Delete a person

<a id="opIdDeleteAccountsAccountPeoplePerson"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/people/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/accounts/{account}/people/{person}`

<p>Deletes an existing person’s relationship to the account’s legal entity. Any person with a relationship for an account can be deleted through the API, except if the person is the <code>representative</code>. If your integration is using the <code>executive</code> parameter, you cannot delete the only verified <code>executive</code> on file.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="delete-a-person-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|person|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

```json
  "deleted": true,
  "id": "string",
  "object": "person"
}
```

## List all persons

<a id="opIdGetAccountsAccountPersons"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/persons \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account}/persons`

<p>Returns a list of people associated with the account’s legal entity. The people are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recent people appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-persons-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|relationship|query|object|false|Filters on the list of people returned based on the person's relationship to the account's company.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Delete a person

<a id="opIdDeleteAccountsAccountPersonsPerson"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/persons/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/accounts/{account}/persons/{person}`

<p>Deletes an existing person’s relationship to the account’s legal entity. Any person with a relationship for an account can be deleted through the API, except if the person is the <code>representative</code>. If your integration is using the <code>executive</code> parameter, you cannot delete the only verified <code>executive</code> on file.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|account|path|string|true|none|
|person|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Reject an account

<a id="opIdPostAccountsAccountReject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/reject \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&payouts_action=none&reason=credit'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/reject`

<p>With <a href="/connect">Connect</a>, you can reject accounts that you have flagged as suspicious.</p>

<p>Only accounts where your platform is liable for negative account balances, which includes Custom and Express accounts, can be rejected.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
payouts_action: none
reason: credit
```

<h3 id="reject-an-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» payouts_action|body|string|false|Whether to pause payouts on the account as part of the rejection. Defaults to `pause`. Use `none` to leave payouts enabled.|
|» reason|body|string|true|The reason for rejecting the account. Can be `fraud_payment_method_casher`, `fraud_payment_method_tester`, `fraud_no_intent_to_fulfill`, `fraud_other`, `credit`, `terms_of_service`, or `other`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» payouts_action|none|
|» payouts_action|pause|
|» reason|credit|
|» reason|fraud_no_intent_to_fulfill|
|» reason|fraud_other|
|» reason|fraud_payment_method_casher|
|» reason|fraud_payment_method_tester|
|» reason|other|
|» reason|terms_of_service|

## Unreject an account

<a id="opIdPostAccountsAccountUnreject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/string/unreject \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/unreject`

<p>With Connect, you can unreject accounts that you have previously rejected.</p>

<p>Only accounts that were rejected by your platform can be unrejected. This API cannot be used to unreject accounts that were rejected by Stripe.</p>

<p>Unreject will only enable charges and/or payouts if there are no other restrictions other than those placed by a previous rejection. If you have separately paused charges and/or payouts outside of rejection, those pauses will remain in place after unrejection.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="unreject-an-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|


|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|

## Update an application fee refund

<a id="opIdPostApplicationFeesFeeRefundsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/application_fees/string/refunds/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/application_fees/{fee}/refunds/{id}`

<p>Updates the specified application fee refund by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.</p>

<p>This request only accepts metadata as an argument.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

## Create an application fee refund

<a id="opIdPostApplicationFeesIdRefunds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/application_fees/string/refunds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/application_fees/{id}/refunds`

<p>Refunds an application fee that has previously been collected but not yet refunded.
Funds will be refunded to the Stripe account from which the fee was originally collected.</p>

<p>You can optionally refund only part of an application fee.
You can do so multiple times, until the entire fee has been refunded.</p>

<p>Once entirely refunded, an application fee can’t be refunded again.
This method will raise an error when called on an already-refunded application fee,
or when trying to refund more money than is left on an application fee.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

<h3 id="create-an-application-fee-refund-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer, in _cents (or local equivalent)_, representing how much of this fee to refund. Can refund only up to the remaining unrefunded amount of the fee.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|


`GET /v1/apps/installs`

<p>Returns a list of app installs. An app developer or embedding platform filtering by its own app sees the installs across the accounts that installed it; other callers see the installs on their own account. The key selects the environment: a live key lists live installs, a sandbox API key lists the installs on that sandbox, and the key of an app’s managed sandbox filtering by <code>app</code> lists that app’s installs across every sandbox. For existing accounts that still use legacy test mode, a test mode key lists legacy test mode installs.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-app-installs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|query|string|false|Only return installs made by this account. Only useful to app developers and embedding platforms, whose lists span the accounts that installed their app.|
|app|query|string|false|Only return installs for the app specified by this app ID.|
|approval_required|query|boolean|false|Only return installs whose installer must authorize pending permissions, content security policy entries, or endpoints.|
|channel|query|string|false|Only return installs in the distribution channel specified by this channel name.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return app installs that were created during the given date interval.|
|created_by|query|string|false|Only return installs created by the embedding platform specified by this account ID.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return installs with the given status.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create an app install

<a id="opIdPostAppsInstalls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/apps/installs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'app=string&channel=private_live&code_challenge=string&code_challenge_method=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/apps/installs`

<p>Creates an app install. An account installs its own private app with its own key; public and testing installs are made from the Dashboard. An app developer or embedding platform acting on a connected account through <code>Stripe-Account</code> installs or reinstalls its app there. For a private app, creating an install installs the newest completed upload; when that version is already installed with nothing pending, the existing install is returned.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
app: string
channel: private_live
code_challenge: string
code_challenge_method: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="create-an-app-install-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|string|true|The ID of the app to install.|
|» channel|body|string|false|The distribution channel to install from. Defaults to `public`. A private app must be installed on `private_test` or `private_live`, matching the mode of the API key.|
|» code_challenge|body|string|false|For OAuth apps, the PKCE code challenge used to issue the `auth_code` returned on the install. Must be 43 to 128 characters and contain only letters, numbers, `-`, `.`, `_`, and `~`. Only applies to installs made by the app developer or an embedding platform; ignored when an account installs its own private app.|
|» code_challenge_method|body|string|false|The method used to derive `code_challenge`. Required when `code_challenge` is provided, and must be `S256`.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» channel|private_live|
|» channel|private_test|
|» channel|public|
|» channel|testing|

## List all balance transactions

<a id="opIdGetBalanceHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance/history \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/balance/history`

<p>Returns a list of transactions that have contributed to the Stripe account balance (for example, charges, transfers, and so on). The transactions return in sorted order, with the most recent transactions appearing first.</p>

<p>The previous name of this endpoint was “Balance history,” and it used the path <code>/v1/balance/history</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-balance-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return transactions that were created during the given date interval.|
|currency|query|string(currency)|false|Only return transactions in a certain currency. Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## Update balance settings

<a id="opIdPostBalanceSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance_settings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&payments=%7B%22debit_negative_balances%22%3Atrue%2C%22payouts%22%3A%7B%22automatic_transfer_rules_by_currency%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%5B%7B%22payout_method%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22transfer_up_to_amount%22%3A0%2C%22type%22%3A%22transfer_all%22%7D%5D%2C%22property2%22%3A%5B%7B%22payout_method%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22transfer_up_to_amount%22%3A0%2C%22type%22%3A%22transfer_all%22%7D%5D%7D%2C%22minimum_balance_by_currency%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A0%2C%22property2%22%3A0%7D%2C%22schedule%22%3A%7B%22interval%22%3A%22daily%22%2C%22monthly_payout_days%22%3A%5B0%5D%2C%22weekly_payout_days%22%3A%5B%22friday%22%5D%7D%2C%22statement_descriptor%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22settlement_timing%22%3A%7B%22delay_days_override%22%3A0%2C%22start_of_day%22%3A%7B%22hour%22%3A0%2C%22minutes%22%3A0%2C%22timezone%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D%7D'
```

`POST /v1/balance_settings`

<p>Updates balance settings for a given connected account.
 Related guide: <a href="/connect/authentication">Making API calls for connected accounts</a></p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
payments:
  debit_negative_balances: true
  payouts:
    automatic_transfer_rules_by_currency:
      property1:
        -
          payout_method: string
          transfer_up_to_amount: 0
          type: transfer_all
      property2:
        -
          payout_method: string
          transfer_up_to_amount: 0
          type: transfer_all
    minimum_balance_by_currency:
      property1: 0
      property2: 0
    schedule:
      interval: daily
      monthly_payout_days:
        - 0
      weekly_payout_days:
        - friday
    statement_descriptor: string
  settlement_timing:
    delay_days_override: 0
    start_of_day:
      hour: 0
      minutes: 0
      timezone: string
```

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/billing/credit_grants \
```

```bash
  -d 'amount=%7B%22monetary%22%3A%7B%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D%2C%22type%22%3A%22monetary%22%7D&applicability_config=%7B%22scope%22%3A%7B%22price_type%22%3A%22metered%22%2C%22prices%22%3A%5B%7B%22id%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%7D%7D&category=paid&customer=string&customer_account=string&effective_at=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&expires_at=0&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string&priority=0'
```

`POST /v1/billing/credit_grants`

<p>Creates a credit grant.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount:
  monetary:
    currency: string
    value: 0
  type: monetary
applicability_config:
  scope:
    price_type: metered
    prices:
      -
        id: string
category: paid
customer: string
customer_account: string
effective_at: 0
expand:
  - string
expires_at: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
priority: 0
```

<h3 id="create-a-credit-grant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|object|true|Amount of this credit grant.|
|» » monetary|body|object|false|none|
|» » » currency|body|string(currency)|true|none|
|» » » value|body|integer|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» applicability_config|body|object|true|Configuration specifying what this credit grant applies to. We currently only support `metered` prices that have a [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) attached to them.|
|» » scope|body|object|true|none|
|» » » price_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » » prices|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » » id|body|string|true|none|
|» category|body|string|false|The category of this credit grant. It defaults to `paid` if not specified.|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the customer receiving the billing credits.|
|» customer_account|body|string|false|ID of the account representing the customer receiving the billing credits.|
|» effective_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The time when the billing credits become effective-when they're eligible for use. It defaults to the current timestamp if not specified.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» expires_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The time when the billing credits expire. If not specified, the billing credits don't expire.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of key-value pairs that you can attach to an object. You can use this to store additional information about the object (for example, cost basis) in a structured format.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A descriptive name shown in the Dashboard.|
|» priority|body|integer|false|The desired priority for applying this credit grant. If not specified, it will be set to the default value of 50. The highest priority is 0 and the lowest is 100.|

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/billing/meter_events \
  -X POST \

  -d 'event_name=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&identifier=string&payload=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&timestamp=0'
```

`POST /v1/billing/meter_events`

<p>Creates a billing meter event.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
event_name: string
expand:
  - string
identifier: string
payload:
  property1: string
  property2: string
timestamp: 0
```

<h3 id="create-a-billing-meter-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» event_name|body|string|true|The name of the meter event. Corresponds with the `event_name` field on a meter.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» identifier|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the event. If not provided, one is generated. We recommend using UUID-like identifiers. Stripe enforces uniqueness within a rolling period of at least 24 hours. The enforcement of uniqueness primarily addresses issues arising from accidental retries or other problems occurring within extremely brief time intervals. This approach helps prevent duplicate entries and ensures data integrity in high-frequency operations.|
|» payload|body|object|true|The payload of the event. This must contain the fields corresponding to a meter's `customer_mapping.event_payload_key` (default is `stripe_customer_id`) and `value_settings.event_payload_key` (default is `value`). Read more about the [payload](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/meters/configure#meter-configuration-attributes).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» timestamp|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The time of the event. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch. Must be within the past 35 calendar days or up to 5 minutes in the future. Defaults to current timestamp if not specified.|

## List billing meter event summaries

<a id="opIdGetBillingMetersIdEventSummaries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/billing/meters/string/event_summaries?customer=string&end_time=0&start_time=0' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/billing/meters/{id}/event_summaries`

<p>Retrieve a list of billing meter event summaries.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-billing-meter-event-summaries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|query|string|true|The customer for which to fetch event summaries.|
|end_time|query|integer(unix-time)|true|The timestamp from when to stop aggregating meter events (exclusive). Must be aligned with minute boundaries.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the object.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|start_time|query|integer(unix-time)|true|The timestamp from when to start aggregating meter events (inclusive). Must be aligned with minute boundaries.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|value_grouping_window|query|string|false|Specifies what granularity to use when generating event summaries. If not specified, a single event summary would be returned for the specified time range. For hourly granularity, start and end times must align with hour boundaries (e.g., 00:00, 01:00, ..., 23:00). For daily granularity, start and end times must align with UTC day boundaries (00:00 UTC).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create a portal configuration

<a id="opIdPostBillingPortalConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/billing_portal/configurations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'business_profile=%7B%22headline%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22privacy_policy_url%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22terms_of_service_url%22%3A%22string%22%7D&default_return_url=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&features=%7B%22customer_update%22%3A%7B%22allowed_updates%22%3A%5B%22address%22%5D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22invoice_history%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22payment_method_update%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22payment_method_configuration%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22subscription_cancel%22%3A%7B%22cancellation_reason%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22feedback_options%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22options%22%3A%5B%22customer_service%22%5D%7D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22mode%22%3A%22at_period_end%22%2C%22proration_behavior%22%3A%22always_invoice%22%7D%2C%22subscription_update%22%3A%7B%22billing_cycle_anchor%22%3A%22now%22%2C%22default_allowed_updates%22%3A%5B%22price%22%5D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22products%22%3A%5B%7B%22adjustable_quantity%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22maximum%22%3A0%2C%22minimum%22%3A0%7D%2C%22prices%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22proration_behavior%22%3A%22always_invoice%22%2C%22schedule_at_period_end%22%3A%7B%22conditions%22%3A%5B%7B%22type%22%3A%22decreasing_item_amount%22%7D%5D%7D%2C%22trial_update_behavior%22%3A%22continue_trial%22%7D%7D&login_page=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string'
```

`POST /v1/billing_portal/configurations`

<p>Creates a configuration that describes the functionality and behavior of a PortalSession</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
business_profile:
  headline: string
  privacy_policy_url: string
  terms_of_service_url: string
default_return_url: string
expand:
  - string
features:
  customer_update:
    allowed_updates:
      - address
    enabled: true
  invoice_history:
    enabled: true
  payment_method_update:
    enabled: true
    payment_method_configuration: string
  subscription_cancel:
    cancellation_reason:
      enabled: true
      feedback_options:
        - string
      options:
        - customer_service
    enabled: true
    mode: at_period_end
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
  subscription_update:
    billing_cycle_anchor: now
    default_allowed_updates:
      - price
    enabled: true
    products:
      -
        adjustable_quantity:
          enabled: true
          maximum: 0
          minimum: 0
        prices:
          - string
        product: string
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
    schedule_at_period_end:
      conditions:
        -
          type: decreasing_item_amount
    trial_update_behavior: continue_trial
login_page:
  enabled: true
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-portal-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» business_profile|body|object|false|The business information shown to customers in the portal.|
|» » headline|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » privacy_policy_url|body|string|false|none|
|» » terms_of_service_url|body|string|false|none|
|» default_return_url|body|string|false|The default URL to redirect customers to when they click on the portal's link to return to your website. This can be [overridden](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customer_portal/sessions/create#create_portal_session-return_url) when creating the session.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## Update a portal configuration

<a id="opIdPostBillingPortalConfigurationsConfiguration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/billing_portal/configurations/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'active=true&business_profile=%7B%22headline%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22privacy_policy_url%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22terms_of_service_url%22%3A%22string%22%7D&default_return_url=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&features=%7B%22customer_update%22%3A%7B%22allowed_updates%22%3A%5B%22address%22%5D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22invoice_history%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22payment_method_update%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22payment_method_configuration%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22subscription_cancel%22%3A%7B%22cancellation_reason%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22feedback_options%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22options%22%3A%5B%22customer_service%22%5D%7D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22mode%22%3A%22at_period_end%22%2C%22proration_behavior%22%3A%22always_invoice%22%7D%2C%22subscription_update%22%3A%7B%22billing_cycle_anchor%22%3A%22now%22%2C%22default_allowed_updates%22%3A%5B%22price%22%5D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22products%22%3A%5B%7B%22adjustable_quantity%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22maximum%22%3A0%2C%22minimum%22%3A0%7D%2C%22prices%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22proration_behavior%22%3A%22always_invoice%22%2C%22schedule_at_period_end%22%3A%7B%22conditions%22%3A%5B%7B%22type%22%3A%22decreasing_item_amount%22%7D%5D%7D%2C%22trial_update_behavior%22%3A%22continue_trial%22%7D%7D&login_page=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string'
```

`POST /v1/billing_portal/configurations/{configuration}`

<p>Updates a configuration that describes the functionality of the customer portal.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
business_profile:
  headline: string
  privacy_policy_url: string
  terms_of_service_url: string
default_return_url: string
expand:
  - string
features:
  customer_update:
    allowed_updates:
      - address
    enabled: true
  invoice_history:
    enabled: true
  payment_method_update:
    enabled: true
    payment_method_configuration: string
  subscription_cancel:
    cancellation_reason:
      enabled: true
      feedback_options:
        - string
      options:
        - customer_service
    enabled: true
    mode: at_period_end
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
  subscription_update:
    billing_cycle_anchor: now
    default_allowed_updates:
      - price
    enabled: true
    products:
      -
        adjustable_quantity:
          enabled: true
          maximum: 0
          minimum: 0
        prices:
          - string
        product: string
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
    schedule_at_period_end:
      conditions:
        -
          type: decreasing_item_amount
    trial_update_behavior: continue_trial
login_page:
  enabled: true
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
```

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/billing_portal/sessions \

```

`POST /v1/billing_portal/sessions`

<p>Creates a session of the customer portal.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
configuration: string
customer: string
customer_account: string
expand:
  - string
flow_data:
  after_completion:
    hosted_confirmation:
      custom_message: string
    redirect:
      return_url: string
    type: hosted_confirmation
  subscription_cancel:
    retention:
      coupon_offer:
        coupon: string
      type: coupon_offer
    subscription: string
  subscription_update:
    subscription: string
  subscription_update_confirm:
    discounts:
      -
        coupon: string
        promotion_code: string
    items:
      -
        id: string
        price: string
        quantity: 0
    subscription: string
  type: customer_update
locale: auto
on_behalf_of: string
return_url: string
```

## List all charges

<a id="opIdGetCharges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/charges`

<p>Returns a list of charges you’ve previously created. The charges are returned in sorted order, with the most recent charges appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-charges-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return charges that were created during the given date interval.|
|customer|query|string|false|Only return charges for the customer specified by this customer ID.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|payment_intent|query|string|false|Only return charges that were created by the PaymentIntent specified by this PaymentIntent ID.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|transfer_group|query|string|false|Only return charges for this transfer group, limited to 100.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="create-a-charge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount intended to be collected by this payment. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|» application_fee|body|integer|false|none|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|A fee in cents (or local equivalent) that will be applied to the charge and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The request must be made with an OAuth key or the `Stripe-Account` header in order to take an application fee. For more information, see the application fees [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/direct-charges#collect-fees).|
|» capture|body|boolean|false|Whether to immediately capture the charge. Defaults to `true`. When `false`, the charge issues an authorization (or pre-authorization), and will need to be [captured](https://docs.stripe.com/api#capture_charge) later. Uncaptured charges expire after a set number of days (7 by default). For more information, see the [authorizing charges and settling later](https://docs.stripe.com/charges/placing-a-hold) documentation.|
|» card|body|object \| string|false|A token, like the ones returned by [Stripe.js](https://stripe.com/docs/js).|

For details, see [Creating Separate Charges and Transfers](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#settlement-merchant).|

The receipt will not be sent until the charge is paid, and no receipts will be sent for test mode charges. If this charge is for a [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object), the email address specified here will override the customer's email address. If `receipt_email` is specified for a charge in live mode, a receipt will be sent regardless of your [email settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/emails).|
|» shipping|body|object|false|Shipping information for the charge. Helps prevent fraud on charges for physical goods.|

|» » » city|body|string|false|none|
|» » » country|body|string|false|none|

|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » phone|body|string|false|none|
|» » tracking_number|body|string|false|none|
|» source|body|string|false|A payment source to be charged. This can be the ID of a [card](https://docs.stripe.com/api#cards) (i.e., credit or debit card), a [bank account](https://docs.stripe.com/api#bank_accounts), a [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api#sources), a [token](https://docs.stripe.com/api#tokens), or a [connected account](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/account-debits#charging-a-connected-account). For certain sources---namely, [cards](https://docs.stripe.com/api#cards), [bank accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api#bank_accounts), and attached [sources](https://docs.stripe.com/api#sources)---you must also pass the ID of the associated customer.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|For a non-card charge, text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see [the Statement Descriptor docs](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors).<br><br>For a card charge, this value is ignored unless you don't specify a `statement_descriptor_suffix`, in which case this value is used as the suffix.|
|» statement_descriptor_suffix|body|string|false|Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's [statement descriptor prefix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#static) to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement. If the account has no prefix value, the suffix is concatenated to the account's statement descriptor.|
|» transfer_data|body|object|false|An optional dictionary including the account to automatically transfer to as part of a destination charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/destination-charges) for details.|

## Search charges

<a id="opIdGetChargesSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/charges/search`

<p>Search for charges you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="search-charges-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://docs.stripe.com/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for charges](https://docs.stripe.com/search#query-fields-for-charges).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Update a charge

<a id="opIdPostChargesCharge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'customer=string&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&fraud_details=%7B%22user_report%22%3A%22%22%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&receipt_email=string&shipping=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22carrier%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tracking_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&transfer_group=string'
```

`POST /v1/charges/{charge}`

<p>Updates the specified charge by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
customer: string
description: string
expand:
  - string
fraud_details:
  user_report: ""
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
receipt_email: string
shipping:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  carrier: string
  name: string
  phone: string
  tracking_number: string
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="update-a-charge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» customer|body|string|false|The ID of an existing customer that will be associated with this request. This field may only be updated if there is no existing associated customer with this charge.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string which you can attach to a charge object. It is displayed when in the web interface alongside the charge. Note that if you use Stripe to send automatic email receipts to your customers, your receipt emails will include the `description` of the charge(s) that they are describing.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» fraud_details|body|object|false|A set of key-value pairs you can attach to a charge giving information about its riskiness. If you believe a charge is fraudulent, include a `user_report` key with a value of `fraudulent`. If you believe a charge is safe, include a `user_report` key with a value of `safe`. Stripe will use the information you send to improve our fraud detection algorithms.|
|» » user_report|body|string|true|none|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» receipt_email|body|string|false|This is the email address that the receipt for this charge will be sent to. If this field is updated, then a new email receipt will be sent to the updated address.|
|» shipping|body|object|false|Shipping information for the charge. Helps prevent fraud on charges for physical goods.|
|» » address|body|object|true|none|
|» » » city|body|string|false|none|
|» » » country|body|string|false|none|
|» » » line1|body|string|false|none|
|» » » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » » postal_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » » state|body|string|false|none|
|» » carrier|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » phone|body|string|false|none|
|» » tracking_number|body|string|false|none|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. `transfer_group` may only be provided if it has not been set. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » user_report|""|
|» » user_report|fraudulent|
|» » user_report|safe|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

## Capture a charge

<a id="opIdPostChargesChargeCapture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/string/capture \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&application_fee=0&application_fee_amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&receipt_email=string&statement_descriptor=string&statement_descriptor_suffix=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%7D&transfer_group=string'
```

`POST /v1/charges/{charge}/capture`

<p>This method is deprecated and will be removed soon. If your integration uses it, you need to update it to use a different payment flow, such as <a href="/docs/payments/payment-intents">the Payment Intents API</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
application_fee: 0
application_fee_amount: 0
expand:
  - string
receipt_email: string
statement_descriptor: string
statement_descriptor_suffix: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="capture-a-charge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|The amount to capture, which must be less than or equal to the original amount.|
|» application_fee|body|integer|false|An application fee to add on to this charge.|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|An application fee amount to add on to this charge, which must be less than or equal to the original amount.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» receipt_email|body|string|false|The email address to send this charge's receipt to. This will override the previously-specified email address for this charge, if one was set. Receipts will not be sent in test mode.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|For a non-card charge, text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see [the Statement Descriptor docs](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors).<br><br>For a card charge, this value is ignored unless you don't specify a `statement_descriptor_suffix`, in which case this value is used as the suffix.|
|» statement_descriptor_suffix|body|string|false|Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's [statement descriptor prefix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#static) to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement. If the account has no prefix value, the suffix is concatenated to the account's statement descriptor.|
|» transfer_data|body|object|false|An optional dictionary including the account to automatically transfer to as part of a destination charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/destination-charges) for details.|
|» » amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. `transfer_group` may only be provided if it has not been set. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

## Create a refund

<a id="opIdPostChargesChargeRefund"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/string/refund \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&instructions_email=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_intent=string&reason=duplicate&refund_application_fee=true&reverse_transfer=true'
```

`POST /v1/charges/{charge}/refund`

<p>When you create a new refund, you must specify either a Charge or a PaymentIntent object.</p>

<p>This action refunds a previously created charge that’s not refunded yet.
Funds are refunded to the credit or debit card that’s originally charged.</p>

<p>You can optionally refund only part of a charge.
You can repeat this until the entire charge is refunded.</p>

<p>After you entirely refund a charge, you can’t refund it again.
This method raises an error when it’s called on an already-refunded charge,
or when you attempt to refund more money than is left on a charge.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
expand:
  - string
instructions_email: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_intent: string
reason: duplicate
refund_application_fee: true
reverse_transfer: true
```

<h3 id="create-a-refund-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|path|string|true|The identifier of the charge to refund.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) representing how much of this charge to refund. Can refund only up to the remaining, unrefunded amount of the charge.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» instructions_email|body|string|false|For payment methods without native refund support (e.g., Konbini, PromptPay), use this email from the customer to receive refund instructions.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» payment_intent|body|string|false|The identifier of the PaymentIntent to refund.|
|» reason|body|string|false|String indicating the reason for the refund. If set, possible values are `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, and `requested_by_customer`. If you believe the charge to be fraudulent, specifying `fraudulent` as the reason will add the associated card and email to your [block lists](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/lists), and will also help us improve our fraud detection algorithms.|
|» refund_application_fee|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when refunding this charge. If a full charge refund is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded in an amount proportional to the amount of the charge refunded. An application fee can be refunded only by the application that created the charge.|
|» reverse_transfer|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the transfer should be reversed when refunding this charge. The transfer will be reversed proportionally to the amount being refunded (either the entire or partial amount).<br><br>A transfer can be reversed only by the application that created the charge.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|
|» reason|duplicate|
|» reason|fraudulent|
|» reason|requested_by_customer|

## List all refunds

<a id="opIdGetChargesChargeRefunds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/string/refunds \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/charges/{charge}/refunds`

<p>You can see a list of the refunds belonging to a specific charge. Note that the 10 most recent refunds are always available by default on the charge object. If you need more than those 10, you can use this API method and the <code>limit</code> and <code>starting_after</code> parameters to page through additional refunds.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-refunds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|path|string|true|none|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create a refund

<a id="opIdPostChargesChargeRefunds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/string/refunds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&customer=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&instructions_email=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&origin=customer_balance&payment_intent=string&reason=duplicate&refund_application_fee=true&reverse_transfer=true'
```

`POST /v1/charges/{charge}/refunds`

<p>When you create a new refund, you must specify a Charge or a PaymentIntent object on which to create it.</p>

<p>Creating a new refund will refund a charge that has previously been created but not yet refunded.
Funds will be refunded to the credit or debit card that was originally charged.</p>

<p>You can optionally refund only part of a charge.
You can do so multiple times, until the entire charge has been refunded.</p>

<p>Once entirely refunded, a charge can’t be refunded again.
This method will raise an error when called on an already-refunded charge,
or when trying to refund more money than is left on a charge.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
customer: string
expand:
  - string
instructions_email: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
origin: customer_balance
payment_intent: string
reason: duplicate
refund_application_fee: true
reverse_transfer: true
```

<h3 id="create-a-refund-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|path|string|true|The identifier of the charge to refund.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|false|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» customer|body|string|false|Customer whose customer balance to refund from.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» instructions_email|body|string|false|For payment methods without native refund support (e.g., Konbini, PromptPay), use this email from the customer to receive refund instructions.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» origin|body|string|false|Origin of the refund|
|» payment_intent|body|string|false|The identifier of the PaymentIntent to refund.|
|» reason|body|string|false|String indicating the reason for the refund. If set, possible values are `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, and `requested_by_customer`. If you believe the charge to be fraudulent, specifying `fraudulent` as the reason will add the associated card and email to your [block lists](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/lists), and will also help us improve our fraud detection algorithms.|
|» refund_application_fee|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when refunding this charge. If a full charge refund is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded in an amount proportional to the amount of the charge refunded. An application fee can be refunded only by the application that created the charge.|
|» reverse_transfer|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the transfer should be reversed when refunding this charge. The transfer will be reversed proportionally to the amount being refunded (either the entire or partial amount).<br><br>A transfer can be reversed only by the application that created the charge.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|
|» origin|customer_balance|
|» reason|duplicate|
|» reason|fraudulent|
|» reason|requested_by_customer|

## List all Checkout Sessions

<a id="opIdGetCheckoutSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/checkout/sessions`

<p>Returns a list of Checkout Sessions.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-checkout-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return Checkout Sessions that were created during the given date interval.|
|customer|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions for the Customer specified.|
|customer_account|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions for the Account specified.|
|customer_details|query|object|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions for the Customer details specified.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|payment_intent|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Session for the PaymentIntent specified.|
|payment_link|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions for the Payment Link specified.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions matching the given status.|
|subscription|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Session for the subscription specified.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|complete|
|status|expired|
|status|open|
