<h3 id="list-all-checkout-sessions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-all-checkout-sessions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[checkout.session](#schemacheckout.session)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

In `payment` mode, the customer’s most recently saved card<br>payment method will be used to prefill the email, name, card details, and billing address<br>on the Checkout page. In `subscription` mode, the customer’s [default payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/update#update_customer-invoice_settings-default_payment_method)<br>will be used if it’s a card, otherwise the most recently saved card will be used. A valid billing address, billing name and billing email are required on the payment method for Checkout to prefill the customer's card details.<br><br>If the Customer already has a valid [email](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-email) set, the email will be prefilled and not editable in Checkout.<br>If the Customer does not have a valid `email`, Checkout will set the email entered during the session on the Customer.<br><br>If blank for Checkout Sessions in `subscription` mode or with `customer_creation` set as `always` in `payment` mode, Checkout will create a new Customer object based on information provided during the payment flow.<br><br>You can set [`payment_intent_data.setup_future_usage`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create#create_checkout_session-payment_intent_data-setup_future_usage) to have Checkout automatically attach the payment method to the Customer you pass in for future reuse.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve a Checkout Session

<a id="opIdGetCheckoutSessionsSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/checkout/sessions/{session}`

<p>Retrieves a Checkout Session object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|body|body|object|false|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Update a Checkout Session

<a id="opIdPostCheckoutSessionsSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'collected_information=%7B%22shipping_details%22%3A%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&line_items=%5B%7B%22adjustable_quantity%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22maximum%22%3A0%2C%22minimum%22%3A0%7D%2C%22id%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22price%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22price_data%22%3A%7B%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product_data%22%3A%7B%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22images%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_details%22%3A%7B%22performance_location%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22unit_label%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22recurring%22%3A%7B%22interval%22%3A%22day%22%2C%22interval_count%22%3A0%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22tax_rates%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&shipping_options=%5B%7B%22shipping_rate%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22shipping_rate_data%22%3A%7B%22delivery_estimate%22%3A%7B%22maximum%22%3A%7B%22unit%22%3A%22business_day%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D%2C%22minimum%22%3A%7B%22unit%22%3A%22business_day%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D%7D%2C%22display_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22fixed_amount%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency_options%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%7D%2C%22property2%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%7D%7D%7D%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22tax_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22fixed_amount%22%7D%7D%5D'
```

`POST /v1/checkout/sessions/{session}`

<p>Updates a Checkout Session object.</p>

<p>Related guide: <a href="/payments/advanced/dynamic-updates">Dynamically update a Checkout Session</a></p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
collected_information:
  shipping_details:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    name: string
expand:
  - string
line_items:
  -
    adjustable_quantity:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
    id: string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      product_data:
        description: string
        images:
          - string
        metadata:
          property1: string
          property2: string
        name: string
        tax_code: string
        tax_details:
          performance_location: string
          tax_code: string
        unit_label: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
shipping_options:
  -
    shipping_rate: string
    shipping_rate_data:
      delivery_estimate:
        maximum:
          unit: business_day
          value: 0
        minimum:
          unit: business_day
          value: 0
      display_name: string
      fixed_amount:
        amount: 0
        currency: string
        currency_options:
          property1:
            amount: 0
            tax_behavior: exclusive
          property2:
            amount: 0
            tax_behavior: exclusive
      metadata:
        property1: string
        property2: string
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      tax_code: string
      type: fixed_amount
```

<h3 id="update-a-checkout-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[checkout.session](#schemacheckout.session)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Expire a Checkout Session

<a id="opIdPostCheckoutSessionsSessionExpire"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions/string/expire \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/checkout/sessions/{session}/expire`

<p>A Checkout Session can be expired when it is in one of these statuses: <code>open</code> </p>

<p>After it expires, a customer can’t complete a Checkout Session and customers loading the Checkout Session see a message saying the Checkout Session is expired.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="expire-a-checkout-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## Retrieve a Checkout Session's line items

<a id="opIdGetCheckoutSessionsSessionLineItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/checkout/sessions/string/line_items \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/checkout/sessions/{session}/line_items`

<p>When retrieving a Checkout Session, there is an includable <strong>line_items</strong> property containing the first handful of those items. There is also a URL where you can retrieve the full (paginated) list of line items.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-checkout-sessions-line-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|session|path|string|true|none|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## List orders

<a id="opIdGetClimateOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/climate/orders \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/climate/orders`

<p>Lists all Climate order objects. The orders are returned sorted by creation date, with the
most recently created orders appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-orders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create an order

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/climate/orders \

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
```

`POST /v1/climate/orders`

<p>Creates a Climate order object for a given Climate product. The order will be processed immediately
after creation and payment will be deducted your Stripe balance.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
beneficiary:
  public_name: string
currency: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
metric_tons: string
product: string
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Requested amount of carbon removal units. Either this or `metric_tons` must be specified.|
|» beneficiary|body|object|false|Publicly sharable reference for the end beneficiary of carbon removal. Assumed to be the Stripe account if not set.|
|» » public_name|body|string|true|none|
|» currency|body|string|false|Request currency for the order as a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a supported [settlement currency for your account](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). If omitted, the account's default currency will be used.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» metric_tons|body|string(decimal)|false|Requested number of tons for the order. Either this or `amount` must be specified.|
|» product|body|string|true|Unique identifier of the Climate product.|

`POST /v1/climate/orders/{order}/cancel`

<p>Cancels a Climate order. You can cancel an order within 24 hours of creation. Stripe refunds the
reservation <code>amount_subtotal</code>, but not the <code>amount_fees</code> for user-triggered cancellations. Frontier
might cancel reservations if suppliers fail to deliver. If Frontier cancels the reservation, Stripe
provides 90 days advance notice and refunds the <code>amount_total</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

## Create a coupon

<a id="opIdPostCoupons"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/coupons \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount_off=0&applies_to=%7B%22products%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D&currency=string&currency_options=%7B%22property1%22%3A%7B%22amount_off%22%3A0%7D%2C%22property2%22%3A%7B%22amount_off%22%3A0%7D%7D&duration=forever&duration_in_months=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&id=string&max_redemptions=0&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string&percent_off=0&redeem_by=0'
```

`POST /v1/coupons`

<p>You can create coupons easily via the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/coupons">coupon management</a> page of the Stripe dashboard. Coupon creation is also accessible via the API if you need to create coupons on the fly.</p>

<p>A coupon has either a <code>percent_off</code> or an <code>amount_off</code> and <code>currency</code>. If you set an <code>amount_off</code>, that amount will be subtracted from any invoice’s subtotal. For example, an invoice with a subtotal of <currency>100</currency> will have a final total of <currency>0</currency> if a coupon with an <code>amount_off</code> of <amount>200</amount> is applied to it and an invoice with a subtotal of <currency>300</currency> will have a final total of <currency>100</currency> if a coupon with an <code>amount_off</code> of <amount>200</amount> is applied to it.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount_off: 0
applies_to:
  products:
    - string
currency: string
currency_options:
  property1:
    amount_off: 0
  property2:
    amount_off: 0
duration: forever
duration_in_months: 0
expand:
  - string
id: string
max_redemptions: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
percent_off: 0
redeem_by: 0
```

<h3 id="create-a-coupon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount_off|body|integer|false|A positive integer representing the amount to subtract from an invoice total (required if `percent_off` is not passed).|
|» applies_to|body|object|false|A hash containing directions for what this Coupon will apply discounts to.|
|» » products|body|[string]|false|none|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|false|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) of the `amount_off` parameter (required if `amount_off` is passed).|
|» currency_options|body|object|false|Coupons defined in each available currency option (only supported if `amount_off` is passed). Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » amount_off|body|integer|true|none|
|» duration|body|string|false|Specifies how long the discount will be in effect if used on a subscription. Defaults to `once`.|
|» duration_in_months|body|integer|false|Required only if `duration` is `repeating`, in which case it must be a positive integer that specifies the number of months the discount will be in effect.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» id|body|string|false|Unique string of your choice that will be used to identify this coupon when applying it to a customer. If you don't want to specify a particular code, you can leave the ID blank and we'll generate a random code for you.|
|» max_redemptions|body|integer|false|A positive integer specifying the number of times the coupon can be redeemed before it's no longer valid. For example, you might have a 50% off coupon that the first 20 readers of your blog can use.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the coupon displayed to customers on, for instance invoices, or receipts. By default the `id` is shown if `name` is not set.|
|» percent_off|body|number|false|A positive float larger than 0, and smaller or equal to 100, that represents the discount the coupon will apply (required if `amount_off` is not passed).|
|» redeem_by|body|integer(unix-time)|false|Unix timestamp specifying the last time at which the coupon can be redeemed (cannot be set to more than 5 years in the future). After the redeem_by date, the coupon can no longer be applied to new customers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» duration|forever|
|» duration|once|
|» duration|repeating|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

```json
    ]
  },
```

## Create a credit note

<a id="opIdPostCreditNotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/credit_notes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&credit_amount=0&effective_at=0&email_type=credit_note&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice=string&lines=%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22invoice_line_item%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22tax_amounts%22%3A%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22tax_rate%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22taxable_amount%22%3A0%7D%5D%2C%22tax_rates%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22type%22%3A%22custom_line_item%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D&memo=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&out_of_band_amount=0&reason=duplicate&refund_amount=0&refunds=%5B%7B%22amount_refunded%22%3A0%2C%22payment_record_refund%22%3A%7B%22payment_record%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22refund_group%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22refund%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22payment_record_refund%22%7D%5D&shipping_cost=%7B%22shipping_rate%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/credit_notes`

<p>Issue a credit note to adjust the amount of a finalized invoice. A credit note will first reduce the invoice’s <code>amount_remaining</code> (and <code>amount_due</code>), but not below zero.
This amount is indicated by the credit note’s <code>pre_payment_amount</code>. The excess amount is indicated by <code>post_payment_amount</code>, and it can result in any combination of the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>Refunds: create a new refund (using <code>refund_amount</code>) or link existing refunds (using <code>refunds</code>).</li>
<li>Customer balance credit: credit the customer’s balance (using <code>credit_amount</code>) which will be automatically applied to their next invoice when it’s finalized.</li>
<li>Outside of Stripe credit: record the amount that is or will be credited outside of Stripe (using <code>out_of_band_amount</code>).</li>
</ul>

<p>The sum of refunds, customer balance credits, and outside of Stripe credits must equal the <code>post_payment_amount</code>.</p>

<p>You may issue multiple credit notes for an invoice. Each credit note may increment the invoice’s <code>pre_payment_credit_notes_amount</code>,
<code>post_payment_credit_notes_amount</code>, or both, depending on the invoice’s <code>amount_remaining</code> at the time of credit note creation.</p>

<p>For invoices that also have refunds created through the <a href="/docs/api/refunds">Refund API</a>, the credit note API subtracts those refund amounts from the maximum creditable amount. This prevents the combined credit notes and refunds from exceeding the invoice amount. If you use both, ensure the combined total does not exceed the invoice’s paid amount.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
credit_amount: 0
effective_at: 0
email_type: credit_note
expand:
  - string
invoice: string
lines:
  -
    amount: 0
    description: string
    invoice_line_item: string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_amounts:
      -
        amount: 0
        tax_rate: string
        taxable_amount: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
    type: custom_line_item
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
memo: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
out_of_band_amount: 0
reason: duplicate
refund_amount: 0
refunds:
  -
    amount_refunded: 0
    payment_record_refund:
      payment_record: string
      refund_group: string
    refund: string
    type: payment_record_refund
shipping_cost:
  shipping_rate: string
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided.|
|» credit_amount|body|integer|false|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount to credit the customer's balance, which will be automatically applied to their next invoice.|
|» effective_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The date when this credit note is in effect. Same as `created` unless overwritten. When defined, this value replaces the system-generated 'Date of issue' printed on the credit note PDF.|

|» invoice|body|string|true|ID of the invoice.|
|» lines|body|[object]|false|Line items that make up the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided.|

## Retrieve a credit note preview's line items

<a id="opIdGetCreditNotesPreviewLines"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/credit_notes/preview/lines?invoice=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/credit_notes/preview/lines`

<p>When retrieving a credit note preview, you’ll get a <strong>lines</strong> property containing the first handful of those items. This URL you can retrieve the full (paginated) list of line items.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-credit-note-previews-line-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|query|integer|false|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided.|
|credit_amount|query|integer|false|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount to credit the customer's balance, which will be automatically applied to their next invoice.|
|effective_at|query|integer(unix-time)|false|The date when this credit note is in effect. Same as `created` unless overwritten. When defined, this value replaces the system-generated 'Date of issue' printed on the credit note PDF.|
|email_type|query|string|false|Type of email to send to the customer, one of `credit_note` or `none` and the default is `credit_note`.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|invoice|query|string|true|ID of the invoice.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|lines|query|[object]|false|Line items that make up the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided.|
|memo|query|string|false|The credit note's memo appears on the credit note PDF.|
|metadata|query|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|out_of_band_amount|query|integer|false|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount that is credited outside of Stripe.|
|reason|query|string|false|Reason for issuing this credit note, one of `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `order_change`, or `product_unsatisfactory`|
|refund_amount|query|integer|false|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount to refund. If set, a refund will be created for the charge associated with the invoice.|
|refunds|query|[object]|false|Refunds to link to this credit note.|
|shipping_cost|query|object|false|When shipping_cost contains the shipping_rate from the invoice, the shipping_cost is included in the credit note. One of `amount`, `lines`, or `shipping_cost` must be provided.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|---|---|

|email_type|none|
|reason|duplicate|
|reason|fraudulent|
|reason|order_change|
|reason|product_unsatisfactory|

## Create a Customer Session

<a id="opIdPostCustomerSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customer_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'components=%7B%22active_entitlements%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22buy_button%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22customer_portal%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22customer_sheet%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22features%22%3A%7B%22payment_method_allow_redisplay_filters%22%3A%5B%22always%22%5D%2C%22payment_method_remove%22%3A%22disabled%22%7D%7D%2C%22mobile_payment_element%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22features%22%3A%7B%22payment_method_allow_redisplay_filters%22%3A%5B%22always%22%5D%2C%22payment_method_redisplay%22%3A%22disabled%22%2C%22payment_method_remove%22%3A%22disabled%22%2C%22payment_method_save%22%3A%22disabled%22%2C%22payment_method_save_allow_redisplay_override%22%3A%22always%22%7D%7D%2C%22payment_element%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22features%22%3A%7B%22payment_method_allow_redisplay_filters%22%3A%5B%22always%22%5D%2C%22payment_method_redisplay%22%3A%22disabled%22%2C%22payment_method_redisplay_limit%22%3A0%2C%22payment_method_remove%22%3A%22disabled%22%2C%22payment_method_save%22%3A%22disabled%22%2C%22payment_method_save_usage%22%3A%22off_session%22%7D%7D%2C%22pricing_table%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%7D&customer=string&customer_account=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/customer_sessions`

<p>Creates a Customer Session object that includes a single-use client secret that you can use on your front-end to grant client-side API access for certain customer resources.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
components:
  active_entitlements:
    enabled: true
  buy_button:
    enabled: true
  customer_portal:
    enabled: true
  customer_sheet:
    enabled: true
    features:
      payment_method_allow_redisplay_filters:
        - always
      payment_method_remove: disabled
  mobile_payment_element:
    enabled: true
    features:
      payment_method_allow_redisplay_filters:
        - always
      payment_method_redisplay: disabled
      payment_method_remove: disabled
      payment_method_save: disabled
      payment_method_save_allow_redisplay_override: always
  payment_element:
    enabled: true
    features:
      payment_method_allow_redisplay_filters:
        - always
      payment_method_redisplay: disabled
      payment_method_redisplay_limit: 0
      payment_method_remove: disabled
      payment_method_save: disabled
      payment_method_save_usage: off_session
  pricing_table:
    enabled: true
customer: string
customer_account: string
expand:
  - string
```

## List all customers

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /v1/customers`

<p>Returns a list of your customers. The customers are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recent customers appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-customers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return customers that were created during the given date interval.|
|email|query|string|false|A case-sensitive filter on the list based on the customer's `email` field. The value must be a string.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|test_clock|query|string|false|Provides a list of customers that are associated with the specified test clock. The response will not include customers with test clocks if this parameter is not set.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/customers`

<p>Creates a new customer object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
address:
  city: string
  country: string
  line1: string
  line2: string
  postal_code: string
  state: string
balance: 0
business_name: string
cash_balance:
  settings:
    reconciliation_mode: automatic
description: string
email: string
expand:
  - string
individual_name: string
invoice_prefix: string
invoice_settings:
  custom_fields:
    -
      name: string
      value: string
  default_payment_method: string
  footer: string
  rendering_options:
    amount_tax_display: ""
    template: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
next_invoice_sequence: 0
payment_method: string
phone: string
preferred_locales:
  - string
shipping:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  name: string
  phone: string
source: string
tax:
  ip_address: string
  validate_location: deferred
tax_exempt: ""
tax_id_data:
  -
    type: ad_nrt
    value: string
test_clock: string
```

## Search customers

<a id="opIdGetCustomersSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/customers/search`

<p>Search for customers you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="search-customers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://docs.stripe.com/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for customers](https://docs.stripe.com/search#query-fields-for-customers).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Update a customer

<a id="opIdPostCustomersCustomer"></a>


`POST /v1/customers/{customer}`

<p>Updates the specified customer by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided are left unchanged. For example, if you pass the <strong>source</strong> parameter, that becomes the customer’s active source (such as a card) to be used for all charges in the future. When you update a customer to a new valid card source by passing the <strong>source</strong> parameter: for each of the customer’s current subscriptions, if the subscription bills automatically and is in the <code>past_due</code> state, then the latest open invoice for the subscription with automatic collection enabled is retried. This retry doesn’t count as an automatic retry, and doesn’t affect the next regularly scheduled payment for the invoice. Changing the <strong>default_source</strong> for a customer doesn’t trigger this behavior.</p>

<p>This request accepts mostly the same arguments as the customer creation call.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
address:
  city: string
  country: string
  line1: string

  postal_code: string

  account_number: string

  object: bank_account
  routing_number: string

  address_line1: string
  address_line2: string

  metadata:

  name: string
  network_token:
    number: string
  number: string
  object: card
  swipe_data: string

    reconciliation_mode: automatic
default_alipay_account: string
default_bank_account: string
default_card: string
default_source: string

email: string

  - string
individual_name: string
invoice_prefix: string

  custom_fields:
    -
      name: string
      value: string
  default_payment_method: string
  footer: string

    amount_tax_display: ""
    template: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string

next_invoice_sequence: 0

  - string
shipping:

    city: string

    postal_code: string

  name: string
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/bank_accounts`

<p>When you create a new credit card, you must specify a customer or recipient on which to create it.</p>

<p>If the card’s owner has no default card, then the new card will become the default.
However, if the owner already has a default, then it will not change.
To change the default, you should <a href="/api/customers/update">update the customer</a> to have a new <code>default_source</code>.</p>

```yaml
alipay_account: string
bank_account:

  account_number: string
  country: string
  currency: string

  routing_number: string
card:
  address_city: string
  address_country: string
  address_line1: string
  address_line2: string
  address_state: string
  address_zip: string
  cvc: string
  encrypted: string
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  network_token:
    number: string
  number: string
  object: card
  swipe_data: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
source: string
```

## Update a card

<a id="opIdPostCustomersCustomerBankAccountsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/bank_accounts/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account_holder_name=string&account_holder_type=company&address_city=string&address_country=string&address_line1=string&address_line2=string&address_state=string&address_zip=string&exp_month=string&exp_year=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string&owner=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/bank_accounts/{id}`

<p>Update a specified source for a given customer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_holder_name: string
account_holder_type: company
address_city: string
address_country: string
address_line1: string
address_line2: string
address_state: string
address_zip: string
exp_month: string
exp_year: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
owner:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
```

<h3 id="update-a-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» account_holder_name|body|string|false|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|
|» account_holder_type|body|string|false|The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`.|
|» address_city|body|string|false|City/District/Suburb/Town/Village.|
|» address_country|body|string|false|Billing address country, if provided when creating card.|

|» address_state|body|string|false|State/County/Province/Region.|
|» address_zip|body|string|false|ZIP or postal code.|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit number representing the card’s expiration month.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit number representing the card’s expiration year.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[card](#schemacard)|false|none|You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer<br>later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to<br>transfer to those cards later.<br><br>Related guide: [Card payments with Sources](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/cards)|
|*anyOf*|[bank_account](#schemabank_account)|false|none|These bank accounts are payment methods on `Customer` objects.<br><br>On the other hand [External Accounts](/api#external_accounts) are transfer<br>destinations on `Account` objects for connected accounts.<br>They can be bank accounts or debit cards as well, and are documented in the links above.<br><br>Related guide: [Bank debits and transfers](/payments/bank-debits-transfers)|
|*anyOf*|[source](#schemasource)|false|none|`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They<br>represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API<br>just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be<br>attached to customers.<br><br>Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources).<br>We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods).<br>This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.<br><br>Related guides: [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/customers).|

## List all cards

<a id="opIdGetCustomersCustomerCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/cards \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/customers/{customer}/cards`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

<p>You can see a list of the cards belonging to a customer.
Note that the 10 most recent sources are always available on the <code>Customer</code> object.
If you need more than those 10, you can use this API method and the <code>limit</code> and <code>starting_after</code> parameters to page through additional cards.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-cards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create a card

<a id="opIdPostCustomersCustomerCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/cards \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'alipay_account=string&bank_account=%7B%22account_holder_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22object%22%3A%22bank_account%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&card=%7B%22address_city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_state%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_zip%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22cvc%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22encrypted%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22exp_month%22%3A0%2C%22exp_year%22%3A0%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22network_token%22%3A%7B%22number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22object%22%3A%22card%22%2C%22swipe_data%22%3A%22string%22%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&source=string'
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/cards`

<p>When you create a new credit card, you must specify a customer or recipient on which to create it.</p>

<p>If the card’s owner has no default card, then the new card will become the default.
However, if the owner already has a default, then it will not change.
To change the default, you should <a href="/api/customers/update">update the customer</a> to have a new <code>default_source</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
alipay_account: string
bank_account:
  account_holder_name: string
  account_holder_type: company
  account_number: string
  country: string
  currency: string
  object: bank_account
  routing_number: string
card:
  address_city: string
  address_country: string
  address_line1: string
  address_line2: string
  address_state: string
  address_zip: string
  cvc: string
  encrypted: string
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  network_token:
    number: string
  number: string
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account_holder_name=string&account_holder_type=company&address_city=string&address_country=string&address_line1=string&address_line2=string&address_state=string&address_zip=string&exp_month=string&exp_year=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string&owner=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

|*anyOf*|[card](#schemacard)|false|none|You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer<br>later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to<br>transfer to those cards later.<br><br>Related guide: [Card payments with Sources](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/cards)|

|*anyOf*|[source](#schemasource)|false|none|`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They<br>represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API<br>just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be<br>attached to customers.<br><br>Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources).<br>We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods).<br>This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.<br><br>Related guides: [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/customers).|

## Create or retrieve funding instructions for a customer cash balance

<a id="opIdPostCustomersCustomerFundingInstructions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/funding_instructions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'bank_transfer=%7B%22eu_bank_transfer%22%3A%7B%22country%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22requested_address_types%22%3A%5B%22iban%22%5D%2C%22type%22%3A%22eu_bank_transfer%22%7D&currency=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&funding_type=bank_transfer'
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/funding_instructions`

<p>Retrieve funding instructions for a customer cash balance. If funding instructions do not yet exist for the customer, new
funding instructions will be created. If funding instructions have already been created for a given customer, the same
funding instructions will be retrieved. In other words, we will return the same funding instructions each time.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
bank_transfer:
  eu_bank_transfer:
    country: string
  requested_address_types:
    - iban
  type: eu_bank_transfer
currency: string
expand:
  - string
funding_type: bank_transfer
```

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|type|query|string|false|An optional filter on the list, based on the object `type` field. Without the filter, the list includes all current and future payment method types. ## Create a card

<a id="opIdPostCustomersCustomerSources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/sources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'alipay_account=string&bank_account=%7B%22account_holder_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22object%22%3A%22bank_account%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&card=%7B%22address_city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_state%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_zip%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22cvc%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22encrypted%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22exp_month%22%3A0%2C%22exp_year%22%3A0%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22network_token%22%3A%7B%22number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22object%22%3A%22card%22%2C%22swipe_data%22%3A%22string%22%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&source=string'
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/sources`

<p>When you create a new credit card, you must specify a customer or recipient on which to create it.</p>

<p>If the card’s owner has no default card, then the new card will become the default.
However, if the owner already has a default, then it will not change.
To change the default, you should <a href="/api/customers/update">update the customer</a> to have a new <code>default_source</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
alipay_account: string
bank_account:
  account_holder_name: string
  account_holder_type: company
  account_number: string
  country: string
  currency: string
  object: bank_account
  routing_number: string
card:
  address_city: string
  address_country: string
  address_line1: string
  address_line2: string
  address_state: string
  address_zip: string
  cvc: string
  encrypted: string
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  network_token:
    number: string
  number: string
  object: card
  swipe_data: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
source: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-card-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» alipay_account|body|string|false|A token returned by [Stripe.js](https://stripe.com/docs/js) representing the user’s Alipay account details.|
|» bank_account|body|object \| string|false|Either a token, like the ones returned by [Stripe.js](https://stripe.com/docs/js), or a dictionary containing a user's bank account details.|

|» » account_holder_name|body|string|false|none|

|» » object|body|string|false|none|

|» card|body|object \| string|false|A token, like the ones returned by [Stripe.js](https://stripe.com/docs/js).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » address_city|body|string|false|none|
|» » address_country|body|string|false|none|

|» » address_line2|body|string|false|none|

## Update a card

<a id="opIdPostCustomersCustomerSourcesId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/sources/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account_holder_name=string&account_holder_type=company&address_city=string&address_country=string&address_line1=string&address_line2=string&address_state=string&address_zip=string&exp_month=string&exp_year=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string&owner=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/sources/{id}`

<p>Update a specified source for a given customer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_holder_name: string
account_holder_type: company
address_city: string
address_country: string
address_line1: string
address_line2: string
address_state: string
address_zip: string
exp_month: string
exp_year: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
owner:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» account_holder_name|body|string|false|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|

|» address_state|body|string|false|State/County/Province/Region.|
|» address_zip|body|string|false|ZIP or postal code.|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit number representing the card’s expiration month.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit number representing the card’s expiration year.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. <h3 id="update-a-card-2-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[card](#schemacard)|false|none|You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer<br>later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to<br>transfer to those cards later.<br><br>Related guide: [Card payments with Sources](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/cards)|
|*anyOf*|[bank_account](#schemabank_account)|false|none|These bank accounts are payment methods on `Customer` objects.<br><br>On the other hand [External Accounts](/api#external_accounts) are transfer<br>destinations on `Account` objects for connected accounts.<br>They can be bank accounts or debit cards as well, and are documented in the links above.<br><br>Related guide: [Bank debits and transfers](/payments/bank-debits-transfers)|
|*anyOf*|[source](#schemasource)|false|none|`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They<br>represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API<br>just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be<br>attached to customers.<br><br>Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources).<br>We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods).<br>This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.<br><br>Related guides: [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/customers).|

## List active subscriptions

<a id="opIdGetCustomersCustomerSubscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/subscriptions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions`

<p>You can see a list of the customer’s active subscriptions. Note that the 10 most recent active subscriptions are always available by default on the customer object. If you need more than those 10, you can use the limit and starting_after parameters to page through additional subscriptions.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-active-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions`

<p>Creates a new subscription on an existing customer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
add_invoice_items:
  -
    discountable: true
    discounts:
      -
        coupon: string
        discount: string
        promotion_code: string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    period:
      end:
        timestamp: 0
        type: min_item_period_end
      start:
        timestamp: 0
        type: max_item_period_start
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
  liability:
    account: string
    type: account
backdate_start_date: 0
billing_cycle_anchor: 0
billing_thresholds:
  amount_gte: 0
  reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
cancel_at: 0
cancel_at_period_end: true
collection_method: charge_automatically
currency: string
days_until_due: 0
default_payment_method: string
default_source: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
    promotion_code: string
expand:
  - string
invoice_settings:
  account_tax_ids:
    - string
  custom_fields:
    -
      name: string
      value: string
  description: string
  footer: string
  issuer:
    account: string
    type: account
items:
  -
    billing_thresholds:
      usage_gte: 0
    current_trial:
      trial_offer: string
    discounts:
      -
        coupon: string
        discount: string
        promotion_code: string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
off_session: true
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
payment_settings:
  payment_method_options:
    acss_debit:
      mandate_options:
        transaction_type: business
      verification_method: automatic
    bancontact:
      preferred_language: de
    billie:
      company_details:
        registered_address:
          city: string
          country: string
          line1: string
          line2: string
          postal_code: string
          state: string
        registered_name: string
        registration_number: string
        registration_type: ""
        vat: string
    blik:
      mandate_options:
        expires_at: 0
    card:
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        amount_type: fixed
        description: string
      network: amex
      request_three_d_secure: any
    customer_balance:
      bank_transfer:
        eu_bank_transfer:
          country: string
        type: string
      funding_type: string
    konbini: {}
    payto:
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        purpose: dependant_support
    pix:
      expires_after_seconds: 0
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        amount_includes_iof: always
        end_date: string
        payment_schedule: halfyearly
    sepa_debit: {}
    upi:
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        amount_type: fixed
        description: string
        end_date: 0
    us_bank_account:
      financial_connections:
        filters:
          account_subcategories:
            - checking
        permissions:
          - balances
        prefetch:
          - balances
      verification_method: automatic
  payment_method_types:
    - ach_credit_transfer
  save_default_payment_method: off
pending_invoice_item_interval:
  interval: day
  interval_count: 0
proration_behavior: always_invoice
transfer_data:
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string
trial_end: now
trial_from_plan: true
trial_period_days: 0
trial_settings:
  end_behavior:
    billing_cycle_anchor: now
    missing_payment_method: cancel
```

|» collection_method|body|string|false|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay this subscription at the end of the cycle using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`. Defaults to `charge_automatically`.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|false|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|

|» default_source|body|string|false|ID of the default payment source for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription and be in a chargeable state. ## Retrieve a subscription

<a id="opIdGetCustomersCustomerSubscriptionsSubscriptionExposedId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/subscriptions/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions/{subscription_exposed_id}`

<p>Updates an existing subscription on a customer to match the specified parameters. When changing plans or quantities, we will optionally prorate the price we charge next month to make up for any price changes. To preview how the proration will be calculated, use the <a href="#upcoming_invoice">upcoming invoice</a> endpoint.</p>

## Cancel a subscription

<a id="opIdDeleteCustomersCustomerSubscriptionsSubscriptionExposedId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/string/subscriptions/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice_now=true&prorate=true'
```

`DELETE /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions/{subscription_exposed_id}`

<p>Cancels a customer’s subscription. If you set the <code>at_period_end</code> parameter to <code>true</code>, the subscription will remain active until the end of the period, at which point it will be canceled and not renewed. Otherwise, with the default <code>false</code> value, the subscription is terminated immediately. In either case, the customer will not be charged again for the subscription.</p>

<p>Note, however, that any pending invoice items that you’ve created will still be charged for at the end of the period, unless manually <a href="/api/invoiceitems/delete">deleted</a>. If you’ve set the subscription to cancel at the end of the period, any pending prorations will also be left in place and collected at the end of the period. But if the subscription is set to cancel immediately, pending prorations will be removed.</p>

<p>By default, upon subscription cancellation, Stripe will stop automatic collection of all finalized invoices for the customer. This is intended to prevent unexpected payment attempts after the customer has canceled a subscription. However, you can resume automatic collection of the invoices manually after subscription cancellation to have us proceed. Or, you could check for unpaid invoices before allowing the customer to cancel the subscription at all.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
invoice_now: true
prorate: true
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|subscription_exposed_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» invoice_now|body|boolean|false|Can be set to `true` if `at_period_end` is not set to `true`. Will generate a final invoice that invoices for any un-invoiced metered usage and new/pending proration invoice items.|
|» prorate|body|boolean|false|Can be set to `true` if `at_period_end` is not set to `true`. Will generate a proration invoice item that credits remaining unused time until the subscription period end.|

## List all disputes

<a id="opIdGetDisputes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/disputes \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/disputes`

<p>Returns a list of your disputes.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-disputes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|query|string|false|Only return disputes associated to the charge specified by this charge ID.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return disputes that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|payment_intent|query|string|false|Only return disputes associated to the PaymentIntent specified by this PaymentIntent ID.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/disputes/{dispute}`

<p>When you get a dispute, contacting your customer is always the best first step. If that doesn’t work, you can submit evidence to help us resolve the dispute in your favor. You can do this in your <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/disputes">dashboard</a>, but if you prefer, you can use the API to submit evidence programmatically.</p>

<p>Depending on your dispute type, different evidence fields will give you a better chance of winning your dispute. To figure out which evidence fields to provide, see our <a href="/docs/disputes/categories">guide to dispute types</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
evidence:
  access_activity_log: string
  billing_address: string
  cancellation_policy: string
  cancellation_policy_disclosure: string
  cancellation_rebuttal: string
  customer_communication: string
  customer_email_address: string
  customer_name: string
  customer_purchase_ip: string
  customer_signature: string
  duplicate_charge_documentation: string
  duplicate_charge_explanation: string
  duplicate_charge_id: string
  enhanced_evidence:
    mastercard_compliance:
      fee_acknowledged: true
    visa_compelling_evidence_3:
      disputed_transaction:
        customer_account_id: string
        customer_device_fingerprint: string
        customer_device_id: string
        customer_email_address: string
        customer_purchase_ip: string
        merchandise_or_services: merchandise
        product_description: string
        shipping_address:
          city: string
          country: string
          line1: string
          line2: string
          postal_code: string
          state: string
      prior_undisputed_transactions:
        -
          charge: string
          customer_account_id: string
          customer_device_fingerprint: string
          customer_device_id: string
          customer_email_address: string
          customer_purchase_ip: string
          product_description: string
          shipping_address:
            city: string
            country: string
            line1: string
            line2: string
            postal_code: string
            state: string
    visa_compliance:
      fee_acknowledged: true
  product_description: string
  receipt: string
  refund_policy: string
  refund_policy_disclosure: string
  refund_refusal_explanation: string
  service_date: string
  service_documentation: string
  shipping_address: string
  shipping_carrier: string
  shipping_date: string
  shipping_documentation: string
  shipping_tracking_number: string
  uncategorized_file: string
  uncategorized_text: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
submit: true
```

## Close a dispute

<a id="opIdPostDisputesDisputeClose"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/disputes/string/close \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/disputes/{dispute}/close`

<p>Closing the dispute for a charge indicates that you do not have any evidence to submit and are essentially dismissing the dispute (accepting it), acknowledging it as lost.</p>

<p>The status of the dispute will change from <code>needs_response</code> to <code>lost</code>. <em>Closing a dispute is irreversible</em>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="close-a-dispute-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dispute|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|type|query|string|false|A string containing a specific event name, or group of events using * as a wildcard. The list will be filtered to include only events with a matching event property.|

## Update a bank account

<a id="opIdPostExternalAccountsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/external_accounts/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account_holder_name=string&account_holder_type=&account_type=checking&address_city=string&address_country=string&address_line1=string&address_line2=string&address_state=string&address_zip=string&default_for_currency=true&documents=%7B%22bank_account_ownership_verification%22%3A%7B%22files%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D%7D&exp_month=string&exp_year=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string'
```

`POST /v1/external_accounts/{id}`

<p>Updates the metadata, account holder name, account holder type of a bank account belonging to
a connected account and optionally sets it as the default for its currency. Other bank account
details are not editable by design.</p>

<p>You can only update bank accounts when <a href="/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection">account.controller.requirement_collection</a> is <code>application</code>, which includes <a href="/connect/custom-accounts">Custom accounts</a>.</p>

<p>You can re-enable a disabled bank account by performing an update call without providing any
arguments or changes.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_holder_name: string
account_holder_type: ""
account_type: checking
address_city: string
address_country: string
address_line1: string
address_line2: string
address_state: string
address_zip: string
default_for_currency: true
documents:
  bank_account_ownership_verification:
    files:
      - string
exp_month: string
exp_year: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
```

<h3 id="update-a-bank-account-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» account_holder_name|body|string|false|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|
|» account_holder_type|body|string|false|The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`.|
|» account_type|body|string|false|The bank account type. This can only be `checking` or `savings` in most countries. In Japan, this can only be `futsu` or `toza`.|
|» address_city|body|string|false|City/District/Suburb/Town/Village.|
|» address_country|body|string|false|Billing address country, if provided when creating card.|
|» address_line1|body|string|false|Address line 1 (Street address/PO Box/Company name).|
|» address_line2|body|string|false|Address line 2 (Apartment/Suite/Unit/Building).|
|» address_state|body|string|false|State/County/Province/Region.|
|» address_zip|body|string|false|ZIP or postal code.|
|» default_for_currency|body|boolean|false|When set to true, this becomes the default external account for its currency.|
|» documents|body|object|false|Documents that may be submitted to satisfy various informational requests.|
|» » bank_account_ownership_verification|body|object|false|none|
|» » » files|body|[string]|false|none|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit number representing the card’s expiration month.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit number representing the card’s expiration year.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Cardholder name.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» account_holder_type|""|
|» account_holder_type|company|
|» account_holder_type|individual|
|» account_type|checking|
|» account_type|futsu|
|» account_type|savings|
|» account_type|toza|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

## Create a file

<a id="opIdPostFiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'expand=["string"]' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'file_link_data={"create":true,"expires_at":0,"metadata":{"property1":"string","property2":"string"}}' \
  -F 'purpose=account_requirement'
```

`POST /v1/files`

<p>To upload a file to Stripe, you need to send a request of type <code>multipart/form-data</code>. Include the file you want to upload in the request, and the parameters for creating a file.</p>

<p>All of Stripe’s officially supported Client libraries support sending <code>multipart/form-data</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
file: string
file_link_data:
  create: true
  expires_at: 0
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
purpose: account_requirement
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|A file to upload. Make sure that the specifications follow RFC 2388, which defines file transfers for the `multipart/form-data` protocol.|
|» file_link_data|body|object|false|Optional parameters that automatically create a [file link](https://docs.stripe.com/api#file_links) for the newly created file.|
|» » create|body|boolean|true|none|
|» » expires_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» purpose|body|string|true|The [purpose](https://docs.stripe.com/file-upload#uploading-a-file) of the uploaded file.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» » » *anyOf*|""|
