```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/linked_accounts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/linked_accounts`

<p>Returns a list of Financial Connections <code>Account</code> objects.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-accounts-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_holder|query|object|false|If present, only return accounts that belong to the specified account holder. `account_holder[customer]` and `account_holder[account]` are mutually exclusive.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|session|query|string|false|If present, only return accounts that were collected as part of the given session.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="list-payment-attempt-records-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-payment-attempt-records-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[payment_attempt_record](#schemapayment_attempt_record)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve a Payment Attempt Record

<a id="opIdGetPaymentAttemptRecordsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_attempt_records/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_attempt_records/{id}`

<p>Retrieves a Payment Attempt Record with the given ID</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-payment-attempt-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the Payment Attempt Record.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-payment-attempt-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[payment_attempt_record](#schemapayment_attempt_record)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## List all PaymentIntents

<a id="opIdGetPaymentIntents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_intents`

<p>Returns a list of PaymentIntents.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-paymentintents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|A filter on the list, based on the object `created` field. The value can be a string with an integer Unix timestamp or a dictionary with a number of different query options.|
|customer|query|string|false|Only return PaymentIntents for the customer that this customer ID specifies.|
|customer_account|query|string|false|Only return PaymentIntents for the account representing the customer that this ID specifies.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="list-all-paymentintents-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-all-paymentintents-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

`POST /v1/payment_intents`

<p>Creates a PaymentIntent object.</p>

<p>After the PaymentIntent is created, attach a payment method and <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/confirm">confirm</a>
to continue the payment. Learn more about <a href="/docs/payments/payment-intents">the available payment flows
with the Payment Intents API</a>.</p>

<p>When you use <code>confirm=true</code> during creation, it’s equivalent to creating
and confirming the PaymentIntent in the same call. You can use any parameters
available in the <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/confirm">confirm API</a> when you supply
<code>confirm=true</code>.</p>

|» setup_future_usage|body|string|false|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Search PaymentIntents

<a id="opIdGetPaymentIntentsSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_intents/search`

<p>Search for PaymentIntents you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="search-paymentintents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://docs.stripe.com/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for payment intents](https://docs.stripe.com/search#query-fields-for-paymentintents).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="search-paymentintents-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="search-paymentintents-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|none|
|next_page|string \| null|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|total_count|integer|false|none|The total number of objects that match the query, only accurate up to 10,000.|
|url|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|search_result|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve a PaymentIntent

<a id="opIdGetPaymentIntentsIntent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_intents/{intent}`

<p>Retrieves the details of a PaymentIntent that has previously been created. </p>

<p>You can retrieve a PaymentIntent client-side using a publishable key when the <code>client_secret</code> is in the query string. </p>

<p>If you retrieve a PaymentIntent with a publishable key, it only returns a subset of properties. Refer to the <a href="/api/payment_intents/object">payment intent</a> object reference for more details.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-paymentintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_secret|query|string|false|The client secret of the PaymentIntent. We require it if you use a publishable key to retrieve the source.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-paymentintent-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Update a PaymentIntent

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}`

<p>Updates properties on a PaymentIntent object without confirming.</p>

<p>Depending on which properties you update, you might need to confirm the
PaymentIntent again. For example, updating the <code>payment_method</code>
always requires you to confirm the PaymentIntent again. If you prefer to
update and confirm at the same time, we recommend updating properties through
the <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/confirm">confirm API</a> instead.</p>

|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» setup_future_usage|body|string|false|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).<br><br>If you've already set `setup_future_usage` and you're performing a request using a publishable key, you can only update the value from `on_session` to `off_session`.|
|» shipping|body|object \| string|false|Shipping information for this PaymentIntent.|

## List all PaymentIntent LineItems

<a id="opIdGetPaymentIntentsIntentAmountDetailsLineItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string/amount_details_line_items \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/amount_details_line_items`

<p>Lists all LineItems of a given PaymentIntent.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-paymentintent-lineitems-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|

|---|---|
|object|list|

## Reconcile a customer_balance PaymentIntent

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentApplyCustomerBalance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string/apply_customer_balance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/apply_customer_balance`

<p>Manually reconcile the remaining amount for a <code>customer_balance</code> PaymentIntent.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="reconcile-a-customerbalance-paymentintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount that you intend to apply to this PaymentIntent from the customer’s cash balance. If the PaymentIntent was created by an Invoice, the full amount of the PaymentIntent is applied regardless of this parameter.<br><br>A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (for example, 100 cents to charge 1 USD or 100 to charge 100 JPY, a zero-decimal currency). The maximum amount is the amount of the PaymentIntent.<br><br>When you omit the amount, it defaults to the remaining amount requested on the PaymentIntent.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|false|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

<h3 id="reconcile-a-customerbalance-paymentintent-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Cancel a PaymentIntent

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'cancellation_reason=abandoned&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/cancel`

<p>You can cancel a PaymentIntent object when it’s in one of these statuses: <code>requires_payment_method</code>, <code>requires_capture</code>, <code>requires_confirmation</code>, <code>requires_action</code> or, <a href="/docs/payments/intents">in rare cases</a>, <code>processing</code>. </p>

<p>After it’s canceled, no additional charges are made by the PaymentIntent and any operations on the PaymentIntent fail with an error. For PaymentIntents with a <code>status</code> of <code>requires_capture</code>, the remaining <code>amount_capturable</code> is automatically refunded. </p>

<p>You can directly cancel the PaymentIntent for a Checkout Session only when the PaymentIntent has a status of <code>requires_capture</code>. Otherwise, you must <a href="/docs/api/checkout/sessions/expire">expire the Checkout Session</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
cancellation_reason: abandoned
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-paymentintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cancellation_reason|body|string|false|Reason for canceling this PaymentIntent. Possible values are: `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`, or `abandoned`|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cancellation_reason|abandoned|
|» cancellation_reason|duplicate|
|» cancellation_reason|fraudulent|
|» cancellation_reason|requested_by_customer|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Capture a PaymentIntent

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentCapture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string/capture \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount_details=%7B%22discount_amount%22%3A0%2C%22enforce_arithmetic_validation%22%3Atrue%2C%22line_items%22%3A%5B%7B%22discount_amount%22%3A0%2C%22payment_method_options%22%3A%7B%22card%22%3A%7B%22commodity_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22card_present%22%3A%7B%22commodity_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22klarna%22%3A%7B%22image_url%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product_url%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22reference%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22subscription_reference%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22paypal%22%3A%7B%22category%22%3A%22digital_goods%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22sold_by%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D%2C%22product_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22tax%22%3A%7B%22total_tax_amount%22%3A0%7D%2C%22unit_cost%22%3A0%2C%22unit_of_measure%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22shipping%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22from_postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22to_postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22tax%22%3A%7B%22total_tax_amount%22%3A0%7D%7D&amount_to_capture=0&application_fee_amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&final_capture=true&hooks=%7B%22inputs%22%3A%7B%22tax%22%3A%7B%22calculation%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_details=%7B%22customer_reference%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22order_reference%22%3A%22string%22%7D&statement_descriptor=string&statement_descriptor_suffix=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/capture`

<p>Capture the funds of an existing uncaptured PaymentIntent when its status is <code>requires_capture</code>.</p>

<p>Uncaptured PaymentIntents are cancelled a set number of days (7 by default) after their creation.</p>

<p>Learn more about <a href="/docs/payments/capture-later">separate authorization and capture</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount_details:
  discount_amount: 0
  enforce_arithmetic_validation: true
  line_items:
    -
      discount_amount: 0
      payment_method_options:
        card:
          commodity_code: string
        card_present:
          commodity_code: string
        klarna:
          image_url: string
          product_url: string
          reference: string
          subscription_reference: string
        paypal:
          category: digital_goods
          description: string
          sold_by: string
      product_code: string
      product_name: string
      quantity: 0
      tax:
        total_tax_amount: 0
      unit_cost: 0
      unit_of_measure: string
  shipping:
    amount: 0
    from_postal_code: string
    to_postal_code: string
  tax:
    total_tax_amount: 0
amount_to_capture: 0
application_fee_amount: 0
expand:
  - string
final_capture: true
hooks:
  inputs:
    tax:
      calculation: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_details:
  customer_reference: string
  order_reference: string
statement_descriptor: string
statement_descriptor_suffix: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
```

<h3 id="capture-a-paymentintent-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Confirm a PaymentIntent

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentConfirm"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string/confirm \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/confirm`

<p>Confirm that your customer intends to pay with current or provided
payment method. Upon confirmation, the PaymentIntent will attempt to initiate
a payment.</p>

<p>If the selected payment method requires additional authentication steps, the
PaymentIntent will transition to the <code>requires_action</code> status and
suggest additional actions via <code>next_action</code>. If payment fails,
the PaymentIntent transitions to the <code>requires_payment_method</code> status or the
<code>canceled</code> status if the confirmation limit is reached. If
payment succeeds, the PaymentIntent will transition to the <code>succeeded</code>
status (or <code>requires_capture</code>, if <code>capture_method</code> is set to <code>manual</code>).</p>

<p>If the <code>confirmation_method</code> is <code>automatic</code>, payment may be attempted
using our <a href="/docs/stripe-js/reference#stripe-handle-card-payment">client SDKs</a>
and the PaymentIntent’s <a href="#payment_intent_object-client_secret">client_secret</a>.
After <code>next_action</code>s are handled by the client, no additional
confirmation is required to complete the payment.</p>

<p>If the <code>confirmation_method</code> is <code>manual</code>, all payment attempts must be
initiated using a secret key.</p>

<p>If any actions are required for the payment, the PaymentIntent will
return to the <code>requires_confirmation</code> state
after those actions are completed. Your server needs to then
explicitly re-confirm the PaymentIntent to initiate the next payment
attempt.</p>

<p>There is a variable upper limit on how many times a PaymentIntent can be confirmed.
After this limit is reached, any further calls to this endpoint will
transition the PaymentIntent to the <code>canceled</code> state.</p>

|» return_url|body|string|false|The URL to redirect your customer back to after they authenticate or cancel their payment on the payment method's app or site.<br>If you'd prefer to redirect to a mobile application, you can alternatively supply an application URI scheme.<br>This parameter is only used for cards and other redirect-based payment methods.|
|» setup_future_usage|body|string|false|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).<br><br>If you've already set `setup_future_usage` and you're performing a request using a publishable key, you can only update the value from `on_session` to `off_session`.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Increment an authorization

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentIncrementAuthorization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string/increment_authorization \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&amount_details=%7B%22discount_amount%22%3A0%2C%22enforce_arithmetic_validation%22%3Atrue%2C%22line_items%22%3A%5B%7B%22discount_amount%22%3A0%2C%22payment_method_options%22%3A%7B%22card%22%3A%7B%22commodity_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22card_present%22%3A%7B%22commodity_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22klarna%22%3A%7B%22image_url%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product_url%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22reference%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22subscription_reference%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22paypal%22%3A%7B%22category%22%3A%22digital_goods%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22sold_by%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D%2C%22product_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22tax%22%3A%7B%22total_tax_amount%22%3A0%7D%2C%22unit_cost%22%3A0%2C%22unit_of_measure%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22shipping%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22from_postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22to_postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22tax%22%3A%7B%22total_tax_amount%22%3A0%7D%7D&application_fee_amount=0&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&hooks=%7B%22inputs%22%3A%7B%22tax%22%3A%7B%22calculation%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_details=%7B%22customer_reference%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22order_reference%22%3A%22string%22%7D&statement_descriptor=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/increment_authorization`

<p>Perform an incremental authorization on an eligible
<a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/object">PaymentIntent</a>. To be eligible, the
PaymentIntent’s status must be <code>requires_capture</code> and
<a href="/docs/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-incremental_authorization_supported">incremental_authorization_supported</a>
must be <code>true</code>.</p>

<p>Incremental authorizations attempt to increase the authorized amount on
your customer’s card to the new, higher <code>amount</code> provided. Similar to the
initial authorization, incremental authorizations can be declined. A
single PaymentIntent can call this endpoint multiple times to further
increase the authorized amount.</p>

<p>If the incremental authorization succeeds, the PaymentIntent object
returns with the updated
<a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/object#payment_intent_object-amount">amount</a>.
If the incremental authorization fails, a
<a href="/docs/error-codes#card-declined">card_declined</a> error returns, and no other
fields on the PaymentIntent or Charge update. The PaymentIntent
object remains capturable for the previously authorized amount.</p>

<p>Each PaymentIntent can have a maximum of 10 incremental authorization attempts, including declines.
After it’s captured, a PaymentIntent can no longer be incremented.</p>

<p>Learn more about incremental authorizations with
<a href="/docs/terminal/features/incremental-authorizations">in-person payments</a> and
<a href="/docs/payments/incremental-authorization?platform=web&ui=elements">online payments</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
amount_details:
  discount_amount: 0
  enforce_arithmetic_validation: true
  line_items:
    -
      discount_amount: 0
      payment_method_options:
        card:
          commodity_code: string
        card_present:
          commodity_code: string
        klarna:
          image_url: string
          product_url: string
          reference: string
          subscription_reference: string
        paypal:
          category: digital_goods
          description: string
          sold_by: string
      product_code: string
      product_name: string
      quantity: 0
      tax:
        total_tax_amount: 0
      unit_cost: 0
      unit_of_measure: string
  shipping:
    amount: 0
    from_postal_code: string
    to_postal_code: string
  tax:
    total_tax_amount: 0
application_fee_amount: 0
description: string
expand:
  - string
hooks:
  inputs:
    tax:
      calculation: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_details:
  customer_reference: string
  order_reference: string
statement_descriptor: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Verify microdeposits on a PaymentIntent

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentVerifyMicrodeposits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/string/verify_microdeposits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amounts=%5B0%5D&client_secret=string&descriptor_code=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/verify_microdeposits`

<p>Verifies microdeposits on a PaymentIntent object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amounts:
  - 0
client_secret: string
descriptor_code: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="verify-microdeposits-on-a-paymentintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amounts|body|[integer]|false|Two positive integers, in *cents*, equal to the values of the microdeposits sent to the bank account.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The client secret of the PaymentIntent.|
|» descriptor_code|body|string|false|A six-character code starting with SM present in the microdeposit sent to the bank account.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## List all payment links

<a id="opIdGetPaymentLinks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_links \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_links`

<p>Returns a list of your payment links.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-payment-links-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|query|boolean|false|Only return payment links that are active or inactive (e.g., pass `false` to list all inactive payment links).|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-all-payment-links-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[payment_link](#schemapayment_link)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Create a payment link

<a id="opIdPostPaymentLinks"></a>

```bash

  -X POST \
```

`POST /v1/payment_links`

<p>Creates a payment link.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
after_completion:
  hosted_confirmation:
    custom_message: string
  redirect:
    url: string
  type: hosted_confirmation
allow_promotion_codes: true
application_fee_amount: 0
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
  liability:
    account: string
    type: account
billing_address_collection: auto

    position: auto
  promotions: auto
  terms_of_service: none
currency: string
custom_fields:
  -
    dropdown:
      default_value: string

        -
          label: string
          value: string
    key: string
    label:
      custom: string
      type: custom
    numeric:
      default_value: string
      maximum_length: 0
      minimum_length: 0
    optional: true
    text:
      default_value: string
      maximum_length: 0
      minimum_length: 0
    type: dropdown
custom_text:
  after_submit:
    message: string
  shipping_address:
    message: string
  submit:
    message: string
  terms_of_service_acceptance:
    message: string
customer_creation: always
expand:
  - string
inactive_message: string
invoice_creation:
  enabled: true
  invoice_data:
    account_tax_ids:
      - string
    custom_fields:
      -
        name: string
        value: string
    description: string
    footer: string
    issuer:
      account: string
      type: account
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    rendering_options:
      amount_tax_display: ""
      template: string
line_items:
  -
    adjustable_quantity:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      product_data:
        description: string
        images:
          - string
        metadata:
          property1: string
          property2: string
        name: string
        tax_code: string
        tax_details:
          performance_location: string
          tax_code: string
        unit_label: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
managed_payments:
  enabled: true
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name_collection:
  business:
    enabled: true
    optional: true
  individual:
    enabled: true
    optional: true
on_behalf_of: string
optional_items:
  -
    adjustable_quantity:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
    price: string
    quantity: 0
payment_intent_data:
  capture_method: automatic
  description: string
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  setup_future_usage: off_session
  statement_descriptor: string
  statement_descriptor_suffix: string
  transfer_group: string
payment_method_collection: always
payment_method_options:
  card:
    restrictions:

        - american_express
payment_method_types:
  - affirm
phone_number_collection:
  enabled: true

    limit: 0
shipping_address_collection:

    - AC
shipping_options:
  -
    shipping_rate: string
submit_type: auto

  description: string

    property2: string

    end_behavior:
      missing_payment_method: cancel

  enabled: true
```

## Retrieve a payment link's line items

<a id="opIdGetPaymentLinksPaymentLinkLineItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_links/string/line_items \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_links/{payment_link}/line_items`

<p>When retrieving a payment link, there is an includable <strong>line_items</strong> property containing the first handful of those items. There is also a URL where you can retrieve the full (paginated) list of line items.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-payment-links-line-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|payment_link|path|string|true|none|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## List payment method configurations

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_method_configurations \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_method_configurations`

<p>List payment method configurations</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-payment-method-configurations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|query|boolean|false|Whether the configuration is active.|
|application|query|string|false|The Connect application to filter by.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
```

<h3 id="list-payment-method-configurations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-payment-method-configurations-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[payment_method_configuration](#schemapayment_method_configuration)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[payment_method_configuration](#schemapayment_method_configuration)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve payment method configuration

<a id="opIdGetPaymentMethodConfigurationsConfiguration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_method_configurations/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_method_configurations/{configuration}`

<p>Retrieve payment method configuration</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|false|none|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|object|false|none|

|» » » preference|body|string|false|none|

|» affirm|body|object|false|[Affirm](https://www.affirm.com/) gives your customers a way to split purchases over a series of payments. |» » display_preference|body|object|false|none|
|» » » preference|body|string|false|none|

|» » display_preference|body|object|false|none|

|» » display_preference|body|object|false|none|
|» » » preference|body|string|false|none|

|» » » preference|body|string|false|none|

|» » » preference|body|string|false|none|

|» » » preference|body|string|false|none|

|domain_name|query|string|false|The domain name that this payment method domain object represents.|
|enabled|query|boolean|false|Whether this payment method domain is enabled. If the domain is not enabled, payment methods will not appear in Elements or Embedded Checkout|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Validate an existing payment method domain

<a id="opIdPostPaymentMethodDomainsPaymentMethodDomainValidate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_method_domains/string/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_method_domains/{payment_method_domain}/validate`

<p>Some payment methods might require additional steps to register a domain. If the requirements weren’t satisfied when the domain was created, the payment method will be inactive on the domain.
The payment method doesn’t appear in Elements or Embedded Checkout for this domain until it is active.</p>

<p>To activate a payment method on an existing payment method domain, complete the required registration steps specific to the payment method, and then validate the payment method domain with this endpoint.</p>

<p>Related guides: <a href="/docs/payments/payment-methods/pmd-registration">Payment method domains</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_method_domain|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

<h3 id="list-paymentmethods-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_redisplay|query|string|false|This field indicates whether this payment method can be shown again to its customer in a checkout flow. Stripe products such as Checkout and Elements use this field to determine whether a payment method can be shown as a saved payment method in a checkout flow.|
|customer|query|string|false|The ID of the customer whose PaymentMethods will be retrieved.|
|customer_account|query|string|false|The ID of the Account whose PaymentMethods will be retrieved.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|type|query|string|false|Filters the list by the object `type` field. Unfiltered, the list returns all payment method types except `custom`. If your integration expects only one type of payment method in the response, specify that type value in the request to reduce your payload.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve a PaymentMethod

<a id="opIdGetPaymentMethodsPaymentMethod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_methods/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_methods/{payment_method}`

<p>Retrieves a PaymentMethod object attached to the StripeAccount. To retrieve a payment method attached to a Customer, you should use <a href="/docs/api/payment_methods/customer">Retrieve a Customer’s PaymentMethods</a></p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|payment_method|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Update a PaymentMethod

<a id="opIdPostPaymentMethodsPaymentMethod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_methods/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'allow_redisplay=always&billing_details=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_id%22%3A%22string%22%7D&card=%7B%22exp_month%22%3A0%2C%22exp_year%22%3A0%2C%22networks%22%3A%7B%22preferred%22%3A%22%22%7D%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&us_bank_account=%7B%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_type%22%3A%22checking%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_methods/{payment_method}`

<p>Updates a PaymentMethod object. A PaymentMethod must be attached to a customer to be updated.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
allow_redisplay: always
billing_details:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
  tax_id: string
card:
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
  networks:
    preferred: ""
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
us_bank_account:
  account_holder_type: company
  account_type: checking
```

## Attach a PaymentMethod to a Customer

<a id="opIdPostPaymentMethodsPaymentMethodAttach"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_methods/string/attach \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'customer=string&customer_account=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_methods/{payment_method}/attach`

<p>Attaches a PaymentMethod object to a Customer.</p>

<p>To attach a new PaymentMethod to a customer for future payments, we recommend you use a <a href="/docs/api/setup_intents">SetupIntent</a>
or a PaymentIntent with <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/create#create_payment_intent-setup_future_usage">setup_future_usage</a>.
These approaches will perform any necessary steps to set up the PaymentMethod for future payments. Using the <code>/v1/payment_methods/:id/attach</code>
endpoint without first using a SetupIntent or PaymentIntent with <code>setup_future_usage</code> does not optimize the PaymentMethod for
future use, which makes later declines and payment friction more likely.
See <a href="/docs/payments/payment-intents#future-usage">Optimizing cards for future payments</a> for more information about setting up
future payments.</p>

<p>To use this PaymentMethod as the default for invoice or subscription payments,
set <a href="/docs/api/customers/update#update_customer-invoice_settings-default_payment_method"><code>invoice_settings.default_payment_method</code></a>,
on the Customer to the PaymentMethod’s ID.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
customer: string
customer_account: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="attach-a-paymentmethod-to-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_method|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» customer|body|string|false|The ID of the customer to which to attach the PaymentMethod.|
|» customer_account|body|string|false|The ID of the Account representing the customer to which to attach the PaymentMethod.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## Detach a PaymentMethod from a Customer

<a id="opIdPostPaymentMethodsPaymentMethodDetach"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_methods/string/detach \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_methods/{payment_method}/detach`

<p>Detaches a PaymentMethod object from a Customer. Detachment is permanent and irreversible — once detached, a PaymentMethod can no longer be used for payments or re-attached to a Customer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

|body|body|object|false|none|

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_records/report_payment \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount_requested=%7B%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D&canceled=%7B%22canceled_at%22%3A0%7D&customer_details=%7B%22customer%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D&customer_presence=off_session&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&failed=%7B%22failed_at%22%3A0%7D&guaranteed=%7B%22guaranteed_at%22%3A0%7D&initiated_at=0&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&outcome=canceled&payment_method_details=%7B%22billing_details%22%3A%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22custom%22%3A%7B%22display_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22payment_method%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22custom%22%7D&processor_details=%7B%22custom%22%3A%7B%22payment_reference%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22type%22%3A%22custom%22%7D&shipping_details=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_records/report_payment`

<p>Report a new Payment Record. You may report a Payment Record as it is
 initialized and later report updates through the other report_* methods, or report Payment
 Records in a terminal state directly, through this method.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount_requested:
  currency: string
  value: 0
canceled:
  canceled_at: 0
customer_details:
  customer: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
customer_presence: off_session
description: string
expand:
  - string
failed:
  failed_at: 0
guaranteed:
  guaranteed_at: 0
initiated_at: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
outcome: canceled
payment_method_details:
  billing_details:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    email: string
    name: string
    phone: string
  custom:
    display_name: string
    type: string
  payment_method: string
  type: custom
processor_details:
  custom:
    payment_reference: string
  type: custom
shipping_details:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  name: string
  phone: string
```

## List all payouts

<a id="opIdGetPayouts"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payouts \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payouts`

<p>Returns a list of existing payouts sent to third-party bank accounts or payouts that Stripe sent to you. The payouts return in sorted order, with the most recently created payouts appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-payouts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|arrival_date|query|object \| integer|false|Only return payouts that are expected to arrive during the given date interval.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return payouts that were created during the given date interval.|
|destination|query|string|false|The ID of an external account - only return payouts sent to this external account.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return payouts that have the given status: `pending`, `paid`, `failed`, or `canceled`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create a payout

<a id="opIdPostPayouts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payouts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&destination=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&method=instant&payout_method=string&source_type=bank_account&statement_descriptor=string'
```

`POST /v1/payouts`

<p>To send funds to your own bank account, create a new payout object. Your <a href="#balance">Stripe balance</a> must cover the payout amount. If it doesn’t, you receive an “Insufficient Funds” error.</p>

<p>If your API key is in test mode, money won’t actually be sent, though every other action occurs as if you’re in live mode.</p>

<p>If you create a manual payout on a Stripe account that uses multiple payment source types, you need to specify the source type balance that the payout draws from. The <a href="/api/balances/object">balance object</a> details available and pending amounts by source type.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
destination: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
method: instant
payout_method: string
source_type: bank_account
statement_descriptor: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-payout-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|A positive integer in cents representing how much to pay out.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination|body|string|false|The ID of a bank account or a card to send the payout to. If you don't provide a destination, we use the default external account for the specified currency.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» method|body|string|false|The method used to send this payout, which is `standard` or `instant`. We support `instant` for payouts to debit cards and bank accounts in certain countries. Learn more about [bank support for Instant Payouts](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts/instant-payouts-banks).|
|» payout_method|body|string|false|The ID of a v2 FinancialAccount to send funds to.|
|» source_type|body|string|false|The balance type of your Stripe balance to draw this payout from. Balances for different payment sources are kept separately. You can find the amounts with the Balances API. One of `bank_account`, `card`, or `fpx`.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|A string that displays on the recipient's bank or card statement (up to 22 characters). A `statement_descriptor` that's longer than 22 characters return an error. Most banks truncate this information and display it inconsistently. Some banks might not display it at all. For US ACH payouts, this maps to the ACH Company Entry Description field, which the NACHA standard limits to 10 characters. Stripe truncates descriptors longer than 10 characters for US ACH payouts.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» method|instant|
|» method|standard|
|» source_type|bank_account|
|» source_type|card|
|» source_type|fpx|

## Reverse a payout

<a id="opIdPostPayoutsPayoutReverse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/payouts/string/reverse \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \

```

`POST /v1/payouts/{payout}/reverse`

<p>Reverses a payout by debiting the destination bank account. At this time, you can only reverse payouts for connected accounts to US and Canadian bank accounts. If the payout is manual and in the <code>pending</code> status, use <code>/v1/payouts/:id/cancel</code> instead.</p>

<p>By requesting a reversal through <code>/v1/payouts/:id/reverse</code>, you confirm that the authorized signatory of the selected bank account authorizes the debit on the bank account and that no other authorization is required.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

## Create a plan

<a id="opIdPostPlans"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/plans \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'active=true&amount=0&amount_decimal=string&billing_scheme=per_unit&currency=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&id=string&interval=day&interval_count=0&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&meter=string&nickname=string&product=%7B%22active%22%3Atrue%2C%22id%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22statement_descriptor%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_details%22%3A%7B%22performance_location%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22unit_label%22%3A%22string%22%7D&tiers=%5B%7B%22flat_amount%22%3A0%2C%22flat_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22up_to%22%3A%22inf%22%7D%5D&tiers_mode=graduated&transform_usage=%7B%22divide_by%22%3A0%2C%22round%22%3A%22down%22%7D&trial_period_days=0&usage_type=licensed'
```

`POST /v1/plans`

<p>You can now model subscriptions more flexibly using the <a href="#prices">Prices API</a>. It replaces the Plans API and is backwards compatible to simplify your migration.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
amount: 0
amount_decimal: string
billing_scheme: per_unit
currency: string
expand:
  - string
id: string
interval: day
interval_count: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
meter: string
nickname: string
product:
  active: true
  id: string
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  statement_descriptor: string
  tax_code: string
  tax_details:
    performance_location: string
    tax_code: string
  unit_label: string
tiers:
  -
    flat_amount: 0
    flat_amount_decimal: string
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
    up_to: inf
tiers_mode: graduated
transform_usage:
  divide_by: 0
  round: down
trial_period_days: 0
usage_type: licensed
```

<h3 id="create-a-plan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether the plan is currently available for new subscriptions. Defaults to `true`.|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) (or 0 for a free plan) representing how much to charge on a recurring basis.|
|» amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|Same as `amount`, but accepts a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places. Only one of `amount` and `amount_decimal` can be set.|
|» billing_scheme|body|string|false|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `amount`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for plans with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for plans with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» id|body|string|false|An identifier randomly generated by Stripe. Used to identify this plan when subscribing a customer. You can optionally override this ID, but the ID must be unique across all plans in your Stripe account. You can use the same plan ID in live mode and in your sandboxes.|
|» interval|body|string|true|Specifies billing frequency. Either `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`.|
|» interval_count|body|integer|false|The number of intervals between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months. Maximum of three years interval allowed (3 years, 36 months, or 156 weeks).|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» meter|body|string|false|The meter tracking the usage of a metered price|
|» nickname|body|string|false|A brief description of the plan, hidden from customers.|
|» product|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|The product whose pricing the created plan will represent. This can either be the ID of an existing product, or a dictionary containing fields used to create a [service product](https://docs.stripe.com/api#product_object-type).|
|» » active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » statement_descriptor|body|string|false|none|
|» » tax_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » tax_details|body|object|false|none|
|» » » performance_location|body|string|false|none|
|» » » tax_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » unit_label|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|The ID of the product whose pricing the created plan will represent.|
|» tiers|body|[object]|false|Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`.|
|» » flat_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » flat_amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|none|
|» » unit_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » unit_amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|none|
|» » up_to|body|string \| integer|true|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» tiers_mode|body|string|false|Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price, in `graduated` tiering pricing can successively change as the quantity grows.|
|» transform_usage|body|object|false|Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the billed price. Cannot be combined with `tiers`.|
|» » divide_by|body|integer|true|none|
|» » round|body|string|true|none|
|» trial_period_days|body|integer|false|Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this plan using [`trial_from_plan=true`](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_subscription-trial_from_plan).|
|» usage_type|body|string|false|Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`.|

## Update a plan

<a id="opIdPostPlansPlan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/plans/string \

```

`POST /v1/plans/{plan}`

<p>Updates the specified plan by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided are left unchanged. By design, you cannot change a plan’s ID, amount, currency, or billing cycle.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
nickname: string
product: string
trial_period_days: 0
```

|» trial_period_days|body|integer|false|Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this plan using [`trial_from_plan=true`](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_subscription-trial_from_plan).|

```yaml
active: true
billing_scheme: per_unit
currency: string
currency_options:
  property1:

      enabled: true

      preset: 0

    tiers:

        flat_amount: 0

    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
  property2:
    custom_unit_amount:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
      preset: 0
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tiers:
      -
        flat_amount: 0
        flat_amount_decimal: string
        unit_amount: 0
        unit_amount_decimal: string
        up_to: inf
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string

  enabled: true

  minimum: 0

  - string
lookup_key: string

  property1: string
  property2: string

  active: true

  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string

    tax_code: string

  -
```

<h3 id="create-a-price-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether the price can be used for new purchases. Defaults to `true`.|
|» billing_scheme|body|string|false|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `unit_amount` or `unit_amount_decimal`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for prices with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for prices with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» currency_options|body|object|false|Prices defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|

|» » » » unit_amount|body|integer|false|none|

|» » » » up_to|body|string \| integer|true|none|

|» » » » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » unit_amount|body|integer|false|none|

## Search prices

<a id="opIdGetPricesSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/prices/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/prices/search`

<p>Search for prices you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://docs.stripe.com/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for prices](https://docs.stripe.com/search#query-fields-for-prices).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Update a price

<a id="opIdPostPricesPrice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/prices/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'active=true&currency_options=%7B%22property1%22%3A%7B%22custom_unit_amount%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22maximum%22%3A0%2C%22minimum%22%3A0%2C%22preset%22%3A0%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22tiers%22%3A%5B%7B%22flat_amount%22%3A0%2C%22flat_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22up_to%22%3A%22inf%22%7D%5D%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22property2%22%3A%7B%22custom_unit_amount%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22maximum%22%3A0%2C%22minimum%22%3A0%2C%22preset%22%3A0%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22tiers%22%3A%5B%7B%22flat_amount%22%3A0%2C%22flat_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22up_to%22%3A%22inf%22%7D%5D%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&lookup_key=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&nickname=string&tax_behavior=exclusive&transfer_lookup_key=true'
```

`POST /v1/prices/{price}`

<p>Updates the specified price by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided are left unchanged.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
currency_options:
  property1:
    custom_unit_amount:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
      preset: 0
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tiers:
      -
        flat_amount: 0
        flat_amount_decimal: string
        unit_amount: 0
        unit_amount_decimal: string
        up_to: inf
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
  property2:
    custom_unit_amount:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
      preset: 0
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tiers:
      -
        flat_amount: 0
        flat_amount_decimal: string
        unit_amount: 0
        unit_amount_decimal: string
        up_to: inf
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
expand:
  - string
lookup_key: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
nickname: string
tax_behavior: exclusive
transfer_lookup_key: true
```
