```

`GET /v1/products`

<p>Returns a list of your products. The products are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created products appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|query|boolean|false|Only return products that are active or inactive (e.g., pass `false` to list all inactive products).|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return products that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|ids|query|[string]|false|Only return products with the given IDs. Cannot be used with [starting_after](https://docs.stripe.com/api#list_products-starting_after) or [ending_before](https://docs.stripe.com/api#list_products-ending_before).|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|shippable|query|boolean|false|Only return products that can be shipped (i.e., physical, not digital products).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|url|query|string|false|Only return products with the given url.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Search products

<a id="opIdGetProductsSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/products/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/products/search`

<p>Search for products you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="search-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://docs.stripe.com/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for products](https://docs.stripe.com/search#query-fields-for-products).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

      "id": "string",
      "images": [
        "string"
      ],
      "livemode": true,
      "marketing_features": [
        {
          "name": "string"
        }
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "name": "string",
      "object": "product",
      "package_dimensions": {
        "height": 0,
        "length": 0,
        "weight": 0,
        "width": 0
      },
      "shippable": true,
      "statement_descriptor": "string",
      "tax_code": "string",
      "tax_details": {
        "performance_location": "string",
        "tax_code": "string"
      },
      "unit_label": "string",
      "updated": 0,
      "url": "string"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_page": "string",
  "object": "search_result",
  "total_count": 0,
  "url": "string"
}

## Create a promotion code

<a id="opIdPostPromotionCodes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/promotion_codes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'active=true&code=string&customer=string&customer_account=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&expires_at=0&max_redemptions=0&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&promotion=%7B%22coupon%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22coupon%22%7D&restrictions=%7B%22currency_options%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%7B%22minimum_amount%22%3A0%7D%2C%22property2%22%3A%7B%22minimum_amount%22%3A0%7D%7D%2C%22first_time_transaction%22%3Atrue%2C%22minimum_amount%22%3A0%2C%22minimum_amount_currency%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/promotion_codes`

<p>A promotion code points to an underlying promotion. You can optionally restrict the code to a specific customer, redemption limit, and expiration date.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
code: string
customer: string
customer_account: string
expand:
  - string
expires_at: 0
max_redemptions: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
promotion:
  coupon: string
  type: coupon
restrictions:
  currency_options:
    property1:
      minimum_amount: 0
    property2:
      minimum_amount: 0
  first_time_transaction: true
  minimum_amount: 0
  minimum_amount_currency: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-promotion-code-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether the promotion code is currently active.|
|» code|body|string|false|The customer-facing code. Regardless of case, this code must be unique across all active promotion codes for a specific customer. Valid characters are lower case letters (a-z), upper case letters (A-Z), digits (0-9), and dashes (-).<br><br>If left blank, we will generate one automatically.|
|» customer|body|string|false|The customer who can use this promotion code. If not set, all customers can use the promotion code.|
|» customer_account|body|string|false|The account representing the customer who can use this promotion code. If not set, all customers can use the promotion code.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» expires_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The timestamp at which this promotion code will expire. If the coupon has specified a `redeems_by`, then this value cannot be after the coupon's `redeems_by`.|
|» max_redemptions|body|integer|false|A positive integer specifying the number of times the promotion code can be redeemed. If the coupon has specified a `max_redemptions`, then this value cannot be greater than the coupon's `max_redemptions`.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» promotion|body|object|true|The promotion referenced by this promotion code.|
|» » coupon|body|string|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» restrictions|body|object|false|Settings that restrict the redemption of the promotion code.|
|» » currency_options|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » minimum_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » first_time_transaction|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » minimum_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » minimum_amount_currency|body|string(currency)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|coupon|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

{
  "active": true,
  "code": "string",

## List all quotes

<a id="opIdGetQuotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/quotes \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/quotes`

<p>Returns a list of your quotes.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-quotes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|query|string|false|The ID of the customer whose quotes you're retrieving.|
|customer_account|query|string|false|The ID of the account representing the customer whose quotes you're retrieving.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the quote.|
|test_clock|query|string|false|Provides a list of quotes that are associated with the specified test clock. The response will not include quotes with test clocks if this and the customer parameter is not set.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|accepted|
|status|canceled|
|status|draft|
|status|open|

## Create a quote

<a id="opIdPostQuotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/quotes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'application_fee_amount=0&application_fee_percent=0&automatic_tax=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22liability%22%3A%7B%22account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22account%22%7D%7D&collection_method=charge_automatically&customer=string&customer_account=string&default_tax_rates=%5B%22string%22%5D&description=string&discounts=%5B%7B%22coupon%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22discount%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22promotion_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&expires_at=0&footer=string&from_quote=%7B%22is_revision%22%3Atrue%2C%22quote%22%3A%22string%22%7D&header=string&invoice_settings=%7B%22custom_fields%22%3A%5B%7B%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22days_until_due%22%3A0%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22footer%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22issuer%22%3A%7B%22account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22account%22%7D%7D&line_items=%5B%7B%22discounts%22%3A%5B%7B%22coupon%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22discount%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22promotion_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22price%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22price_data%22%3A%7B%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22recurring%22%3A%7B%22interval%22%3A%22day%22%2C%22interval_count%22%3A0%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22tax_rates%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&on_behalf_of=string&subscription_data=%7B%22billing_mode%22%3A%7B%22flexible%22%3A%7B%22proration_discounts%22%3A%22included%22%7D%2C%22type%22%3A%22classic%22%7D%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22effective_date%22%3A%22current_period_end%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22trial_period_days%22%3A0%7D&test_clock=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22amount_percent%22%3A0%2C%22destination%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/quotes`

<p>A quote models prices and services for a customer. Default options for <code>header</code>, <code>description</code>, <code>footer</code>, and <code>expires_at</code> can be set in the dashboard via the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/quote">quote template</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
application_fee_amount: 0
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
  liability:
    account: string
    type: account
collection_method: charge_automatically
customer: string
customer_account: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
description: string
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
    promotion_code: string
expand:
  - string
expires_at: 0
footer: string
from_quote:
  is_revision: true
  quote: string
header: string
invoice_settings:
  custom_fields:
    -
      name: string
      value: string
  days_until_due: 0
  description: string
  footer: string
  issuer:
    account: string
    type: account
line_items:
  -
    discounts:
      -
        coupon: string
        discount: string
        promotion_code: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
on_behalf_of: string
subscription_data:
  billing_mode:
    flexible:
      proration_discounts: included
    type: classic
  description: string
  effective_date: current_period_end
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  trial_period_days: 0
test_clock: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string
```

|» application_fee_amount|body|integer \| string|false|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. There cannot be any line items with recurring prices when using this field.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. ## Update a quote

<a id="opIdPostQuotesQuote"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

`POST /v1/quotes/{quote}`

<p>A quote models prices and services for a customer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
application_fee_amount: 0
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
  liability:
    account: string
    type: account
collection_method: charge_automatically
customer: string
customer_account: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
description: string
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
    promotion_code: string
expand:
  - string
expires_at: 0
footer: string
header: string
invoice_settings:
  custom_fields:
    -
      name: string
      value: string
  days_until_due: 0
  description: string
  footer: string
  issuer:
    account: string
    type: account
line_items:
  -
    discounts:
      -
        coupon: string
        discount: string
        promotion_code: string
    id: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
on_behalf_of: string
subscription_data:
  description: string
  effective_date: current_period_end
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  trial_period_days: 0
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string

## Accept a quote

<a id="opIdPostQuotesQuoteAccept"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/quotes/string/accept \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/quotes/{quote}/accept`

<p>Accepts the specified quote.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:

## Cancel a quote

<a id="opIdPostQuotesQuoteCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/quotes/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/quotes/{quote}/cancel`

<p>Cancels the quote.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-quote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|quote|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## Retrieve a quote's upfront line items

<a id="opIdGetQuotesQuoteComputedUpfrontLineItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/quotes/string/computed_upfront_line_items \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/quotes/{quote}/computed_upfront_line_items`

<p>When retrieving a quote, there is an includable <a href="https://stripe.com/docs/api/quotes/object#quote_object-computed-upfront-line_items"><strong>computed.upfront.line_items</strong></a> property containing the first handful of those items. There is also a URL where you can retrieve the full (paginated) list of upfront line items.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-quotes-upfront-line-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|quote|path|string|true|none|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Finalize a quote

<a id="opIdPostQuotesQuoteFinalize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/quotes/string/finalize \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&expires_at=0'

expand:

## List all early fraud warnings

<a id="opIdGetRadarEarlyFraudWarnings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/radar/early_fraud_warnings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/radar/early_fraud_warnings`

<p>Returns a list of early fraud warnings.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-early-fraud-warnings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|query|string|false|Only return early fraud warnings for the charge specified by this charge ID.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return early fraud warnings that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|

## List all value list items

<a id="opIdGetRadarValueListItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/radar/value_list_items?value_list=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/radar/value_list_items`

<p>Returns a list of <code>ValueListItem</code> objects. The objects are sorted in descending order by creation date, with the most recently created object appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-value-list-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return items that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|value|query|string|false|Return items belonging to the parent list whose value matches the specified value (using an "is like" match).|
|value_list|query|string|true|Identifier for the parent value list this item belongs to.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create a refund

<a id="opIdPostRefunds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/refunds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&charge=string&currency=string&customer=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&instructions_email=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&origin=customer_balance&payment_intent=string&reason=duplicate&refund_application_fee=true&reverse_transfer=true'
```

`POST /v1/refunds`

<p>When you create a new refund, you must specify a Charge or a PaymentIntent object on which to create it.</p>

<p>Creating a new refund will refund a charge that has previously been created but not yet refunded.
Funds will be refunded to the credit or debit card that was originally charged.</p>

<p>You can optionally refund only part of a charge.
You can do so multiple times, until the entire charge has been refunded.</p>

<p>Once entirely refunded, a charge can’t be refunded again.
This method will raise an error when called on an already-refunded charge,
or when trying to refund more money than is left on a charge.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
charge: string
currency: string
customer: string
expand:
  - string
instructions_email: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
origin: customer_balance
payment_intent: string
reason: duplicate
refund_application_fee: true
reverse_transfer: true
```

<h3 id="create-a-refund-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» charge|body|string|false|The identifier of the charge to refund.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|false|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» customer|body|string|false|Customer whose customer balance to refund from.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» instructions_email|body|string|false|For payment methods without native refund support (e.g., Konbini, PromptPay), use this email from the customer to receive refund instructions.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» origin|body|string|false|Origin of the refund|
|» payment_intent|body|string|false|The identifier of the PaymentIntent to refund.|
|» reason|body|string|false|String indicating the reason for the refund. If set, possible values are `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, and `requested_by_customer`. If you believe the charge to be fraudulent, specifying `fraudulent` as the reason will add the associated card and email to your [block lists](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/lists), and will also help us improve our fraud detection algorithms.|
|» refund_application_fee|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when refunding this charge. If a full charge refund is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded in an amount proportional to the amount of the charge refunded. An application fee can be refunded only by the application that created the charge.|
|» reverse_transfer|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the transfer should be reversed when refunding this charge. The transfer will be reversed proportionally to the amount being refunded (either the entire or partial amount).<br><br>A transfer can be reversed only by the application that created the charge.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|
|» origin|customer_balance|
|» reason|duplicate|
|» reason|fraudulent|
|» reason|requested_by_customer|

<h3 id="cancel-a-refund-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[refund](#schemarefund)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## List all Report Runs

<a id="opIdGetReportingReportRuns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/reporting/report_runs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/reporting/report_runs`

<p>Returns a list of Report Runs, with the most recent appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-report-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return Report Runs that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

{

    {
      "created": 0,
      "error": "string",

          "string"
        ],

      },

        "filename": "string",

        "links": {
          "data": [
            {}
          ],
          "has_more": true,
          "object": "list",
          "url": "string"
        },
        "object": "file",

        "size": 0,
        "title": "string",
        "type": "string",
        "url": "string"
      },

    }
  ],

<h3 id="list-all-report-runs-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[reporting.report_run](#schemareporting.report_run)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|

|object|list|

## Create a Report Run

<a id="opIdPostReportingReportRuns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/reporting/report_runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&parameters=%7B%22columns%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22connected_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22interval_end%22%3A0%2C%22interval_start%22%3A0%2C%22payout%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22reporting_category%22%3A%22advance%22%2C%22timezone%22%3A%22Africa%2FAbidjan%22%7D&report_type=string'
```

`POST /v1/reporting/report_runs`

<p>Creates a new object and begin running the report. (Certain report types require a <a href="https://stripe.com/docs/keys#test-live-modes">live-mode API key</a>.)</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
parameters:
  columns:
    - string
  connected_account: string
  currency: string
  interval_end: 0
  interval_start: 0
  payout: string
  reporting_category: advance
  timezone: Africa/Abidjan
report_type: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-report-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» parameters|body|object|false|Parameters specifying how the report should be run. Different Report Types have different required and optional parameters, listed in the [API Access to Reports](https://docs.stripe.com/reporting/statements/api) documentation.|
|» » columns|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » connected_account|body|string|false|none|
|» » currency|body|string(currency)|false|none|
|» » interval_end|body|integer(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » interval_start|body|integer(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » payout|body|string|false|none|
|» » reporting_category|body|string|false|none|
|» » timezone|body|string|false|none|
|» report_type|body|string|true|The ID of the [report type](https://docs.stripe.com/reporting/statements/api#report-types) to run, such as `"balance.summary.1"`.|

## List all open reviews

<a id="opIdGetReviews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/reviews \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/reviews`

<p>Returns a list of <code>Review</code> objects that have <code>open</code> set to <code>true</code>. The objects are sorted in descending order by creation date, with the most recently created object appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-open-reviews-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return reviews that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

        "platform": "string",

    }
  ],

  "url": "string"
}

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|

`POST /v1/setup_intents`

<p>Creates a SetupIntent object.</p>

<p>After you create the SetupIntent, attach a payment method and <a href="/docs/api/setup_intents/confirm">confirm</a>
it to collect any required permissions to charge the payment method later.</p>

<h3 id="create-a-setupintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allowed_payment_method_types|body|[string]|false|The list of payment method types to allow for this SetupIntent. Stripe will only use methods in this list when determining the payment methods to offer. A list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).|
|» attach_to_self|body|boolean|false|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|» automatic_payment_methods|body|object|false|When you enable this parameter, this SetupIntent accepts payment methods that you enable in the Dashboard and that are compatible with its other parameters.|
|» » allow_redirects|body|string|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» confirm|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to attempt to confirm this SetupIntent immediately. This parameter defaults to `false`. If a card is the attached payment method, you can provide a `return_url` in case further authentication is necessary.|
|» confirmation_token|body|string|false|ID of the ConfirmationToken used to confirm this SetupIntent.<br><br>If the provided ConfirmationToken contains properties that are also being provided in this request, such as `payment_method`, then the values in this request will take precedence.|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|» customer_account|body|string|false|ID of the Account this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Account on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Accounts cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» excluded_payment_method_types|body|[string]|false|The list of payment method types to exclude from use with this SetupIntent.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» flow_directions|body|[string]|false|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|» mandate_data|body|object \| string|false|This hash contains details about the mandate to create. This parameter can only be used with [`confirm=true`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/create#create_setup_intent-confirm).|

|» » » » user_agent|body|string|true|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» on_behalf_of|body|string|false|The Stripe account ID created for this SetupIntent.|
|» payment_method|body|string|false|ID of the payment method (a PaymentMethod, Card, or saved Source object) to attach to this SetupIntent.|
|» payment_method_configuration|body|string|false|The ID of the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) to use with this SetupIntent.|
|» payment_method_data|body|object|false|When included, this hash creates a PaymentMethod that is set as the [`payment_method`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-payment_method)<br>value in the SetupIntent.|

|» return_url|body|string|false|The URL to redirect your customer back to after they authenticate or cancel their payment on the payment method's app or site. To redirect to a mobile application, you can alternatively supply an application URI scheme. This parameter can only be used with [`confirm=true`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/create#create_setup_intent-confirm).|
|» single_use|body|object|false|If you populate this hash, this SetupIntent generates a `single_use` mandate after successful completion.<br><br>Single-use mandates are only valid for the following payment methods: `acss_debit`, `alipay`, `au_becs_debit`, `bacs_debit`, `bancontact`, `boleto`, `ideal`, `link`, `sepa_debit`, and `us_bank_account`.|
|» » amount|body|integer|true|none|
|» » currency|body|string(currency)|true|none|
|» usage|body|string|false|Indicates how the payment method is intended to be used in the future. If not provided, this value defaults to `off_session`.|
|» use_stripe_sdk|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` when confirming server-side and using Stripe.js, iOS, or Android client-side SDKs to handle the next actions.|

## Retrieve a SetupIntent

<a id="opIdGetSetupIntentsIntent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/setup_intents/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/setup_intents/{intent}`

<p>Retrieves the details of a SetupIntent that has previously been created. </p>

<p>Client-side retrieval using a publishable key is allowed when the <code>client_secret</code> is provided in the query string. </p>

<p>When retrieved with a publishable key, only a subset of properties will be returned. Please refer to the <a href="#setup_intent_object">SetupIntent</a> object reference for more details.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-setupintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_secret|query|string|false|The client secret of the SetupIntent. We require this string if you use a publishable key to retrieve the SetupIntent.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Update a SetupIntent

<a id="opIdPostSetupIntentsIntent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/setup_intents/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

<h3 id="update-a-setupintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» allowed_payment_method_types|body|[string] \| string|false|The list of payment method types to allow for this SetupIntent. Stripe will only use methods in this list when determining the payment methods to offer. A list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» attach_to_self|body|boolean|false|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|» customer_account|body|string|false|ID of the Account this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Account on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Accounts cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» excluded_payment_method_types|body|[string] \| string|false|The list of payment method types to exclude from use with this SetupIntent.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» flow_directions|body|[string]|false|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|

|» payment_method_configuration|body|string|false|The ID of the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) to use with this SetupIntent.|
|» payment_method_data|body|object|false|When included, this hash creates a PaymentMethod that is set as the [`payment_method`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-payment_method)<br>value in the SetupIntent.|

## Cancel a SetupIntent

<a id="opIdPostSetupIntentsIntentCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/setup_intents/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'cancellation_reason=abandoned&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/setup_intents/{intent}/cancel`

<p>You can cancel a SetupIntent object when it’s in one of these statuses: <code>requires_payment_method</code>, <code>requires_confirmation</code>, or <code>requires_action</code>. </p>

<p>After you cancel it, setup is abandoned and any operations on the SetupIntent fail with an error. You can’t cancel the SetupIntent for a Checkout Session. <a href="/docs/api/checkout/sessions/expire">Expire the Checkout Session</a> instead.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
cancellation_reason: abandoned
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-setupintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cancellation_reason|body|string|false|Reason for canceling this SetupIntent. Possible values are: `abandoned`, `requested_by_customer`, or `duplicate`|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cancellation_reason|abandoned|
|» cancellation_reason|duplicate|
|» cancellation_reason|requested_by_customer|

`POST /v1/setup_intents/{intent}/confirm`

<p>Confirm that your customer intends to set up the current or
provided payment method. For example, you would confirm a SetupIntent
when a customer hits the “Save” button on a payment method management
page on your website.</p>

<p>If the selected payment method does not require any additional
steps from the customer, the SetupIntent will transition to the
<code>succeeded</code> status.</p>

<p>Otherwise, it will transition to the <code>requires_action</code> status and
suggest additional actions via <code>next_action</code>. If setup fails,
the SetupIntent will transition to the
<code>requires_payment_method</code> status or the <code>canceled</code> status if the
confirmation limit is reached.</p>

## Verify microdeposits on a SetupIntent

<a id="opIdPostSetupIntentsIntentVerifyMicrodeposits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/setup_intents/string/verify_microdeposits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amounts=%5B0%5D&client_secret=string&descriptor_code=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/setup_intents/{intent}/verify_microdeposits`

<p>Verifies microdeposits on a SetupIntent object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amounts:
  - 0
client_secret: string
descriptor_code: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="verify-microdeposits-on-a-setupintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amounts|body|[integer]|false|Two positive integers, in *cents*, equal to the values of the microdeposits sent to the bank account.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The client secret of the SetupIntent.|
|» descriptor_code|body|string|false|A six-character code starting with SM present in the microdeposit sent to the bank account.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## List all shipping rates

<a id="opIdGetShippingRates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/shipping_rates \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/shipping_rates`

<p>Returns a list of your shipping rates.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-shipping-rates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|query|boolean|false|Only return shipping rates that are active or inactive.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|A filter on the list, based on the object `created` field. The value can be a string with an integer Unix timestamp, or it can be a dictionary with a number of different query options.|
|currency|query|string(currency)|false|Only return shipping rates for the given currency.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

          "unit": "business_day",
          "value": 0
        }
      },

        "amount": 0,

          "property1": {
            "amount": 0,

            "tax_behavior": "exclusive"
          }

## Create a shipping rate

<a id="opIdPostShippingRates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/shipping_rates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'delivery_estimate=%7B%22maximum%22%3A%7B%22unit%22%3A%22business_day%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D%2C%22minimum%22%3A%7B%22unit%22%3A%22business_day%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D%7D&display_name=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&fixed_amount=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency_options%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%7D%2C%22property2%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%7D%7D%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&tax_behavior=exclusive&tax_code=string&type=fixed_amount'
```

`POST /v1/shipping_rates`

<p>Creates a new shipping rate object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
delivery_estimate:
  maximum:
    unit: business_day
    value: 0
  minimum:
    unit: business_day
    value: 0
display_name: string
expand:
  - string
fixed_amount:
  amount: 0
  currency: string
  currency_options:
    property1:
      amount: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
    property2:
      amount: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
tax_behavior: exclusive
tax_code: string
type: fixed_amount
```

<h3 id="create-a-shipping-rate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

  amount: 0
  currency: string
  interval: one_time
  notification_method: deprecated_none
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
original_source: string
owner:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
receiver:
  refund_attributes_method: email
redirect:
  return_url: string
source_order:
  items:
    -
      amount: 0
      currency: string
      description: string
      parent: string
      quantity: 0
      type: discount
  shipping:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    carrier: string
    name: string
    phone: string
    tracking_number: string
statement_descriptor: string
token: string
type: string
usage: reusable
```

<h3 id="create-a-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount associated with the source. This is the amount for which the source will be chargeable once ready. Required for `single_use` sources. Not supported for `receiver` type sources, where charge amount may not be specified until funds land.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|false|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) associated with the source. This is the currency for which the source will be chargeable once ready.|
|» customer|body|string|false|The `Customer` to whom the original source is attached to. Must be set when the original source is not a `Source` (e.g., `Card`).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» flow|body|string|false|The authentication `flow` of the source to create. `flow` is one of `redirect`, `receiver`, `code_verification`, `none`. It is generally inferred unless a type supports multiple flows.|
|» mandate|body|object|false|Information about a mandate possibility attached to a source object (generally for bank debits) as well as its acceptance status.|

## Retrieve a source

<a id="opIdGetSourcesSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/sources/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/sources/{source}`

<p>Retrieves an existing source object. Supply the unique source ID from a source creation request and Stripe will return the corresponding up-to-date source object information.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|source|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Update a source

<a id="opIdPostSourcesSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/sources/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&mandate=%7B%22acceptance%22%3A%7B%22date%22%3A0%2C%22ip%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22offline%22%3A%7B%22contact_email%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22online%22%3A%7B%22date%22%3A0%2C%22ip%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22user_agent%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22status%22%3A%22accepted%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22offline%22%2C%22user_agent%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22interval%22%3A%22one_time%22%2C%22notification_method%22%3A%22deprecated_none%22%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&owner=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D&source_order=%7B%22items%22%3A%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22parent%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22type%22%3A%22discount%22%7D%5D%2C%22shipping%22%3A%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22carrier%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tracking_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D'
```

`POST /v1/sources/{source}`

<p>Updates the specified source by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.</p>

<p>This request accepts the <code>metadata</code> and <code>owner</code> as arguments. It is also possible to update type specific information for selected payment methods. Please refer to our <a href="/docs/sources">payment method guides</a> for more detail.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
expand:
  - string
mandate:
  acceptance:
    date: 0
    ip: string
    offline:
      contact_email: string
    online:
      date: 0
      ip: string
      user_agent: string
    status: accepted
    type: offline
    user_agent: string
  amount: 0
  currency: string
  interval: one_time
  notification_method: deprecated_none
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
owner:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
source_order:
  items:
    -
      amount: 0
      currency: string
      description: string
      parent: string
      quantity: 0
      type: discount
  shipping:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    carrier: string
    name: string
    phone: string
    tracking_number: string
```

## Create a subscription item

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/subscription_items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'billing_thresholds=%7B%22usage_gte%22%3A0%7D&current_trial=%7B%22trial_offer%22%3A%22string%22%7D&discounts=%5B%7B%22coupon%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22discount%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22promotion_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_behavior=allow_incomplete&price=string&price_data=%7B%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22recurring%22%3A%7B%22interval%22%3A%22day%22%2C%22interval_count%22%3A0%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D&proration_behavior=always_invoice&proration_date=0&quantity=0&subscription=string&tax_rates=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/subscription_items`

<p>Adds a new item to an existing subscription. No existing items will be changed or replaced.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
billing_thresholds:
  usage_gte: 0
current_trial:
  trial_offer: string
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
    promotion_code: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
price: string
price_data:
  currency: string
  product: string
  recurring:
    interval: day
    interval_count: 0
  tax_behavior: exclusive
  unit_amount: 0
  unit_amount_decimal: string
proration_behavior: always_invoice
proration_date: 0
quantity: 0
subscription: string
tax_rates:
  - string
```

<h3 id="create-a-subscription-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» billing_thresholds|body|object \| string|false|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period. Pass an empty string to remove previously-defined thresholds.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » usage_gte|body|integer|true|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» current_trial|body|object|false|The trial offer to apply to this subscription item.|
|» » trial_offer|body|string|true|none|
|» discounts|body|[object] \| string|false|The coupons to redeem into discounts for the subscription item.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[object]|false|none|
|» coupon|body|string|false|none|
|» discount|body|string|false|none|
|» promotion_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» payment_behavior|body|string|false|Controls how Stripe handles payment when a subscription update requires payment and `collection_method=charge_automatically`.|
|» price|body|string|false|The ID of the price object.|
|» price_data|body|object|false|Data used to generate a new [Price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices) object inline.|
|» » currency|body|string(currency)|true|none|
|» » product|body|string|true|none|
|» » recurring|body|object|true|none|
|» » » interval|body|string|true|none|
|» » » interval_count|body|integer|false|none|
|» » tax_behavior|body|string|false|none|
|» » unit_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » unit_amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|none|
|» proration_behavior|body|string|false|Determines how to handle [prorations](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/prorations) when the billing cycle changes (e.g., when switching plans, resetting `billing_cycle_anchor=now`, or starting a trial), or if an item's `quantity` changes. The default value is `create_prorations`.|
|» proration_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|If set, the proration will be calculated as though the subscription was updated at the given time. This can be used to apply the same proration that was previewed with the [upcoming invoice](/api/invoices/create_preview) endpoint.|
|» quantity|body|integer|false|The quantity you'd like to apply to the subscription item you're creating.|
|» subscription|body|string|true|The identifier of the subscription to modify.|
|» tax_rates|body|[string] \| string|false|A list of [Tax Rate](https://docs.stripe.com/api/tax_rates) ids. These Tax Rates will override the [`default_tax_rates`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/create#create_subscription-default_tax_rates) on the Subscription. When updating, pass an empty string to remove previously-defined tax rates.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

## Delete a subscription item

<a id="opIdDeleteSubscriptionItemsItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/subscription_items/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'clear_usage=true&payment_behavior=allow_incomplete&proration_behavior=always_invoice&proration_date=0'
```

`DELETE /v1/subscription_items/{item}`

<p>Deletes an item from the subscription. Removing a subscription item from a subscription will not cancel the subscription.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
clear_usage: true
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
proration_behavior: always_invoice
proration_date: 0
```

<h3 id="delete-a-subscription-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|item|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» clear_usage|body|boolean|false|Delete all usage for the given subscription item. Allowed only when the current plan's `usage_type` is `metered`.|
|» payment_behavior|body|string|false|Controls how Stripe handles payment when a subscription update requires payment and `collection_method=charge_automatically`.|
|» proration_behavior|body|string|false|Determines how to handle [prorations](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/prorations) when the billing cycle changes (e.g., when switching plans, resetting `billing_cycle_anchor=now`, or starting a trial), or if an item's `quantity` changes. The default value is `create_prorations`.|
|» proration_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|If set, the proration will be calculated as though the subscription was updated at the given time. This can be used to apply the same proration that was previewed with the [upcoming invoice](/api/invoices/create_preview) endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» payment_behavior|allow_incomplete|
|» payment_behavior|default_incomplete|
|» payment_behavior|error_if_incomplete|
|» payment_behavior|pending_if_incomplete|
|» proration_behavior|always_invoice|
|» proration_behavior|create_prorations|
|» proration_behavior|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "deleted": true,
  "id": "string",
  "object": "subscription_item"
}
```

> default Response

{
  "error": {
    "advice_code": "string",
    "charge": "string",
    "code": "string",
    "decline_code": "string",
    "doc_url": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "network_advice_code": "string",
    "network_decline_code": "string",
    "param": "string",
    "payment_intent": {},
    "payment_method": {},
    "payment_method_type": "string",
    "request_log_url": "string",
    "setup_intent": {},
    "source": {},
    "type": "api_error"
  }
}
```

## Retrieve a schedule

<a id="opIdGetSubscriptionSchedulesSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/subscription_schedules/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /v1/subscription_schedules/{schedule}`

<p>Updates an existing subscription schedule.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
default_settings:
  application_fee_percent: 0
  automatic_tax:
    enabled: true
    liability:
      account: string
      type: account
  billing_cycle_anchor: automatic
  billing_thresholds:
    amount_gte: 0
    reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
  collection_method: charge_automatically
  default_payment_method: string
  description: string
  invoice_settings:
    account_tax_ids:
      - string
    custom_fields:
      -
        name: string
        value: string
    days_until_due: 0
    description: string
    footer: string
    issuer:
      account: string
      type: account
  on_behalf_of: string
  transfer_data:
    amount_percent: 0
    destination: string
end_behavior: cancel
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
pause_schedules:
  -
    key: string
    pause:
      pause_at:
        timestamp: 0
        type: now
      settings:
        bill_for:
          outstanding_usage_through:
            type: none
          unused_time_from:
            type: item_current_period_start
        invoicing_behavior: invoice
        type: subscription
    resume:
      resume_at:
        duration:
          interval: day
          interval_count: 0
        timestamp: 0
        type: duration
      settings:
        billing_cycle_anchor: resume_at
        payment_behavior: resume_on_payment_attempt
        proration_behavior: always_invoice
phases:
  -
    add_invoice_items:
      -
        discountable: true
        discounts:
          -
            coupon: string
            discount: string
            promotion_code: string
        metadata:
          property1: string
          property2: string
        period:
          end:
            timestamp: 0
            type: min_item_period_end
          start:
            timestamp: 0
            type: max_item_period_start
        price: string
        price_data:
          currency: string
          product: string
          tax_behavior: exclusive
          unit_amount: 0
          unit_amount_decimal: string
        quantity: 0
        tax_rates:
          - string
    application_fee_percent: 0
    automatic_tax:
      enabled: true
      liability:
        account: string
        type: account
    billing_cycle_anchor: automatic
    billing_thresholds:
      amount_gte: 0
      reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
    collection_method: charge_automatically
    default_payment_method: string
    default_tax_rates:
      - string
    description: string
    discounts:
      -
        coupon: string
        discount: string
        promotion_code: string
    duration:
      interval: day
      interval_count: 0
    end_date: 0
    invoice_settings:
      account_tax_ids:
        - string
      custom_fields:
        -
          name: string
          value: string
      days_until_due: 0
      description: string
      footer: string
      issuer:
        account: string
        type: account
    items:
      -
        billing_thresholds:
          usage_gte: 0
        discounts:
          -
            coupon: string
            discount: string
            promotion_code: string
        metadata:
          property1: string
          property2: string
        price: string
        price_data:
          currency: string
          product: string
          recurring:
            interval: day
            interval_count: 0
          tax_behavior: exclusive
          unit_amount: 0
          unit_amount_decimal: string
        quantity: 0
        tax_rates:
          - string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    on_behalf_of: string
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
    start_date: 0
    transfer_data:
      amount_percent: 0
      destination: string
    trial: true
    trial_end: 0
proration_behavior: always_invoice
```

## Cancel a schedule

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionSchedulesScheduleCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/subscription_schedules/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice_now=true&prorate=true'
```

`POST /v1/subscription_schedules/{schedule}/cancel`

<p>Cancels a subscription schedule and its associated subscription immediately (if the subscription schedule has an active subscription). A subscription schedule can only be canceled if its status is <code>not_started</code> or <code>active</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
invoice_now: true
prorate: true
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|schedule|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» invoice_now|body|boolean|false|If the subscription schedule is `active`, indicates if a final invoice will be generated that contains any un-invoiced metered usage and new/pending proration invoice items. Defaults to `true`.|
|» prorate|body|boolean|false|If the subscription schedule is `active`, indicates if the cancellation should be prorated. Defaults to `true`.|

## Release a schedule

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionSchedulesScheduleRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/subscription_schedules/string/release \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&preserve_cancel_date=true'
```

`POST /v1/subscription_schedules/{schedule}/release`

<p>Releases the subscription schedule immediately, which will stop scheduling of its phases, but leave any existing subscription in place. A schedule can only be released if its status is <code>not_started</code> or <code>active</code>. If the subscription schedule is currently associated with a subscription, releasing it will remove its <code>subscription</code> property and set the subscription’s ID to the <code>released_subscription</code> property.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
preserve_cancel_date: true
```

<h3 id="release-a-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|schedule|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» preserve_cancel_date|body|boolean|false|Keep any cancellation on the subscription that the schedule has set|

## List subscriptions

<a id="opIdGetSubscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/subscriptions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/subscriptions`

<p>By default, returns a list of subscriptions that have not been canceled. In order to list canceled subscriptions, specify <code>status=canceled</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automatic_tax|query|object|false|Filter subscriptions by their automatic tax settings.|
|collection_method|query|string|false|The collection method of the subscriptions to retrieve. Either `charge_automatically` or `send_invoice`.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return subscriptions that were created during the given date interval.|
|current_period_end|query|object \| integer|false|Only return subscriptions whose minimum item current_period_end falls within the given date interval.|
|current_period_start|query|object \| integer|false|Only return subscriptions whose maximum item current_period_start falls within the given date interval.|
|customer|query|string|false|The ID of the customer whose subscriptions you're retrieving.|
|customer_account|query|string|false|The ID of the account representing the customer whose subscriptions you're retrieving.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|price|query|string|false|Filter for subscriptions that contain this recurring price ID.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the subscriptions to retrieve. Passing in a value of `canceled` will return all canceled subscriptions, including those belonging to deleted customers. Pass `ended` to find subscriptions that are canceled and subscriptions that are expired due to [incomplete payment](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview#subscription-statuses). Passing in a value of `all` will return subscriptions of all statuses. If no value is supplied, all subscriptions that have not been canceled are returned.|
|test_clock|query|string|false|Filter for subscriptions that are associated with the specified test clock. The response will not include subscriptions with test clocks if this and the customer parameter is not set.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|collection_method|charge_automatically|
|collection_method|send_invoice|
|status|active|
|status|all|
|status|canceled|
|status|ended|
|status|incomplete|
|status|incomplete_expired|
|status|past_due|
|status|paused|
|status|trialing|
|status|unpaid|

|Property|Value|

`POST /v1/subscriptions`

<p>Creates a new subscription on an existing customer. Each customer can have up to 500 active or scheduled subscriptions.</p>

<p>When you create a subscription with <code>collection_method=charge_automatically</code>, the first invoice is finalized as part of the request.
The <code>payment_behavior</code> parameter determines the exact behavior of the initial payment.</p>

<p>To start subscriptions where the first invoice always begins in a <code>draft</code> status, use <a href="/docs/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules#managing">subscription schedules</a> instead.
Schedules provide the flexibility to model more complex billing configurations that change over time.</p>

## Search subscriptions

<a id="opIdGetSubscriptionsSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.stripe.com/v1/subscriptions/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/subscriptions/search`

<p>Search for subscriptions you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="search-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://docs.stripe.com/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/search#query-fields-for-subscriptions).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
