## Simulate a successful input collection

<a id="opIdPostTestHelpersTerminalReadersReaderSucceedInputCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/test_helpers/terminal/readers/string/succeed_input_collection \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&skip_non_required_inputs=all'
```

`POST /v1/test_helpers/terminal/readers/{reader}/succeed_input_collection`

<p>Use this endpoint to trigger a successful input collection on a simulated reader.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
skip_non_required_inputs: all
```

<h3 id="simulate-a-successful-input-collection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reader|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» skip_non_required_inputs|body|string|false|This parameter defines the skip behavior for input collection.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» skip_non_required_inputs|all|
|» skip_non_required_inputs|none|

## List all test clocks

<a id="opIdGetTestHelpersTestClocks"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/test_helpers/test_clocks \

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/test_helpers/test_clocks`

<p>Returns a list of your test clocks.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-test-clocks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

## Create a test clock

<a id="opIdPostTestHelpersTestClocks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/test_helpers/test_clocks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'customer=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&frozen_time=0&name=string'
```

`POST /v1/test_helpers/test_clocks`

<p>Creates a new test clock that can be attached to new customers and quotes.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
customer: string
expand:
  - string
frozen_time: 0
name: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-test-clock-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» customer|body|string|false|Existing customer this test clock will be attached to. Once attached, customers can't be removed from a test clock.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» frozen_time|body|integer(unix-time)|true|The initial frozen time for this test clock.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name for this test clock.|

> Example responses

```json
  "created": 0,
```

## Advance a test clock

<a id="opIdPostTestHelpersTestClocksTestClockAdvance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/test_helpers/test_clocks/string/advance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&frozen_time=0'
```

`POST /v1/test_helpers/test_clocks/{test_clock}/advance`

<p>Starts advancing a test clock to a specified time in the future. Advancement is done when status changes to <code>Ready</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
frozen_time: 0
```

<h3 id="advance-a-test-clock-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|test_clock|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» frozen_time|body|integer(unix-time)|true|The time to advance the test clock. Must be after the test clock's current frozen time. Cannot be more than two intervals in the future from the shortest subscription in this test clock. If there are no subscriptions in this test clock, it cannot be more than two years in the future.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "deletes_after": 0,
  "frozen_time": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "name": "string",
  "object": "test_helpers.test_clock",
  "status": "advancing",
  "status_details": {
    "advancing": {
      "target_frozen_time": 0
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
  -X POST \
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&financial_account=string&initiating_payment_method_details=%7B%22type%22%3A%22us_bank_account%22%2C%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22account_holder_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D&network=ach'
```

`POST /v1/test_helpers/treasury/received_credits`

<p>Use this endpoint to simulate a test mode ReceivedCredit initiated by a third party. In live mode, you can’t directly create ReceivedCredits initiated by third parties.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
expand:
  - string
financial_account: string
initiating_payment_method_details:
  type: us_bank_account
  us_bank_account:
    account_holder_name: string
    account_number: string
    routing_number: string
network: ach
```

<h3 id="test-mode-create-a-receivedcredit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to be transferred.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» financial_account|body|string|true|The FinancialAccount to send funds to.|
|» initiating_payment_method_details|body|object|false|Initiating payment method details for the object.|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » us_bank_account|body|object|false|none|
|» » » account_holder_name|body|string|false|none|
|» » » account_number|body|string|false|none|
|» » » routing_number|body|string|false|none|
|» network|body|string|true|Specifies the network rails to be used. If not set, will default to the PaymentMethod's preferred network. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type.|

`POST /v1/test_helpers/treasury/received_debits`

## Cancel a 3DS Authentication

<a id="opIdPostThreeDSecureAuthenticationsAuthenticationCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/three_d_secure/authentications/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/three_d_secure/authentications/{authentication}/cancel`

<p>This endpoint cancels a 3DS Authentication. You can cancel a 3DS Authentication object when it’s in a non-final status:
<code>requires_submission</code> or <code>requires_challenge</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

`POST /v1/tokens`

<p>Creates a single-use token that represents a bank account’s details.
You can use this token with any v1 API method in place of a bank account dictionary. You can only use this token once. To do so, attach it to a <a href="#accounts">connected account</a> where <a href="/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection">controller.requirement_collection</a> is <code>application</code>, which includes Custom accounts.</p>

## List all top-ups

<a id="opIdGetTopups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/topups \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/topups`

<p>Returns a list of top-ups.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-top-ups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|query|object \| integer|false|A positive integer representing how much to transfer.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|A filter on the list, based on the object `created` field. The value can be a string with an integer Unix timestamp, or it can be a dictionary with a number of different query options.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return top-ups that have the given status. One of `canceled`, `failed`, `pending` or `succeeded`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|canceled|
|status|failed|
|status|pending|
|status|succeeded|

|---|---|

## Create a top-up

<a id="opIdPostTopups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/topups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_method=string&payment_method_options=%7B%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22network%22%3A%22ach%22%7D%7D&source=string&statement_descriptor=string&transfer_group=string'
```

`POST /v1/topups`

<p>Top up the balance of an account</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_method: string
payment_method_options:
  us_bank_account:
    network: ach
source: string
statement_descriptor: string
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-top-up-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|A positive integer representing how much to transfer.|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» payment_method|body|string|false|The ID of a PaymentMethod representing the payment method to be used for the top-up. A PaymentMethod of type `us_bank_account` can be used.|
|» payment_method_options|body|object|false|Payment method-specific configuration for this top-up.|
|» » us_bank_account|body|object|false|none|
|» » » network|body|string|true|none|
|» source|body|string|false|The ID of a source to transfer funds from. For most users, this should be left unspecified which will use the bank account that was set up in the dashboard for the specified currency. While testing, this can be a test bank token (see [Testing Top-ups](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing#testing-top-ups)).|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|Extra information about a top-up for the source's bank statement. Limited to 15 ASCII characters.|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this top-up as part of a group.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|
|» » » network|ach|

## Update a top-up

<a id="opIdPostTopupsTopup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/topups/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/topups/{topup}`

<p>Updates the metadata of a top-up. Other top-up details are not editable by design.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
description: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

<h3 id="update-a-top-up-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|topup|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

## Cancel a top-up

<a id="opIdPostTopupsTopupCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/topups/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/topups/{topup}/cancel`

<p>Cancels a top-up. Only pending top-ups can be canceled.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

## List all transfers

<a id="opIdGetTransfers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/transfers \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/transfers`

<p>Returns a list of existing transfers sent to connected accounts. The transfers are returned in sorted order, with the most recently created transfers appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="list-all-transfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return transfers that were created during the given date interval.|
|destination|query|string|false|Only return transfers for the destination specified by this account ID.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|transfer_group|query|string|false|Only return transfers with the specified transfer group.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Create a transfer

<a id="opIdPostTransfers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/transfers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&destination=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&source_transaction=string&source_type=bank_account&transfer_group=string'
```

`POST /v1/transfers`

<p>To send funds from your Stripe account to a connected account, you create a new transfer object. Your <a href="#balance">Stripe balance</a> must be able to cover the transfer amount, or you’ll receive an “Insufficient Funds” error.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
destination: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
source_transaction: string
source_type: bank_account
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) representing how much to transfer.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|true|Three-letter [ISO code for currency](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination|body|string|true|The ID of a connected Stripe account. <a href="/docs/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers">See the Connect documentation</a> for details.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» source_transaction|body|string|false|You can use this parameter to transfer funds from a charge before they are added to your available balance. A pending balance will transfer immediately but the funds will not become available until the original charge becomes available. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-availability) for details.|
|» source_type|body|string|false|The source balance to use for this transfer. One of `bank_account`, `card`, or `fpx`. For most users, this will default to `card`.|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» source_type|bank_account|
|» source_type|card|
|» source_type|fpx|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "amount_reversed": 0,

  "currency": "string",

    "data": [
      {}
    ],

    "url": "string"
  },
  "reversed": true,

  "source_type": "string",
  "transfer_group": "string"
}
```

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|

## Create a transfer reversal

<a id="opIdPostTransfersIdReversals"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/transfers/string/reversals \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&refund_application_fee=true'
```

`POST /v1/transfers/{id}/reversals`

<p>When you create a new reversal, you must specify a transfer to create it on.</p>

<p>When reversing transfers, you can optionally reverse part of the transfer. You can do so as many times as you wish until the entire transfer has been reversed.</p>

<p>Once entirely reversed, a transfer can’t be reversed again. This method will return an error when called on an already-reversed transfer, or when trying to reverse more money than is left on a transfer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
description: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
refund_application_fee: true
```

<h3 id="create-a-transfer-reversal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) representing how much of this transfer to reverse. Can only reverse up to the unreversed amount remaining of the transfer. Partial transfer reversals are only allowed for transfers to Stripe Accounts. Defaults to the entire transfer amount.|

|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» refund_application_fee|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when reversing this transfer. If a full transfer reversal is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded with an amount proportional to the amount of the transfer reversed.|

```yaml
  - string
```
```yaml
features:
```

```yaml
  payment_method: string

metadata:

nickname: string
platform_restrictions:
  inbound_flows: restricted
  outbound_flows: restricted
```

## Close a FinancialAccount

<a id="opIdPostTreasuryFinancialAccountsFinancialAccountClose"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/treasury/financial_accounts/string/close \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&forwarding_settings=%7B%22financial_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22payment_method%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22financial_account%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/treasury/financial_accounts/{financial_account}/close`

<p>Closes a FinancialAccount. A FinancialAccount can only be closed if it has a zero balance, has no pending InboundTransfers, and has canceled all attached Issuing cards.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
forwarding_settings:
  financial_account: string
  payment_method: string
  type: financial_account
```

|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» origin_payment_method|body|string|true|The origin payment method to be debited for the InboundTransfer.|

## Create an OutboundPayment

<a id="opIdPostTreasuryOutboundPayments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/treasury/outbound_payments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&customer=string&description=string&destination_payment_method=string&destination_payment_method_data=%7B%22billing_details%22%3A%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22financial_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22type%22%3A%22financial_account%22%2C%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_type%22%3A%22checking%22%2C%22financial_connections_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D&destination_payment_method_options=%7B%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22network%22%3A%22ach%22%7D%7D&end_user_details=%7B%22ip_address%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22present%22%3Atrue%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&financial_account=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&statement_descriptor=string'
```

`POST /v1/treasury/outbound_payments`

<p>Creates an OutboundPayment.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
customer: string
description: string
destination_payment_method: string
destination_payment_method_data:
  billing_details:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    email: string
    name: string
    phone: string
  financial_account: string
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  type: financial_account
  us_bank_account:
    account_holder_type: company
    account_number: string
    account_type: checking
    financial_connections_account: string
    routing_number: string
destination_payment_method_options:
  us_bank_account:
    network: ach
end_user_details:
  ip_address: string
  present: true
expand:
  - string
financial_account: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
statement_descriptor: string
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to be transferred.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the customer to whom the OutboundPayment is sent. Must match the Customer attached to the `destination_payment_method` passed in.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination_payment_method|body|string|false|The PaymentMethod to use as the payment instrument for the OutboundPayment. Exclusive with `destination_payment_method_data`.|

## Create an OutboundTransfer

<a id="opIdPostTreasuryOutboundTransfers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/treasury/outbound_transfers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&destination_payment_method=string&destination_payment_method_data=%7B%22financial_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22financial_account%22%7D&destination_payment_method_options=%7B%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22network%22%3A%22ach%22%7D%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&financial_account=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&statement_descriptor=string'
```

`POST /v1/treasury/outbound_transfers`

<p>Creates an OutboundTransfer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
destination_payment_method: string
destination_payment_method_data:
  financial_account: string
  type: financial_account
destination_payment_method_options:
  us_bank_account:
    network: ach
expand:
  - string
financial_account: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
statement_descriptor: string
```

<h3 id="create-an-outboundtransfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to be transferred.|
|» currency|body|string(currency)|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination_payment_method|body|string|false|The PaymentMethod to use as the payment instrument for the OutboundTransfer.|
|» destination_payment_method_data|body|object|false|Hash used to generate the PaymentMethod to be used for this OutboundTransfer. Exclusive with `destination_payment_method`.|
|» » financial_account|body|string|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» destination_payment_method_options|body|object|false|Hash describing payment method configuration details.|
|» » us_bank_account|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » network|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» financial_account|body|string|true|The FinancialAccount to pull funds from.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|Statement descriptor to be shown on the receiving end of an OutboundTransfer. Maximum 10 characters for `ach` transfers or 140 characters for `us_domestic_wire` transfers. The default value is "transfer". Can only include -#.$&*, spaces, and alphanumeric characters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|financial_account|
|» » » network|ach|
|» » » network|us_domestic_wire|
|» » » *anyOf*|""|

## Create a webhook endpoint

<a id="opIdPostWebhookEndpoints"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/webhook_endpoints \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'api_version=2011-01-01&connect=true&description=string&enabled_events=%5B%22*%22%5D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&url=string'
```

`POST /v1/webhook_endpoints`

<p>A webhook endpoint must have a <code>url</code> and a list of <code>enabled_events</code>. You may optionally specify the Boolean <code>connect</code> parameter. If set to true, then a Connect webhook endpoint that notifies the specified <code>url</code> about events from all connected accounts is created; otherwise an account webhook endpoint that notifies the specified <code>url</code> only about events from your account is created. You can also create webhook endpoints in the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/webhooks">webhooks settings</a> section of the Dashboard.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
api_version: "2011-01-01"
connect: true
description: string
enabled_events:
  - "*"
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
url: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-webhook-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» api_version|body|string|false|Events sent to this endpoint will be generated with this Stripe Version instead of your account's default Stripe Version.|
|» connect|body|boolean|false|Whether this endpoint should receive events from connected accounts (`true`), or from your account (`false`). Defaults to `false`.|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional description of what the webhook is used for.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» enabled_events|body|[string]|true|The list of events to enable for this endpoint. You may specify `['*']` to enable all events, except those that require explicit selection.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL of the webhook endpoint.|

## Retrieve a webhook endpoint

<a id="opIdGetWebhookEndpointsWebhookEndpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/webhook_endpoints/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

## Update a webhook endpoint

<a id="opIdPostWebhookEndpointsWebhookEndpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/webhook_endpoints/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'description=string&disabled=true&enabled_events=%5B%22*%22%5D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&url=string'
```

`POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{webhook_endpoint}`

<p>Updates the webhook endpoint. You may edit the <code>url</code>, the list of <code>enabled_events</code>, and the status of your endpoint.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
description: string
disabled: true
enabled_events:
  - "*"
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
url: string
```

<h3 id="update-a-webhook-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook_endpoint|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional description of what the webhook is used for.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» disabled|body|boolean|false|Disable the webhook endpoint if set to true.|
|» enabled_events|body|[string]|false|The list of events to enable for this endpoint. You may specify `['*']` to enable all events, except those that require explicit selection.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» url|body|string|false|The URL of the webhook endpoint.|

|» enabled_events|treasury.received_debit.created|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

For new integrations, we recommend using the [Accounts v2 API](/api/v2/core/accounts), in place of /v1/accounts and /v1/customers to represent a user.

This is an object representing a Stripe account. You can retrieve it to see
properties on the account like its current requirements or if the account is
enabled to make live charges or receive payouts.

For accounts where [controller.requirement_collection](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection)
is `application`, which includes Custom accounts, the properties below are always
returned.

For accounts where [controller.requirement_collection](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection)
is `stripe`, which includes Standard and Express accounts, some properties are only returned
until you create an [Account Link](/api/account_links) or [Account Session](/api/account_sessions)
to start Connect Onboarding. Learn about the [differences between accounts](/connect/accounts).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|business_profile|[account_business_profile](#schemaaccount_business_profile) \| null|false|none|Business information about the account.|
|business_type|string \| null|false|none|The business type.|
|capabilities|[account_capabilities](#schemaaccount_capabilities)|false|none|none|
|charges_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the account can process charges.|
|company|[legal_entity_company](#schemalegal_entity_company)|false|none|none|
|controller|[account_unification_account_controller](#schemaaccount_unification_account_controller)|false|none|none|
|country|string|false|none|The account's country.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Time at which the account was connected. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|default_currency|string|false|none|Three-letter ISO currency code representing the default currency for the account. This must be a currency that [Stripe supports in the account's country](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts).|
|details_submitted|boolean|false|none|Whether account details have been submitted. Accounts with Stripe Dashboard access, which includes Standard accounts, cannot receive payouts before this is true. Accounts where this is false should be directed to [an onboarding flow](/connect/onboarding) to finish submitting account details.|
|email|string \| null|false|none|An email address associated with the account. It's not used for authentication and Stripe doesn't market to this field without explicit approval from the platform.|
|external_accounts|object|false|none|External accounts (bank accounts and debit cards) currently attached to this account. External accounts are only returned for requests where `controller[is_controller]` is true.|
|future_requirements|[account_future_requirements](#schemaaccount_future_requirements)|false|none|none|
|groups|[account_group_membership](#schemaaccount_group_membership) \| null|false|none|The groups associated with the account.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|individual|[person](#schemaperson)|false|none|This is an object representing a person associated with a Stripe account.<br><br>A platform can only access a subset of data in a person for an account where [account.controller.requirement_collection](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection) is `stripe`, which includes Standard and Express accounts, after creating an Account Link or Account Session to start Connect onboarding.<br><br>See the [Standard onboarding](/connect/standard-accounts) or [Express onboarding](/connect/express-accounts) documentation for information about prefilling information and account onboarding steps. Learn more about [handling identity verification with the API](/connect/handling-api-verification#person-information).|
|metadata|object|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payouts_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the funds in this account can be paid out.|
|requirements|[account_requirements](#schemaaccount_requirements)|false|none|none|
|settings|[account_settings](#schemaaccount_settings) \| null|false|none|Options for customizing how the account functions within Stripe.|
|tos_acceptance|[account_tos_acceptance](#schemaaccount_tos_acceptance)|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|The Stripe account type. Can be `standard`, `express`, `custom`, or `none`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|business_type|company|
|business_type|government_entity|
|business_type|individual|
|business_type|non_profit|
|object|account|
|type|custom|
|type|express|
|type|none|
|type|standard|

<a id="schema_account_annual_revenue"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "fiscal_year_end": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|A non-negative integer representing the amount in the [smallest currency unit](/currencies#zero-decimal).|
|currency|string(currency) \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|fiscal_year_end|string \| null|false|none|The close-out date of the preceding fiscal year in ISO 8601 format. E.g. 2023-12-31 for the 31st of December, 2023.|

<h2 id="tocS_account_bacs_debit_payments_settings">account_bacs_debit_payments_settings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount_bacs_debit_payments_settings"></a>
<a id="schema_account_bacs_debit_payments_settings"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount_bacs_debit_payments_settings"></a>
<a id="tocsaccount_bacs_debit_payments_settings"></a>

```json
{
  "display_name": "string",
  "service_user_number": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|display_name|string \| null|false|none|The Bacs Direct Debit display name for this account. For payments made with Bacs Direct Debit, this name appears on the mandate as the statement descriptor. Mobile banking apps display it as the name of the business. To use custom branding, set the Bacs Direct Debit Display Name during or right after creation. Custom branding incurs an additional monthly fee for the platform. The fee appears 5 business days after requesting Bacs. If you don't set the display name before requesting Bacs capability, it's automatically set as "Stripe" and the account is onboarded to Stripe branding, which is free.|
|service_user_number|string \| null|false|none|The Bacs Direct Debit Service user number for this account. For payments made with Bacs Direct Debit, this number is a unique identifier of the account with our banking partners.|

<h2 id="tocS_account_branding_settings">account_branding_settings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount_branding_settings"></a>
<a id="schema_account_branding_settings"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount_branding_settings"></a>
<a id="tocsaccount_branding_settings"></a>

```json
{
  "icon": "string",
  "logo": "string",
  "primary_color": "string",
  "secondary_color": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|icon|string \| [file](#schemafile) \| null|false|none|(ID of a [file upload](https://stripe.com/docs/guides/file-upload)) An icon for the account. Must be square and at least 128px x 128px.|
|logo|string \| [file](#schemafile) \| null|false|none|(ID of a [file upload](https://stripe.com/docs/guides/file-upload)) A logo for the account that will be used in Checkout instead of the icon and without the account's name next to it if provided. Must be at least 128px x 128px.|
|primary_color|string \| null|false|none|A CSS hex color value representing the primary branding color for this account|
|secondary_color|string \| null|false|none|A CSS hex color value representing the secondary branding color for this account|

```json
  },

  ],
  "monthly_estimated_revenue": {
    "amount": 0,

  },
  "name": "string",
  "product_description": "string",
  "specified_commercial_transactions_act_url": "string",
  "support_address": {
    "city": "string",
    "country": "string",
    "line1": "string",
    "line2": "string",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "state": "string"
  },
  "support_email": "string",
  "support_phone": "string",
  "support_url": "string",
  "url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|annual_revenue|[account_annual_revenue](#schemaaccount_annual_revenue) \| null|false|none|The applicant's gross annual revenue for its preceding fiscal year.|
|estimated_worker_count|integer \| null|false|none|An estimated upper bound of employees, contractors, vendors, etc. currently working for the business.|
|mcc|string \| null|false|none|[The merchant category code for the account](/connect/setting-mcc). MCCs are used to classify businesses based on the goods or services they provide.|
|minority_owned_business_designation|[string]|false|none|Whether the business is a minority-owned, women-owned, and/or LGBTQI+ -owned business.|
|monthly_estimated_revenue|[account_monthly_estimated_revenue](#schemaaccount_monthly_estimated_revenue)|false|none|none|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The customer-facing business name.|
|product_description|string \| null|false|none|Internal-only description of the product sold or service provided by the business. It's used by Stripe for risk and underwriting purposes.|
|specified_commercial_transactions_act_url|string \| null|false|none|A link to the business's publicly available terms related to the Specified Commercial Transaction Act. Only used for accounts in Japan.|
|support_address|[address](#schemaaddress) \| null|false|none|A publicly available mailing address for sending support issues to.|
|support_email|string \| null|false|none|A publicly available email address for sending support issues to.|
|support_phone|string \| null|false|none|A publicly available phone number to call with support issues.|
|support_url|string \| null|false|none|A publicly available website for handling support issues.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|The business's publicly available website.|

|minority_owned_business_designation|prefer_not_to_answer|
|minority_owned_business_designation|women_owned_business|

<h2 id="tocS_account_capability_future_requirements">account_capability_future_requirements</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount_capability_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="schema_account_capability_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount_capability_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="tocsaccount_capability_future_requirements"></a>

```json
{
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "alternative_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ],
      "original_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "current_deadline": 0,
  "currently_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "disabled_reason": "other",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "external_request",
      "reason": "string",
      "requirement": "string"
    }
  ],
  "eventually_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "past_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "pending_verification": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be resolved by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead. Multiple alternatives can reference the same `original_fields_due`. When this happens, any of these alternatives can serve as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields. Additionally, providing `original_fields_due` again also serves as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields.|
|current_deadline|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date on which `future_requirements` becomes the main `requirements` hash and `future_requirements` becomes empty. After the transition, `currently_due` requirements may immediately become `past_due`, but the account may also be given a grace period depending on the capability's enablement state prior to transitioning.|
|currently_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that need to be resolved to keep the capability enabled. If not resolved by `future_requirements[current_deadline]`, these fields will transition to the main `requirements` hash.|
|disabled_reason|string \| null|false|none|This is typed as an enum for consistency with `requirements.disabled_reason`, but it safe to assume `future_requirements.disabled_reason` is null because fields in `future_requirements` will never disable the account.|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|true|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|true|none|Fields you must collect when all thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well.|
|past_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that haven't been resolved by `requirements.current_deadline`. These fields need to be resolved to enable the capability on the account. `future_requirements.past_due` is a subset of `requirements.past_due`.|
|pending_verification|[string]|true|none|Fields that are being reviewed, or might become required depending on the results of a review. If the review fails, these fields can move to `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives`. Fields might appear in `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives` and in `pending_verification` if one verification fails but another is still pending.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|disabled_reason|other|
|disabled_reason|paused.inactivity|
|disabled_reason|pending.onboarding|
|disabled_reason|pending.review|
|disabled_reason|platform_disabled|
|disabled_reason|platform_paused|
|disabled_reason|rejected.inactivity|
|disabled_reason|rejected.other|
|disabled_reason|rejected.unsupported_business|
|disabled_reason|requirements.fields_needed|

```json
{
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "alternative_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ],
      "original_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "current_deadline": 0,
  "currently_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "disabled_reason": "other",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "external_request",
      "reason": "string",
      "requirement": "string"
    }
  ],
  "eventually_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "past_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "pending_verification": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be resolved by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead. Multiple alternatives can reference the same `original_fields_due`. When this happens, any of these alternatives can serve as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields. Additionally, providing `original_fields_due` again also serves as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields.|
|current_deadline|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The date by which all required account information must be both submitted and verified. This includes fields listed in `currently_due` as well as those in `pending_verification`. If any required information is missing or unverified by this date, the account may be disabled. Note that `current_deadline` may change if additional `currently_due` requirements are requested.|
|currently_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that need to be resolved to keep the capability enabled. If not resolved by `current_deadline`, these fields will appear in `past_due` as well, and the capability is disabled.|
|disabled_reason|string \| null|false|none|Description of why the capability is disabled. [Learn more about handling verification issues](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/handling-api-verification).|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|true|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|true|none|Fields you must collect when all thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well, and `current_deadline` becomes set.|
|past_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that haven't been resolved by `current_deadline`. These fields need to be resolved to enable the capability on the account.|
|pending_verification|[string]|true|none|Fields that are being reviewed, or might become required depending on the results of a review. If the review fails, these fields can move to `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives`. Fields might appear in `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives` and in `pending_verification` if one verification fails but another is still pending.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be resolved by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead. Many alternatives can list the same `original_fields_due`, and any of these alternatives can serve as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields again. Re-providing `original_fields_due` also serves as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields again.|
|current_deadline|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date by which the fields in `currently_due` must be collected to keep the account enabled. These fields may disable the account sooner if the next threshold is reached before they are collected.|
|currently_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that need to be resolved to keep the account enabled. If not resolved by `current_deadline`, these fields will appear in `past_due` as well, and the account will be disabled.|
|disabled_reason|string \| null|false|none|If the account is disabled, this enum describes why. [Learn more about handling verification issues](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/handling-api-verification).|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|false|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|false|none|Fields you must collect when all thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well, and `current_deadline` becomes set.|
|past_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that haven't been resolved by `current_deadline`. These fields need to be resolved to enable the account.|
|pending_verification|[string]|false|none|Fields that are being reviewed, or might become required depending on the results of a review. If the review fails, these fields can move to `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives`. Fields might appear in `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives` and in `pending_verification` if one verification fails but another is still pending.|

An AccountSession allows a Connect platform to grant access to a connected account in Connect embedded components.

We recommend that you create an AccountSession each time you need to display an embedded component
to your user. Do not save AccountSessions to your database as they expire relatively
quickly, and cannot be used more than once.

Related guide: [Connect embedded components](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/get-started-connect-embedded-components)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|string|true|none|The ID of the account the AccountSession was created for|
|client_secret|string|true|none|The client secret of this AccountSession. Used on the client to set up secure access to the given `account`.<br><br>The client secret can be used to provide access to `account` from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the connected account. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret.<br><br>Refer to our docs to [setup Connect embedded components](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/get-started-connect-embedded-components) and learn about how `client_secret` should be handled.|
|components|[connect_embedded_account_session_create_components](#schemaconnect_embedded_account_session_create_components)|true|none|none|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The timestamp at which this AccountSession will expire.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|account_session|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|advice_code|string|false|none|For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating [how to proceed with an error](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/card#retrying-issuer-declines) if they provide one.|
|charge|string|false|none|For card errors, the ID of the failed charge.|
|code|string|false|none|For some errors that could be handled programmatically, a short string indicating the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.|
|decline_code|string|false|none|For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating the [card issuer's reason for the decline](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#issuer-declines) if they provide one.|
|doc_url|string|false|none|A URL to more information about the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.|
|message|string|false|none|A human-readable message providing more details about the error. For card errors, these messages can be shown to your users.|
|network_advice_code|string|false|none|For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice given to merchant by the card network on how to proceed with an error.|
|network_decline_code|string|false|none|For payments declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the payment failed.|
|param|string|false|none|If the error is parameter-specific, the parameter related to the error. For example, you can use this to display a message near the correct form field.|
|payment_intent|[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|false|none|A PaymentIntent guides you through the process of collecting a payment from your customer.<br>We recommend that you create exactly one PaymentIntent for each order or<br>customer session in your system. You can reference the PaymentIntent later to<br>see the history of payment attempts for a particular session.<br><br>A PaymentIntent transitions through<br>[multiple statuses](/payments/paymentintents/lifecycle)<br>throughout its lifetime as it interfaces with Stripe.js to perform<br>authentication flows and ultimately creates at most one successful charge.<br><br>Related guide: [Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents)|
|payment_method|[payment_method](#schemapayment_method)|false|none|PaymentMethod objects represent your customer's payment instruments.<br>You can use them with [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents) to collect payments or save them to<br>Customer objects to store instrument details for future payments.<br><br>Related guides: [Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods) and [More Payment Scenarios](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/more-payment-scenarios).|
|payment_method_type|string|false|none|If the error is specific to the type of payment method, the payment method type that had a problem. This field is only populated for invoice-related errors.|
|request_log_url|string|false|none|A URL to the request log entry in your dashboard.|
|setup_intent|[setup_intent](#schemasetup_intent)|false|none|A SetupIntent guides you through the process of setting up and saving a customer's payment credentials for future payments.<br>For example, you can use a SetupIntent to set up and save your customer's card without immediately collecting a payment.<br>Later, you can use [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intents) to drive the payment flow.<br><br>Create a SetupIntent when you're ready to collect your customer's payment credentials.<br>Don't maintain long-lived, unconfirmed SetupIntents because they might not be valid.<br>The SetupIntent transitions through multiple [statuses](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses) as it guides<br>you through the setup process.<br><br>Successful SetupIntents result in payment credentials that are optimized for future payments.<br>For example, cardholders in [certain regions](https://stripe.com/guides/strong-customer-authentication) might need to be run through<br>[Strong Customer Authentication](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication) during payment method collection<br>to streamline later [off-session payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/setup-intents).<br>If you use the SetupIntent with a [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#setup_intent_object-customer),<br>it automatically attaches the resulting payment method to that Customer after successful setup.<br>We recommend using SetupIntents or [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) on<br>PaymentIntents to save payment methods to prevent saving invalid or unoptimized payment methods.<br><br>By using SetupIntents, you can reduce friction for your customers, even as regulations change over time.<br><br>Related guide: [Setup Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/setup-intents)|
|source|[bank_account](#schemabank_account) \| [card](#schemacard) \| [source](#schemasource)|false|none|The [source object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources/object) for errors returned on a request involving a source.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of error returned. One of `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, or `invalid_request_error`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|api_error|
|type|card_error|
|type|idempotency_error|
|type|invalid_request_error|

```json
  ],

    "string"
```
```json
  ],
```

```json
}
```

An app install represents a Stripe App that is installed on an account. It reports the permissions,
content security policy entries, and endpoints that the installing account has authorized, along with any
that the app's latest version requests but the account has not authorized yet. Use the Install API to
install, reauthorize, and uninstall apps, and to check the state of existing installs.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|string|true|none|The ID of the account that the app install belongs to.|
|app|string|true|none|The ID of the app installed.|
|approval_required|boolean|true|none|Whether the installer must authorize pending permissions, content security policy entries, or endpoints. For private apps, `approval_required` stays `false`; creating or reauthorizing the install through the API installs the newest completed upload and grants its permissions.|
|auth_code|string \| null|false|none|The authorization code for an oauth app install.|
|channel|string|true|none|The distribution channel associated with the app install.|
|content_security_policy_granted|[app_service_resource_install_content_security_policy](#schemaapp_service_resource_install_content_security_policy)|true|none|none|
|content_security_policy_pending|[app_service_resource_install_content_security_policy](#schemaapp_service_resource_install_content_security_policy)|true|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|created_by|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the embedding platform that created the install, if applicable.|
|endpoints_granted|[string]|true|none|The endpoint URLs authorized by the installer.|
|endpoints_pending|[string]|true|none|The endpoint URLs requested by the latest app version that the installer has not authorized.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|permissions_granted|[string]|true|none|The permissions authorized by the installer.|
|permissions_pending|[string]|true|none|The permissions requested by the latest app version that the installer has not authorized.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the app install.|

|channel|private_test|

|channel|review|
|channel|testing|
|object|apps.install|

|status|installed|
|status|installing|
|status|uninstall_failed|
|status|uninstalling|

<h2 id="tocS_apps.secret">apps.secret</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapps.secret"></a>
<a id="schema_apps.secret"></a>
<a id="tocSapps.secret"></a>
<a id="tocsapps.secret"></a>

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "deleted": true,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "name": "string",
  "object": "apps.secret",
  "payload": "string",
  "scope": {
    "type": "account",
    "user": "string"
  }
}
```

Secret Store is an API that allows Stripe Apps developers to securely persist secrets for use by UI Extensions and app backends.

The primary resource in Secret Store is a `secret`. Other apps can't view secrets created by an app. Additionally, secrets are scoped to provide further permission control.

All Dashboard users and the app backend share `account` scoped secrets. Use the `account` scope for secrets that don't change per-user, like a third-party API key.

A `user` scoped secret is accessible by the app backend and one specific Dashboard user. Use the `user` scope for per-user secrets like per-user OAuth tokens, where different users might have different permissions.

Related guide: [Store data between page reloads](https://docs.stripe.com/stripe-apps/store-auth-data-custom-objects)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|deleted|boolean|false|none|If true, indicates that this secret has been deleted|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The Unix timestamp for the expiry time of the secret, after which the secret deletes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|name|string|true|none|A name for the secret that's unique within the scope.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payload|string \| null|false|none|The plaintext secret value to be stored.|
|scope|[secret_service_resource_scope](#schemasecret_service_resource_scope)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|apps.secret|

This is an object representing your Stripe balance. You can retrieve it to see
the balance currently on your Stripe account.

The top-level `available` and `pending` comprise your "payments balance."

Related guide: [Balances and settlement time](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/balances), [Understanding Connect account balances](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/account-balances)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|[[balance_amount](#schemabalance_amount)]|true|none|Available funds that you can transfer or pay out automatically by Stripe or explicitly through the [Transfers API](https://docs.stripe.com/api#transfers) or [Payouts API](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payouts). You can find the available balance for each currency and payment type in the `source_types` property.|
|connect_reserved|[[balance_amount](#schemabalance_amount)]|false|none|Funds held due to negative balances on connected accounts where [account.controller.requirement_collection](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection) is `application`, which includes Custom accounts. You can find the connect reserve balance for each currency and payment type in the `source_types` property.|
|instant_available|[[balance_amount_net](#schemabalance_amount_net)]|false|none|Funds that you can pay out using Instant Payouts.|
|issuing|[balance_detail](#schemabalance_detail)|false|none|none|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|pending|[[balance_amount](#schemabalance_amount)]|true|none|Funds that aren't available in the balance yet. You can find the pending balance for each currency and each payment type in the `source_types` property.|
|refund_and_dispute_prefunding|[balance_detail_ungated](#schemabalance_detail_ungated)|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|balance|

<h2 id="tocS_balance_transaction">balance_transaction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabalance_transaction"></a>
<a id="schema_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocSbalance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocsbalance_transaction"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "available_on": 0,
  "balance_type": "issuing",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "exchange_rate": 0,
  "fee": 0,
  "fee_details": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "application": "string",
      "currency": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "net": 0,
  "object": "balance_transaction",
  "reporting_category": "string",
  "source": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "type": "adjustment"
}
```

Balance transactions represent funds moving through your Stripe account.
Stripe creates them for every type of transaction that enters or leaves your Stripe account balance.

Related guide: [Balance transaction types](https://docs.stripe.com/reports/balance-transaction-types)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Gross amount of this transaction (in cents (or local equivalent)). A positive value represents funds charged to another party, and a negative value represents funds sent to another party.|
|available_on|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The date that the transaction's net funds become available in the Stripe balance.|
|balance_type|string|true|none|The balance that this transaction impacts.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|exchange_rate|number \| null|false|none|If applicable, this transaction uses an exchange rate. If money converts from currency A to currency B, then the `amount` in currency A, multiplied by the `exchange_rate`, equals the `amount` in currency B. For example, if you charge a customer 10.00 EUR, the PaymentIntent's `amount` is `1000` and `currency` is `eur`. If this converts to 12.34 USD in your Stripe account, the BalanceTransaction's `amount` is `1234`, its `currency` is `usd`, and the `exchange_rate` is `1.234`.|
|fee|integer|true|none|Fees (in cents (or local equivalent)) paid for this transaction. Represented as a positive integer when assessed.|
|fee_details|[[fee](#schemafee)]|true|none|Detailed breakdown of fees (in cents (or local equivalent)) paid for this transaction.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|net|integer|true|none|Net impact to a Stripe balance (in cents (or local equivalent)). A positive value represents incrementing a Stripe balance, and a negative value decrementing a Stripe balance. You can calculate the net impact of a transaction on a balance by `amount` - `fee`|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|reporting_category|string|true|none|Learn more about how [reporting categories](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/reporting-categories) can help you understand balance transactions from an accounting perspective.|
|source|string \| [application_fee](#schemaapplication_fee) \| [charge](#schemacharge) \| [connect_collection_transfer](#schemaconnect_collection_transfer) \| [customer_cash_balance_transaction](#schemacustomer_cash_balance_transaction) \| [dispute](#schemadispute) \| [fee_refund](#schemafee_refund) \| [issuing.authorization](#schemaissuing.authorization) \| [issuing.dispute](#schemaissuing.dispute) \| [issuing.transaction](#schemaissuing.transaction) \| [payout](#schemapayout) \| [refund](#schemarefund) \| [reserve_transaction](#schemareserve_transaction) \| [tax_deducted_at_source](#schematax_deducted_at_source) \| [topup](#schematopup) \| [transfer](#schematransfer) \| [transfer_reversal](#schematransfer_reversal) \| null|false|none|This transaction relates to the Stripe object.|
|status|string|true|none|The transaction's net funds status in the Stripe balance, which are either `available` or `pending`.|
|type|string|true|none|Transaction type: `tax_fund`, `adjustment`, `advance`, `advance_funding`, `anticipation_repayment`, `application_fee`, `application_fee_refund`, `charge`, `climate_order_purchase`, `climate_order_refund`, `connect_collection_transfer`, `contribution`, `inbound_transfer`, `inbound_transfer_reversal`, `issuing_authorization_hold`, `issuing_authorization_release`, `issuing_dispute`, `issuing_dispute_provisional_credit`, `issuing_dispute_provisional_credit_reversal`, `issuing_transaction`, `obligation_outbound`, `obligation_reversal_inbound`, `payment`, `payment_failure_refund`, `payment_network_reserve_hold`, `payment_network_reserve_release`, `payment_refund`, `payment_reversal`, `payment_unreconciled`, `payout`, `payout_cancel`, `payout_failure`, `payout_minimum_balance_hold`, `payout_minimum_balance_release`, `refund`, `refund_failure`, `reserve_transaction`, `reserved_funds`, `reserve_hold`, `reserve_release`, `stripe_fee`, `stripe_fx_fee`, `stripe_balance_payment_debit`, `stripe_balance_payment_debit_reversal`, `tax_fee`, `topup`, `topup_reversal`, `transfer`, `transfer_cancel`, `transfer_failure`, `transfer_refund`, or `fee_credit_funding`. Learn more about [balance transaction types and what they represent](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/balance-transaction-types). To classify transactions for accounting purposes, consider `reporting_category` instead.|

```json
  "status": "string"
```
