
These bank accounts are payment methods on `Customer` objects.

On the other hand [External Accounts](/api#external_accounts) are transfer
destinations on `Account` objects for connected accounts.
They can be bank accounts or debit cards as well, and are documented in the links above.

Related guide: [Bank debits and transfers](/payments/bank-debits-transfers)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account this bank account belongs to. Only applicable on Accounts (not customers or recipients) This property is only available when returned as an [External Account](/api/external_account_bank_accounts/object) where [controller.is_controller](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-is_controller) is `true`.|
|account_holder_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|
|account_holder_type|string \| null|false|none|The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`.|
|account_type|string \| null|false|none|The bank account type. This can only be `checking` or `savings` in most countries. In Japan, this can only be `futsu` or `toza`.|
|available_payout_methods|[string]|false|none|A set of available payout methods for this bank account. Only values from this set should be passed as the `method` when creating a payout.|
|bank_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the bank associated with the routing number (e.g., `WELLS FARGO`).|
|country|string|true|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts) paid out to the bank account.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The ID of the customer that the bank account is associated with.|
|default_for_currency|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this bank account is the default external account for its currency.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.|
|future_requirements|[external_account_requirements](#schemaexternal_account_requirements) \| null|false|none|Information about the [upcoming new requirements for the bank account](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/custom-accounts/future-requirements), including what information needs to be collected, and by when.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|last4|string|true|none|The last four digits of the bank account number.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|requirements|[external_account_requirements](#schemaexternal_account_requirements) \| null|false|none|Information about the requirements for the bank account, including what information needs to be collected.|
|routing_number|string \| null|false|none|The routing transit number for the bank account.|
|status|string|true|none|For bank accounts, possible values are `new`, `validated`, `verified`, `verification_failed`, `tokenized_account_number_deactivated` or `errored`. A bank account that hasn't had any activity or validation performed is `new`. If Stripe can determine that the bank account exists, its status will be `validated`. Note that there often isn’t enough information to know (e.g., for smaller credit unions), and the validation is not always run. If customer bank account verification has succeeded, the bank account status will be `verified`. If the verification failed for any reason, such as microdeposit failure, the status will be `verification_failed`. If the status is `tokenized_account_number_deactivated`, the account utilizes a tokenized account number which has been deactivated due to expiration or revocation. This account will need to be reverified to continue using it for money movement. If a payout sent to this bank account fails, we'll set the status to `errored` and will not continue to send [scheduled payouts](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts#payout-schedule) until the bank details are updated.<br><br>For external accounts, possible values are `new`, `errored`, `verification_failed`, and `tokenized_account_number_deactivated`. If a payout fails, the status is set to `errored` and scheduled payouts are stopped until account details are updated. In the US and India, if we can't [verify the owner of the bank account](https://support.stripe.com/questions/bank-account-ownership-verification), we'll set the status to `verification_failed`. Other validations aren't run against external accounts because they're only used for payouts. This means the other statuses don't apply.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|available_payout_methods|instant|
|available_payout_methods|standard|
|object|bank_account|

<h2 id="tocS_billing.alert">billing.alert</h2>

```json
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "billing.alert",
  "status": "active",
  "title": "string",

      {

      }
    ],

  }
```

A billing alert is a resource that notifies you when a certain usage threshold on a meter is crossed. For example, you might create a billing alert to notify you when a certain user made 100 API requests.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alert_type|string|true|none|Defines the type of the alert.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|Status of the alert. This can be active, inactive or archived.|
|title|string|true|none|Title of the alert.|
|usage_threshold|[thresholds_resource_usage_threshold_config](#schemathresholds_resource_usage_threshold_config) \| null|false|none|Encapsulates configuration of the alert to monitor usage on a specific [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|alert_type|usage_threshold|
|object|billing.alert|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|status|inactive|

A credit grant is an API resource that documents the allocation of some billing credits to a customer.

Related guide: [Billing credits](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/billing-credits)

### Properties

|category|string|true|none|The category of this credit grant. This is for tracking purposes and isn't displayed to the customer.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer)|true|none|ID of the customer receiving the billing credits.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|ID of the account representing the customer receiving the billing credits|
|effective_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The time when the billing credits become effective-when they're eligible for use.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The time when the billing credits expire. If not present, the billing credits don't expire.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|A descriptive name shown in dashboard.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|priority|integer \| null|false|none|The priority for applying this credit grant. The highest priority is 0 and the lowest is 100.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this credit grant belongs to.|
|updated|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|voided_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The time when this credit grant was voided. If not present, the credit grant hasn't been voided.|

Meters specify how to aggregate meter events over a billing period. Meter events represent the actions that customers take in your system. Meters attach to prices and form the basis of the bill.

Related guide: [Usage based billing](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based)

|default_aggregation|[billing_meter_resource_aggregation_settings](#schemabilling_meter_resource_aggregation_settings)|true|none|none|
|display_name|string|true|none|The meter's name.|
|event_name|string|true|none|The name of the meter event to record usage for. Corresponds with the `event_name` field on meter events.|
|event_time_window|string \| null|false|none|The time window which meter events have been pre-aggregated for, if any.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|status|string|true|none|The meter's status.|
|status_transitions|[billing_meter_resource_billing_meter_status_transitions](#schemabilling_meter_resource_billing_meter_status_transitions)|true|none|none|
|updated|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|value_settings|[billing_meter_resource_billing_meter_value](#schemabilling_meter_resource_billing_meter_value)|true|none|none|

Meter events represent actions that customers take in your system. You can use meter events to bill a customer based on their usage. Meter events are associated with billing meters, which define both the contents of the event’s payload and how to aggregate those events.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|identifier|string|true|none|A unique identifier for the event.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payload|object|true|none|The payload of the event. This contains the fields corresponding to a meter's `customer_mapping.event_payload_key` (default is `stripe_customer_id`) and `value_settings.event_payload_key` (default is `value`). Read more about the [payload](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/meters/configure#meter-configuration-attributes).|
|timestamp|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The timestamp passed in when creating the event. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|

|---|---|

<a id="tocsbilling.meter_event_adjustment"></a>

```json
{
  "cancel": {
    "identifier": "string"
  },
  "event_name": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "billing.meter_event_adjustment",
  "status": "complete",
  "type": "cancel"
}
```

A billing meter event adjustment is a resource that allows you to cancel a meter event. For example, you might create a billing meter event adjustment to cancel a meter event that was created in error or attached to the wrong customer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cancel|[billing_meter_resource_billing_meter_event_adjustment_cancel](#schemabilling_meter_resource_billing_meter_event_adjustment_cancel) \| null|false|none|Specifies which event to cancel.|
|event_name|string|true|none|The name of the meter event. Corresponds with the `event_name` field on a meter.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|status|string|true|none|The meter event adjustment's status.|
|type|string|true|none|Specifies whether to cancel a single event or a range of events for a time period. Time period cancellation is not supported yet.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|billing.meter_event_adjustment|
|status|complete|
|status|pending|
|type|cancel|

<h2 id="tocS_billing.meter_event_summary">billing.meter_event_summary</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabilling.meter_event_summary"></a>
<a id="schema_billing.meter_event_summary"></a>
<a id="tocSbilling.meter_event_summary"></a>
<a id="tocsbilling.meter_event_summary"></a>

```json
{
  "aggregated_value": 0,
  "end_time": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "meter": "string",
  "object": "billing.meter_event_summary",
  "start_time": 0
}
```

A billing meter event summary represents an aggregated view of a customer's billing meter events within a specified timeframe. It indicates how much
usage was accrued by a customer for that period.

Note: Meters events are aggregated asynchronously so the meter event summaries provide an eventually consistent view of the reported usage.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregated_value|number|true|none|Aggregated value of all the events within `start_time` (inclusive) and `end_time` (inclusive). The aggregation strategy is defined on meter via `default_aggregation`.|
|end_time|integer(unix-time)|true|none|End timestamp for this event summary (exclusive). Must be aligned with minute boundaries.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|meter|string|true|none|The meter associated with this event summary.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|start_time|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Start timestamp for this event summary (inclusive). Must be aligned with minute boundaries.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|billing.meter_event_summary|

A portal configuration describes the functionality and behavior you embed in a portal session. Related guide: [Configure the customer portal](/customer-management/configure-portal).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the configuration is active and can be used to create portal sessions.|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect Application that created the configuration.|
|business_profile|[portal_business_profile](#schemaportal_business_profile)|true|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|default_return_url|string \| null|false|none|The default URL to redirect customers to when they click on the portal's link to return to your website. This can be [overridden](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customer_portal/sessions/create#create_portal_session-return_url) when creating the session.|
|features|[portal_features](#schemaportal_features)|true|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|is_default|boolean|true|none|Whether the configuration is the default. If `true`, this configuration can be managed in the Dashboard and portal sessions will use this configuration unless it is overriden when creating the session.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|login_page|[portal_login_page](#schemaportal_login_page)|true|none|none|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the configuration.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|updated|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|billing_portal.configuration|

```json
  "url": "string"

```

The Billing customer portal is a Stripe-hosted UI for subscription and
billing management.

A portal configuration describes the functionality and features that you
want to provide to your customers through the portal.

A portal session describes the instantiation of the customer portal for
a particular customer. By visiting the session's URL, the customer
can manage their subscriptions and billing details. For security reasons,
sessions are short-lived and will expire if the customer does not visit the URL.
Create sessions on-demand when customers intend to manage their subscriptions
and billing details.

Related guide: [Customer management](/customer-management)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|configuration|string \| [billing_portal.configuration](#schemabilling_portal.configuration)|true|none|The configuration used by this session, describing the features available.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string|true|none|The ID of the customer for this session.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the account for this session.|
|flow|[portal_flows_flow](#schemaportal_flows_flow) \| null|false|none|Information about a specific flow for the customer to go through. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/customer-management/portal-deep-links) to learn more about using customer portal deep links and flows.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|locale|string \| null|false|none|The IETF language tag of the locale Customer Portal is displayed in. If blank or auto, the customer’s `preferred_locales` or browser’s locale is used.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| null|false|none|The account for which the session was created on behalf of. When specified, only subscriptions and invoices with this `on_behalf_of` account appear in the portal. For more information, see the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#settlement-merchant). Use the [Accounts API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object#account_object-settings-branding) to modify the `on_behalf_of` account's branding settings, which the portal displays.|
|return_url|string \| null|false|none|The URL to redirect customers to when they click on the portal's link to return to your website.|
|url|string|true|none|The short-lived URL of the session that gives customers access to the customer portal.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|requested|boolean|true|none|Whether the capability has been requested.|
|requested_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the capability was requested. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|requirements|[account_capability_requirements](#schemaaccount_capability_requirements)|false|none|none|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the capability.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|status|active|

<h2 id="tocS_card">card</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacard"></a>
<a id="schema_card"></a>
<a id="tocScard"></a>
<a id="tocscard"></a>

```json
{
  "account": "string",
  "address_city": "string",
  "address_country": "string",
  "address_line1": "string",
  "address_line1_check": "string",
  "address_line2": "string",
  "address_state": "string",
  "address_zip": "string",
  "address_zip_check": "string",
  "allow_redisplay": "always",
  "available_payout_methods": [
    "instant"
  ],
  "brand": "string",
  "country": "string",
  "currency": "string",
  "customer": "string",
  "cvc_check": "string",
  "default_for_currency": true,
  "dynamic_last4": "string",
  "exp_month": 0,
  "exp_year": 0,
  "fingerprint": "string",
  "funding": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "last4": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "networks": {
    "preferred": "string"
  },
  "object": "card",
  "regulated_status": "regulated",
  "status": "string",
  "tokenization_method": "string"
}
```

You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer
later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to
transfer to those cards later.

Related guide: [Card payments with Sources](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/cards)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|none|
|address_city|string \| null|false|none|City/District/Suburb/Town/Village.|
|address_country|string \| null|false|none|Billing address country, if provided when creating card.|
|address_line1|string \| null|false|none|Address line 1 (Street address/PO Box/Company name).|
|address_line1_check|string \| null|false|none|If `address_line1` was provided, results of the check: `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.|
|address_line2|string \| null|false|none|Address line 2 (Apartment/Suite/Unit/Building).|
|address_state|string \| null|false|none|State/County/Province/Region.|
|address_zip|string \| null|false|none|ZIP or postal code.|
|address_zip_check|string \| null|false|none|If `address_zip` was provided, results of the check: `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.|
|allow_redisplay|string \| null|false|none|This field indicates whether this payment method can be shown again to its customer in a checkout flow. Stripe products such as Checkout and Elements use this field to determine whether a payment method can be shown as a saved payment method in a checkout flow. The field defaults to “unspecified”.|
|available_payout_methods|[string]|false|none|A set of available payout methods for this card. Only values from this set should be passed as the `method` when creating a payout.|
|brand|string|true|none|Card brand. Can be `American Express`, `Cartes Bancaires`, `Diners Club`, `Discover`, `Eftpos Australia`, `Girocard`, `JCB`, `MasterCard`, `UnionPay`, `Visa`, or `Unknown`.|
|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.|
|currency|string(currency) \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO code for currency](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies). Only applicable on accounts (not customers or recipients). The card can be used as a transfer destination for funds in this currency. This property is only available when returned as an [External Account](/api/external_account_cards/object) where [controller.is_controller](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-is_controller) is `true`.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The customer that this card belongs to. This attribute will not be in the card object if the card belongs to an account or recipient instead.|
|cvc_check|string \| null|false|none|If a CVC was provided, results of the check: `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`. A result of unchecked indicates that CVC was provided but hasn't been checked yet. Checks are typically performed when attaching a card to a Customer object, or when creating a charge. For more details, see [Check if a card is valid without a charge](https://support.stripe.com/questions/check-if-a-card-is-valid-without-a-charge).|
|default_for_currency|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this card is the default external account for its currency. This property is only available for accounts where [controller.requirement_collection](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection) is `application`, which includes Custom accounts.|
|dynamic_last4|string \| null|false|none|(For tokenized numbers only.) The last four digits of the device account number.|
|exp_month|integer|true|none|Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.|
|exp_year|integer|true|none|Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|
|funding|string|true|none|Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|last4|string|true|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Cardholder name.|
|networks|[token_card_networks](#schematoken_card_networks)|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|regulated_status|string \| null|false|none|Status of a card based on the card issuer.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|For external accounts that are cards, possible values are `new` and `errored`. If a payout fails, the status is set to `errored` and [scheduled payouts](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts#payout-schedule) are stopped until account details are updated.|
|tokenization_method|string \| null|false|none|If the card number is tokenized, this is the method that was used. Can be `android_pay` (includes Google Pay), `apple_pay`, `masterpass`, `visa_checkout`, or null.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|allow_redisplay|always|
|allow_redisplay|limited|
|allow_redisplay|unspecified|
|available_payout_methods|instant|
|available_payout_methods|standard|
|object|card|
|regulated_status|regulated|
|regulated_status|unregulated|

<h2 id="tocS_cash_balance">cash_balance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacash_balance"></a>
<a id="schema_cash_balance"></a>
<a id="tocScash_balance"></a>
<a id="tocscash_balance"></a>

```json
{
  "available": {
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "customer": "string",
  "customer_account": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "cash_balance",
  "settings": {
    "reconciliation_mode": "automatic",
    "using_merchant_default": true
  }
}
```

A customer's `Cash balance` represents real funds. Customers can add funds to their cash balance by sending a bank transfer. These funds can be used for payment and can eventually be paid out to your bank account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|object \| null|false|none|A hash of all cash balances available to this customer. You cannot delete a customer with any cash balances, even if the balance is 0. Amounts are represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).|
|customer|string|true|none|The ID of the customer whose cash balance this object represents.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|The ID of an Account representing a customer whose cash balance this object represents.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|settings|[customer_balance_customer_balance_settings](#schemacustomer_balance_customer_balance_settings)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|cash_balance|

The `Charge` object represents a single attempt to move money into your Stripe account.
PaymentIntent confirmation is the most common way to create Charges, but [Account Debits](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/account-debits) may also create Charges.
The create and capture methods are deprecated and will be deleted soon. If your integration uses either of them, you need to update it to use a different payment flow, such as [the Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount intended to be collected by this payment. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|amount_captured|integer|true|none|Amount in cents (or local equivalent) captured (can be less than the amount attribute on the charge if a partial capture was made).|
|amount_refunded|integer|true|none|Amount in cents (or local equivalent) refunded (can be less than the amount attribute on the charge if a partial refund was issued).|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect application that created the charge.|
|application_fee|string \| [application_fee](#schemaapplication_fee) \| null|false|none|The application fee (if any) for the charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/direct-charges#collect-fees) for details.|
|application_fee_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount of the application fee (if any) requested for the charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/direct-charges#collect-fees) for details.|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this charge on your account balance (not including refunds or disputes).|
|billing_details|[billing_details](#schemabilling_details)|true|none|none|
|calculated_statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|The full statement descriptor that is passed to card networks, and that is displayed on your customers' credit card and bank statements. Allows you to see what the statement descriptor looks like after the static and dynamic portions are combined. This value only exists for card payments.|
|captured|boolean|true|none|If the charge was created without capturing, this Boolean represents whether it is still uncaptured or has since been captured.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|ID of the customer this charge is for if one exists.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|disputed|boolean|true|none|Whether the charge has been disputed.|
|failure_balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the reversal of the balance on your account due to payment failure.|
|failure_code|string \| null|false|none|Error code explaining reason for charge failure if available (see [the errors section](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) for a list of codes).|
|failure_message|string \| null|false|none|Message to user further explaining reason for charge failure if available.|
|fraud_details|[charge_fraud_details](#schemacharge_fraud_details) \| null|false|none|Information on fraud assessments for the charge.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the charge was made on behalf of without triggering an automatic transfer. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers) for details.|
|outcome|[charge_outcome](#schemacharge_outcome) \| null|false|none|Details about whether the payment was accepted, and why. See [understanding declines](https://docs.stripe.com/declines) for details.|
|paid|boolean|true|none|`true` if the charge succeeded, or was successfully authorized for later capture.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent) \| null|false|none|ID of the PaymentIntent associated with this charge, if one exists.|
|payment_method|string \| null|false|none|ID of the payment method used in this charge.|
|payment_method_details|[payment_method_details](#schemapayment_method_details) \| null|false|none|Details about the payment method at the time of the transaction.|
|presentment_details|[payment_flows_payment_intent_presentment_details](#schemapayment_flows_payment_intent_presentment_details)|false|none|none|
|radar_options|[radar_radar_options](#schemaradar_radar_options)|false|none|Options to configure Radar. See [Radar Session](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/radar-session) for more information.|
|receipt_email|string \| null|false|none|This is the email address that the receipt for this charge was sent to.|
|receipt_number|string \| null|false|none|This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this charge. This attribute will be `null` until a receipt has been sent.|
|receipt_url|string \| null|false|none|This is the URL to view the receipt for this charge. The receipt is kept up-to-date to the latest state of the charge, including any refunds. If the charge is for an Invoice, the receipt will be stylized as an Invoice receipt.|
|refunded|boolean|true|none|Whether the charge has been fully refunded. If the charge is only partially refunded, this attribute will still be false.|
|refunds|object \| null|false|none|A list of refunds that have been applied to the charge.|
|review|string \| [review](#schemareview) \| null|false|none|ID of the review associated with this charge if one exists.|
|shipping|[shipping](#schemashipping) \| null|false|none|Shipping information for the charge.|
|source_transfer|string \| [transfer](#schematransfer) \| null|false|none|The transfer ID which created this charge. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/destination-charges) for details.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|For a non-card charge, text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see [the Statement Descriptor docs](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors).<br><br>For a card charge, this value is ignored unless you don't specify a `statement_descriptor_suffix`, in which case this value is used as the suffix.|
|statement_descriptor_suffix|string \| null|false|none|Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's [statement descriptor prefix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#static) to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement. If the account has no prefix value, the suffix is concatenated to the account's statement descriptor.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the payment is either `succeeded`, `pending`, or `failed`.|
|transfer|string \| [transfer](#schematransfer)|false|none|ID of the transfer to the `destination` account (only applicable if the charge was created using the `destination` parameter).|
|transfer_data|[charge_transfer_data](#schemacharge_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|An optional dictionary including the account to automatically transfer to as part of a destination charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/destination-charges) for details.|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|charge|
|status|failed|
|status|pending|
|status|succeeded|

<h2 id="tocS_charge_outcome">charge_outcome</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacharge_outcome"></a>
<a id="schema_charge_outcome"></a>
<a id="tocScharge_outcome"></a>
<a id="tocscharge_outcome"></a>

```json
{
  "advice_code": "confirm_card_data",
  "network_advice_code": "string",
  "network_decline_code": "string",
  "network_status": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "risk_level": "string",
  "risk_score": 0,
  "rule": "string",
  "seller_message": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|advice_code|string \| null|false|none|An enumerated value providing a more detailed explanation on [how to proceed with an error](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#retrying-issuer-declines).|
|network_advice_code|string \| null|false|none|For charges declined by the network, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice returned by the network on how to proceed with an error.|
|network_decline_code|string \| null|false|none|For charges declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the charge failed.|
|network_status|string \| null|false|none|Possible values are `approved_by_network`, `declined_by_network`, `not_sent_to_network`, and `reversed_after_approval`. The value `reversed_after_approval` indicates the payment was [blocked by Stripe](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#blocked-payments) after bank authorization, and may temporarily appear as "pending" on a cardholder's statement.|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|An enumerated value providing a more detailed explanation of the outcome's `type`. Charges blocked by Radar's default block rule have the value `highest_risk_level`. Charges placed in review by Radar's default review rule have the value `elevated_risk_level`. Charges blocked because the payment is unlikely to be authorized have the value `low_probability_of_authorization`. Charges authorized, blocked, or placed in review by custom rules have the value `rule`. See [understanding declines](https://docs.stripe.com/declines) for more details.|
|risk_level|string|false|none|Stripe Radar's evaluation of the riskiness of the payment. Possible values for evaluated payments are `normal`, `elevated`, `highest`. For non-card payments, and card-based payments predating the public assignment of risk levels, this field will have the value `not_assessed`. In the event of an error in the evaluation, this field will have the value `unknown`. This field is only available with Radar.|
|risk_score|integer|false|none|Stripe Radar's evaluation of the riskiness of the payment. Possible values for evaluated payments are between 0 and 100. For non-card payments, card-based payments predating the public assignment of risk scores, or in the event of an error during evaluation, this field will not be present. This field is only available with Radar for Fraud Teams.|
|rule|string \| [rule](#schemarule)|false|none|The ID of the Radar rule that matched the payment, if applicable.|
|seller_message|string \| null|false|none|A human-readable description of the outcome type and reason, designed for you (the recipient of the payment), not your customer.|
|type|string|true|none|Possible values are `authorized`, `manual_review`, `issuer_declined`, `blocked`, and `invalid`. See [understanding declines](https://docs.stripe.com/declines) and [Radar reviews](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|advice_code|confirm_card_data|
|advice_code|do_not_try_again|
|advice_code|try_again_later|


A Checkout Session represents your customer's session as they pay for
one-time purchases or subscriptions through [Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout)
or [Payment Links](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-links). We recommend creating a
new Session each time your customer attempts to pay.

Once payment is successful, the Checkout Session will contain a reference
to the [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers), and either the successful
[PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents) or an active
[Subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions).

You can create a Checkout Session on your server and redirect to its URL
to begin Checkout.

Related guide: [Checkout quickstart](https://docs.stripe.com/checkout/quickstart)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|adaptive_pricing|[payment_pages_checkout_session_adaptive_pricing](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_adaptive_pricing) \| null|false|none|Settings for price localization with [Adaptive Pricing](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/adaptive-pricing).|
|after_expiration|[payment_pages_checkout_session_after_expiration](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_after_expiration) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration for actions to take if this Checkout Session expires.|
|allow_promotion_codes|boolean \| null|false|none|Enables user redeemable promotion codes.|
|allowed_payment_method_types|[string]|false|none|A list of the types of payment methods (e.g., `card`) this Checkout Session can accept.|
|amount_subtotal|integer \| null|false|none|Total of all items before discounts or taxes are applied.|
|amount_total|integer \| null|false|none|Total of all items after discounts and taxes are applied.|
|automatic_tax|[payment_pages_checkout_session_automatic_tax](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_automatic_tax)|true|none|none|
|billing_address_collection|string \| null|false|none|Describes whether Checkout should collect the customer's billing address. Defaults to `auto`.|
|branding_settings|[payment_pages_checkout_session_branding_settings](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_branding_settings)|false|none|none|
|cancel_url|string \| null|false|none|If set, Checkout displays a back button and customers will be directed to this URL if they decide to cancel payment and return to your website.|
|client_reference_id|string \| null|false|none|A unique string to reference the Checkout Session. This can be a<br>customer ID, a cart ID, or similar, and can be used to reconcile the<br>Session with your internal systems.|
|client_secret|string \| null|false|none|The client secret of your Checkout Session. Applies to Checkout Sessions with `ui_mode: embedded_page` or `ui_mode: elements`. For `ui_mode: embedded_page`, the client secret is to be used when initializing Stripe.js embedded checkout.<br> For `ui_mode: elements`, use the client secret with [initCheckout](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/init) on your front end.|
|collected_information|[payment_pages_checkout_session_collected_information](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_collected_information) \| null|false|none|Information about the customer collected within the Checkout Session.|
|consent|[payment_pages_checkout_session_consent](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_consent) \| null|false|none|Results of `consent_collection` for this session.|
|consent_collection|[payment_pages_checkout_session_consent_collection](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_consent_collection) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration for the Checkout Session to gather active consent from customers.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency) \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|currency_conversion|[payment_pages_checkout_session_currency_conversion](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_currency_conversion) \| null|false|none|Currency conversion details for [Adaptive Pricing](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/adaptive-pricing) sessions created before 2025-03-31.|
|custom_fields|[[payment_pages_checkout_session_custom_fields](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_custom_fields)]|true|none|Collect additional information from your customer using custom fields. Up to 3 fields are supported. You can't set this parameter if `ui_mode` is `elements`.|
|custom_text|[payment_pages_checkout_session_custom_text](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_custom_text)|true|none|none|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The ID of the customer for this Session.<br>For Checkout Sessions in `subscription` mode or Checkout Sessions with `customer_creation` set as `always` in `payment` mode, Checkout<br>will create a new customer object based on information provided<br>during the payment flow unless an existing customer was provided when<br>the Session was created.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the account for this Session.|
|customer_creation|string \| null|false|none|Configure whether a Checkout Session creates a Customer when the Checkout Session completes.|
|customer_details|[payment_pages_checkout_session_customer_details](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_customer_details) \| null|false|none|The customer details including the customer's tax exempt status and the customer's tax IDs. To access information about the customer once the payment flow is<br>complete, use the `customer` attribute.|

```json
{
  "currency": "cad",
  "mandate_options": {
    "custom_mandate_url": "string",
    "default_for": [
      "invoice"
    ],
    "interval_description": "string",
    "payment_schedule": "combined",
    "transaction_type": "business"
  },
  "setup_future_usage": "none",
  "target_date": "string",
  "verification_method": "automatic"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|currency|string|false|none|Currency supported by the bank account. Returned when the Session is in `setup` mode.|
|mandate_options|[checkout_acss_debit_mandate_options](#schemacheckout_acss_debit_mandate_options)|false|none|none|
|setup_future_usage|string|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).|
|target_date|string|false|none|Controls when Stripe will attempt to debit the funds from the customer's account. The date must be a string in YYYY-MM-DD format. The date must be in the future and between 3 and 15 calendar days from now.|
|verification_method|string|false|none|Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`.|

|verification_method|string|false|none|Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|setup_future_usage|none|
|setup_future_usage|off_session|
|setup_future_usage|on_session|
|verification_method|automatic|
|verification_method|instant|


Orders represent your intent to purchase a particular Climate product. When you create an order, the
payment is deducted from your merchant balance.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_fees|integer|true|none|Total amount of [Frontier](https://frontierclimate.com/)'s service fees in the currency's smallest unit.|
|amount_subtotal|integer|true|none|Total amount of the carbon removal in the currency's smallest unit.|
|amount_total|integer|true|none|Total amount of the order including fees in the currency's smallest unit.|
|beneficiary|[climate_removals_beneficiary](#schemaclimate_removals_beneficiary)|false|none|none|
|canceled_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the order was canceled. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|cancellation_reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for the cancellation of this order.|
|certificate|string \| null|false|none|For delivered orders, a URL to a delivery certificate for the order.|
|confirmed_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the order was confirmed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase, representing the currency for this order.|
|delayed_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the order's expected_delivery_year was delayed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|delivered_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the order was delivered. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|delivery_details|[[climate_removals_order_deliveries](#schemaclimate_removals_order_deliveries)]|true|none|Details about the delivery of carbon removal for this order.|
|expected_delivery_year|integer|true|none|The year this order is expected to be delivered. If the year is in the past, the order is a spot purchase and will be delivered within 30 days of purchase.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|metric_tons|string(decimal)|true|none|Quantity of carbon removal that is included in this order.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|product|string \| [climate.product](#schemaclimate.product)|true|none|Unique ID for the Climate `Product` this order is purchasing.|
|product_substituted_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the order's product was substituted for a different product. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|status|string|true|none|The current status of this order.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|cancellation_reason|expired|
|cancellation_reason|product_unavailable|
|cancellation_reason|requested|
|object|climate.order|
|status|awaiting_funds|
|status|canceled|
|status|confirmed|
|status|delivered|
|status|open|

A Climate product represents a type of carbon removal unit available for reservation.
You can retrieve it to see the current price and availability.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|current_prices_per_metric_ton|object|true|none|Current prices for a metric ton of carbon removal in a currency's smallest unit.|
|delivery_year|integer \| null|false|none|The year in which the carbon removal is expected to be delivered. If the year is in the past, this represents spot inventory with guaranteed delivery.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object. For convenience, Climate product IDs are human-readable strings<br>that start with `climsku_`. See [carbon removal inventory](https://stripe.com/docs/climate/orders/carbon-removal-inventory)<br>for a list of available carbon removal products.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metric_tons_available|string(decimal)|true|none|The quantity of metric tons available for reservation.|
|name|string|true|none|The Climate product's name.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|suppliers|[[climate.supplier](#schemaclimate.supplier)]|true|none|The carbon removal suppliers that fulfill orders for this Climate product.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|climate.product|

```json
  },
```


ConfirmationTokens help transport client side data collected by Stripe JS over
to your server for confirming a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent. If the confirmation
is successful, values present on the ConfirmationToken are written onto the Intent.

To learn more about how to use ConfirmationToken, visit the related guides:
- [Finalize payments on the server](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/finalize-payments-on-the-server)
- [Build two-step confirmation](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/build-a-two-step-confirmation).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which this ConfirmationToken expires and can no longer be used to confirm a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|mandate_data|[confirmation_tokens_resource_mandate_data](#schemaconfirmation_tokens_resource_mandate_data) \| null|false|none|Data used for generating a Mandate.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of key-value pairs that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_intent|string \| null|false|none|ID of the PaymentIntent that this ConfirmationToken was used to confirm, or null if this ConfirmationToken has not yet been used.|
|payment_method_options|[confirmation_tokens_resource_payment_method_options](#schemaconfirmation_tokens_resource_payment_method_options) \| null|false|none|Payment-method-specific configuration for this ConfirmationToken.|
|payment_method_preview|[confirmation_tokens_resource_payment_method_preview](#schemaconfirmation_tokens_resource_payment_method_preview) \| null|false|none|Payment details collected by the Payment Element, used to create a PaymentMethod when a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent is confirmed with this ConfirmationToken.|
|return_url|string \| null|false|none|Return URL used to confirm the Intent.|
|setup_future_usage|string \| null|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this ConfirmationToken's payment method.<br><br>The presence of this property will [attach the payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment) to the PaymentIntent's Customer, if present, after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete.|
|setup_intent|string \| null|false|none|ID of the SetupIntent that this ConfirmationToken was used to confirm, or null if this ConfirmationToken has not yet been used.|
|shipping|[confirmation_tokens_resource_shipping](#schemaconfirmation_tokens_resource_shipping) \| null|false|none|Shipping information collected on this ConfirmationToken.|
|use_stripe_sdk|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the Stripe SDK is used to handle confirmation flow. Defaults to `true` on ConfirmationToken.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|confirmation_token|
|setup_future_usage|off_session|
|setup_future_usage|on_session|

```json
  "disable_stripe_user_authentication": true,

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|disable_stripe_user_authentication|boolean|true|none|Whether Stripe user authentication is disabled. This value can only be `true` for accounts where `controller.requirement_collection` is `application` for the account. The default value is the opposite of the `external_account_collection` value. For example, if you don't set `external_account_collection`, it defaults to `true` and `disable_stripe_user_authentication` defaults to `false`.|
|external_account_collection|boolean|true|none|Whether external account collection is enabled. This feature can only be `false` for accounts where you’re responsible for collecting updated information when requirements are due or change, like Custom accounts. The default value for this feature is `true`.|

|dispute_management|boolean|true|none|Whether responding to disputes is enabled, including submitting evidence and accepting disputes. This is `true` by default.|
|refund_management|boolean|true|none|Whether sending refunds is enabled. This is `true` by default.|
|smart_disputes_management|boolean|true|none|Whether to allow connected accounts to submit disputes using Smart Disputes. Defaults to the value of `dispute_management`.|

This value can only be `true` for accounts where `controller.requirement_collection` is `application` for the account. The default value is the opposite of the `external_account_collection` value. <h2 id="tocS_country_spec">country_spec</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacountry_spec"></a>
<a id="schema_country_spec"></a>
<a id="tocScountry_spec"></a>
<a id="tocscountry_spec"></a>

```json
{
  "default_currency": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "object": "country_spec",
  "supported_bank_account_currencies": {
    "property1": [
      "string"
    ],
    "property2": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "supported_payment_currencies": [
    "string"
  ],
  "supported_payment_methods": [
    "string"
  ],
  "supported_transfer_countries": [
    "string"
  ],
  "verification_fields": {
    "company": {
      "additional": [
        "string"
      ],
      "minimum": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "individual": {
      "additional": [
        "string"
      ],
      "minimum": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Stripe needs to collect certain pieces of information about each account
created. These requirements can differ depending on the account's country. The
Country Specs API makes these rules available to your integration.

You can also view the information from this API call as [an online
guide](/docs/connect/required-verification-information).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default_currency|string|true|none|The default currency for this country. This applies to both payment methods and bank accounts.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object. Represented as the ISO country code for this country.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|supported_bank_account_currencies|object|true|none|Currencies that can be accepted in the specific country (for transfers).|
|supported_payment_currencies|[string]|true|none|Currencies that can be accepted in the specified country (for payments).|
|supported_payment_methods|[string]|true|none|Payment methods available in the specified country. You may need to enable some payment methods (e.g., [ACH](https://stripe.com/docs/ach)) on your account before they appear in this list. The `stripe` payment method refers to [charging through your platform](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/destination-charges).|
|supported_transfer_countries|[string]|true|none|Countries that can accept transfers from the specified country.|
|verification_fields|[country_spec_verification_fields](#schemacountry_spec_verification_fields)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|country_spec|

<h2 id="tocS_coupon">coupon</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacoupon"></a>
<a id="schema_coupon"></a>
<a id="tocScoupon"></a>
<a id="tocscoupon"></a>

```json
{
  "amount_off": 0,
  "applies_to": {
    "products": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "currency_options": {
    "property1": {
      "amount_off": 0
    },
    "property2": {
      "amount_off": 0
    }
  },
  "duration": "forever",
  "duration_in_months": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "max_redemptions": 0,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "object": "coupon",
  "percent_off": 0,
  "redeem_by": 0,
  "times_redeemed": 0,
  "valid": true
}
```

A coupon contains information about a percent-off or amount-off discount you
might want to apply to a customer. Coupons may be applied to [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/api#subscriptions), [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/api#invoices),
[checkout sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions), [quotes](https://docs.stripe.com/api#quotes), and more. Coupons do not work with conventional one-off [charges](/api/charges/create) or [payment intents](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_off|integer \| null|false|none|Amount (in the `currency` specified) that will be taken off the subtotal of any invoices for this customer.|
|applies_to|[coupon_applies_to](#schemacoupon_applies_to)|false|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency) \| null|false|none|If `amount_off` has been set, the three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) of the amount to take off.|
|currency_options|object|false|none|Coupons defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|duration|string|true|none|One of `forever`, `once`, or `repeating`. Describes how long a customer who applies this coupon will get the discount.|
|duration_in_months|integer \| null|false|none|If `duration` is `repeating`, the number of months the coupon applies. Null if coupon `duration` is `forever` or `once`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|max_redemptions|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of times this coupon can be redeemed, in total, across all customers, before it is no longer valid.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the coupon displayed to customers on for instance invoices or receipts.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|percent_off|number \| null|false|none|Percent that will be taken off the subtotal of any invoices for this customer for the duration of the coupon. For example, a coupon with percent_off of 50 will make a $ (or local equivalent)100 invoice $ (or local equivalent)50 instead.|
|redeem_by|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date after which the coupon can no longer be redeemed.|
|times_redeemed|integer|true|none|Number of times this coupon has been applied to a customer.|
|valid|boolean|true|none|Taking account of the above properties, whether this coupon can still be applied to a customer.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|duration|forever|
|duration|once|
|duration|repeating|
|object|coupon|

Issue a credit note to adjust an invoice's amount after the invoice is finalized.

Related guide: [Credit notes](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/credit-notes)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note, including tax.|
|amount_shipping|integer|true|none|This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer)|true|none|ID of the customer.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|ID of the account representing the customer.|
|customer_balance_transaction|string \| [customer_balance_transaction](#schemacustomer_balance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Customer balance transaction related to this credit note.|
|discount_amount|integer|true|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of discount that was credited.|
|discount_amounts|[[discounts_resource_discount_amount](#schemadiscounts_resource_discount_amount)]|true|none|The aggregate amounts calculated per discount for all line items.|
|effective_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The date when this credit note is in effect. Same as `created` unless overwritten. When defined, this value replaces the system-generated 'Date of issue' printed on the credit note PDF.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|none|ID of the invoice.|
|lines|object|true|none|Line items that make up the credit note|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|memo|string \| null|false|none|Customer-facing text that appears on the credit note PDF.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|number|string|true|none|A unique number that identifies this particular credit note and appears on the PDF of the credit note and its associated invoice.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|out_of_band_amount|integer \| null|false|none|Amount that was credited outside of Stripe.|
|pdf|string|true|none|The link to download the PDF of the credit note.|
|post_payment_amount|integer|true|none|The amount of the credit note that was refunded to the customer, credited to the customer's balance, credited outside of Stripe, or any combination thereof.|
|pre_payment_amount|integer|true|none|The amount of the credit note by which the invoice's `amount_remaining` and `amount_due` were reduced.|
|pretax_credit_amounts|[[credit_notes_pretax_credit_amount](#schemacredit_notes_pretax_credit_amount)]|true|none|The pretax credit amounts (ex: discount, credit grants, etc) for all line items.|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for issuing this credit note, one of `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `order_change`, or `product_unsatisfactory`|
|refunds|[[credit_note_refund](#schemacredit_note_refund)]|true|none|Refunds related to this credit note.|
|shipping_cost|[invoices_resource_shipping_cost](#schemainvoices_resource_shipping_cost) \| null|false|none|The details of the cost of shipping, including the ShippingRate applied to the invoice.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of this credit note, one of `issued` or `void`. Learn more about [voiding credit notes](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/credit-notes#voiding).|
|subtotal|integer|true|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount of the credit note, excluding exclusive tax and invoice level discounts.|
|subtotal_excluding_tax|integer \| null|false|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the amount of the credit note, excluding all tax and invoice level discounts.|
|total|integer|true|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note, including tax and all discount.|
|total_excluding_tax|integer \| null|false|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the total amount of the credit note, excluding tax, but including discounts.|
|total_taxes|[[billing_bill_resource_invoicing_taxes_tax](#schemabilling_bill_resource_invoicing_taxes_tax)]|false|none|The aggregate tax information for all line items.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of this credit note, one of `pre_payment` or `post_payment`. A `pre_payment` credit note means it was issued when the invoice was open. A `post_payment` credit note means it was issued when the invoice was paid.|
|voided_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The time that the credit note was voided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|credit_note|
|reason|duplicate|
|reason|fraudulent|
|reason|order_change|
|reason|product_unsatisfactory|
|status|issued|
|status|void|
|type|mixed|
|type|post_payment|
|type|pre_payment|

The credit note line item object

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the gross amount being credited for this line item, excluding (exclusive) tax and discounts.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Description of the item being credited.|
|discount_amount|integer|true|none|The integer amount in cents (or local equivalent) representing the discount being credited for this line item.|
|discount_amounts|[[discounts_resource_discount_amount](#schemadiscounts_resource_discount_amount)]|true|none|The amount of discount calculated per discount for this line item|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice_line_item|string|false|none|ID of the invoice line item being credited|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|pretax_credit_amounts|[[credit_notes_pretax_credit_amount](#schemacredit_notes_pretax_credit_amount)]|true|none|The pretax credit amounts (ex: discount, credit grants, etc) for this line item.|
|quantity|integer \| null|false|none|The number of units of product being credited.|
|tax_rates|[[tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|true|none|The tax rates which apply to the line item.|
|taxes|[[billing_bill_resource_invoicing_taxes_tax](#schemabilling_bill_resource_invoicing_taxes_tax)]|false|none|The tax information of the line item.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the credit note line item, one of `invoice_line_item` or `custom_line_item`. When the type is `invoice_line_item` there is an additional `invoice_line_item` property on the resource the value of which is the id of the credited line item on the invoice.|
|unit_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The cost of each unit of product being credited.|
|unit_amount_decimal|string(decimal) \| null|false|none|Same as `unit_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|credit_note_line_item|
|type|custom_line_item|
|type|invoice_line_item|
