A PaymentIntent guides you through the process of collecting a payment from your customer.
We recommend that you create exactly one PaymentIntent for each order or
customer session in your system. You can reference the PaymentIntent later to
see the history of payment attempts for a particular session.

A PaymentIntent transitions through
[multiple statuses](/payments/paymentintents/lifecycle)
throughout its lifetime as it interfaces with Stripe.js to perform
authentication flows and ultimately creates at most one successful charge.

Related guide: [Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_payment_method_types|[string]|false|none|The list of payment method types allowed for use with this payment. Stripe automatically returns compatible payment methods from this list in the `payment_method_types` field of the response, based on the other PaymentIntent parameters, such as `currency`, `amount`, and `customer`.|
|amount|integer|false|none|Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|amount_capturable|integer|false|none|Amount that can be captured from this PaymentIntent.|
|amount_details|[payment_flows_amount_details](#schemapayment_flows_amount_details) \| [payment_flows_amount_details_client](#schemapayment_flows_amount_details_client)|false|none|none|
|amount_received|integer|false|none|Amount that this PaymentIntent collects.|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect application that created the PaymentIntent.|
|application_fee_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The amount of the application fee collected will be capped at the total amount captured. For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/connected-accounts).|
|automatic_payment_methods|[payment_flows_automatic_payment_methods_payment_intent](#schemapayment_flows_automatic_payment_methods_payment_intent) \| null|false|none|Settings to configure compatible payment methods from the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/payment_methods)|
|canceled_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Populated when `status` is `canceled`, this is the time at which the PaymentIntent was canceled. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|cancellation_reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for cancellation of this PaymentIntent, either user-provided (`duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`, or `abandoned`) or generated by Stripe internally (`failed_invoice`, `void_invoice`, `automatic`, or `expired`).|
|capture_method|string|false|none|Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account.|
|client_secret|string \| null|false|none|The client secret of this PaymentIntent. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key. <br><br>The client secret can be used to complete a payment from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the customer. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret.<br><br>Refer to our docs to [accept a payment](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment?ui=elements) and learn about how `client_secret` should be handled.|
|confirmation_method|string|false|none|Describes whether we can confirm this PaymentIntent automatically, or if it requires customer action to confirm the payment.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|false|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|ID of the Customer this PaymentIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this PaymentIntent.<br><br>If [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) is set and this PaymentIntent's payment method is not `card_present`, then the payment method attaches to the Customer after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card is created and attached to the Customer instead.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|ID of the Account representing the customer that this PaymentIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>Payment methods attached to other Accounts cannot be used with this PaymentIntent.<br><br>If [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) is set and this PaymentIntent's payment method is not `card_present`, then the payment method attaches to the Account after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card is created and attached to the Account instead.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|excluded_payment_method_types|[string]|false|none|The list of payment method types to exclude from use with this payment.|
|hooks|[payment_flows_payment_intent_async_workflows](#schemapayment_flows_payment_intent_async_workflows)|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|last_payment_error|[api_errors](#schemaapi_errors) \| null|false|none|The payment error encountered in the previous PaymentIntent confirmation. It will be cleared if the PaymentIntent is later updated for any reason.|
|latest_charge|string \| [charge](#schemacharge) \| null|false|none|ID of the latest [Charge object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges) created by this PaymentIntent. This property is `null` until PaymentIntent confirmation is attempted.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|managed_payments|[smor_resource_managed_payments](#schemasmor_resource_managed_payments) \| null|false|none|Settings for Managed Payments.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Learn more about [storing information in metadata](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/creating-payment-intents#storing-information-in-metadata).|
|next_action|[payment_intent_next_action](#schemapayment_intent_next_action) \| null|false|none|If present, this property tells you what actions you need to take in order for your customer to fulfill a payment using the provided source.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|You can specify the settlement merchant as the<br>connected account using the `on_behalf_of` attribute on the charge. See the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](/payments/connected-accounts) for details.|
|payment_details|[payment_flows_payment_details](#schemapayment_flows_payment_details)|false|none|none|
|payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the payment method used in this PaymentIntent.|
|payment_method_configuration_details|[payment_method_config_biz_payment_method_configuration_details](#schemapayment_method_config_biz_payment_method_configuration_details) \| null|false|none|Information about the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) used for this PaymentIntent.|
|payment_method_options|[payment_intent_payment_method_options](#schemapayment_intent_payment_method_options) \| null|false|none|Payment-method-specific configuration for this PaymentIntent.|
|payment_method_types|[string]|false|none|The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this PaymentIntent is allowed to use. A comprehensive list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).|
|payment_record|string \| [payment_record](#schemapayment_record) \| null|false|none|ID of the [Payment Record object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-record) created by this PaymentIntent.|
|presentment_details|[payment_flows_payment_intent_presentment_details](#schemapayment_flows_payment_intent_presentment_details)|false|none|none|
|processing|[payment_intent_processing](#schemapayment_intent_processing) \| null|false|none|If present, this property tells you about the processing state of the payment.|
|receipt_email|string \| null|false|none|Email address that the receipt for the resulting payment will be sent to. If `receipt_email` is specified for a payment in live mode, a receipt will be sent regardless of your [email settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/emails).|
|review|string \| [review](#schemareview) \| null|false|none|ID of the review associated with this PaymentIntent, if any.|
|setup_future_usage|string \| null|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).|
|shipping|[shipping](#schemashipping) \| null|false|none|Shipping information for this PaymentIntent.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor for a non-card charge. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see [the Statement Descriptor docs](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors).<br><br>Setting this value for a card charge returns an error. For card charges, set the [statement_descriptor_suffix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#dynamic) instead.|
|statement_descriptor_suffix|string \| null|false|none|Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's [statement descriptor prefix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#static) to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of this PaymentIntent, one of `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `requires_capture`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`. Read more about each PaymentIntent [status](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses).|
|transfer_data|[transfer_data](#schematransfer_data) \| null|false|none|The data that automatically creates a Transfer after the payment finalizes. Learn more about the [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/connected-accounts).|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies the resulting payment as part of a group. Learn more about the [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers).|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|discount_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The discount applied on this line item represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). An integer greater than 0.<br><br>This field is mutually exclusive with the `amount_details[discount_amount]` field.|

|product_code|string \| null|false|none|The product code of the line item, such as an SKU. Required for L3 rates. At most 12 characters long.|
|product_name|string|true|none|The product name of the line item. Required for L3 rates. At most 1024 characters long.<br><br>For Cards, this field is truncated to 26 alphanumeric characters before being sent to the card networks. For PayPal, this field is truncated to 127 characters.|
|quantity|integer|true|none|The quantity of items. Required for L3 rates. An integer greater than 0.|
|tax|[payment_flows_amount_details_resource_line_items_list_resource_line_item_resource_tax](#schemapayment_flows_amount_details_resource_line_items_list_resource_line_item_resource_tax) \| null|false|none|Contains information about the tax on the item.|
|unit_cost|integer|true|none|The unit cost of the line item represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). Required for L3 rates. An integer greater than or equal to 0.|
|unit_of_measure|string \| null|false|none|A unit of measure for the line item, such as gallons, feet, meters, etc. Required for L3 rates. At most 12 alphanumeric characters long.|

<h2 id="tocS_payment_intent_payment_method_options_acss_debit">payment_intent_payment_method_options_acss_debit</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapayment_intent_payment_method_options_acss_debit"></a>
<a id="schema_payment_intent_payment_method_options_acss_debit"></a>
<a id="tocSpayment_intent_payment_method_options_acss_debit"></a>
<a id="tocspayment_intent_payment_method_options_acss_debit"></a>

```json
{
  "mandate_options": {
    "custom_mandate_url": "string",
    "interval_description": "string",
    "payment_schedule": "combined",
    "transaction_type": "business"
  },
  "setup_future_usage": "none",
  "target_date": "string",
  "verification_method": "automatic"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mandate_options|[payment_intent_payment_method_options_mandate_options_acss_debit](#schemapayment_intent_payment_method_options_mandate_options_acss_debit)|false|none|none|
|setup_future_usage|string|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).|
|target_date|string|false|none|Controls when Stripe will attempt to debit the funds from the customer's account. The date must be a string in YYYY-MM-DD format. The date must be in the future and between 3 and 15 calendar days from now.|
|verification_method|string|false|none|Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|setup_future_usage|none|
|setup_future_usage|off_session|
|setup_future_usage|on_session|
|verification_method|automatic|
|verification_method|instant|
|verification_method|microdeposits|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|capture_method|string|false|none|Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account.|

|mandate_options|[payment_method_options_card_mandate_options](#schemapayment_method_options_card_mandate_options) \| null|false|none|Configuration options for setting up an eMandate for cards issued in India.|
|network|string \| null|false|none|Selected network to process this payment intent on. Depends on the available networks of the card attached to the payment intent. Can be only set confirm-time.|
|request_extended_authorization|string|false|none|Request ability to [capture beyond the standard authorization validity window](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/extended-authorization) for this PaymentIntent.|
|request_incremental_authorization|string|false|none|Request ability to [increment the authorization](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/incremental-authorization) for this PaymentIntent.|
|request_multicapture|string|false|none|Request ability to make [multiple captures](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multicapture) for this PaymentIntent.|
|request_overcapture|string|false|none|Request ability to [overcapture](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/overcapture) for this PaymentIntent.|
|request_three_d_secure|string \| null|false|none|We strongly recommend that you rely on our SCA Engine to automatically prompt your customers for authentication based on risk level and [other requirements](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). However, if you wish to request 3D Secure based on logic from your own fraud engine, provide this option. If not provided, this value defaults to `automatic`. Read our guide on [manually requesting 3D Secure](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/authentication-flow#manual-three-ds) for more information on how this configuration interacts with Radar and our SCA Engine.|
|require_cvc_recollection|boolean|false|none|When enabled, using a card that is attached to a customer will require the CVC to be provided again (i.e. using the cvc_token parameter).|
|setup_future_usage|string|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).|
|statement_descriptor_suffix_kana|string|false|none|Provides information about a card payment that customers see on their statements. Concatenated with the Kana prefix (shortened Kana descriptor) or Kana statement descriptor that’s set on the account to form the complete statement descriptor. Maximum 22 characters. On card statements, the *concatenation* of both prefix and suffix (including separators) will appear truncated to 22 characters.|
|statement_descriptor_suffix_kanji|string|false|none|Provides information about a card payment that customers see on their statements. Concatenated with the Kanji prefix (shortened Kanji descriptor) or Kanji statement descriptor that’s set on the account to form the complete statement descriptor. Maximum 17 characters. On card statements, the *concatenation* of both prefix and suffix (including separators) will appear truncated to 17 characters.|

|setup_future_usage|string|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).|
|target_date|string|false|none|Controls when Stripe will attempt to debit the funds from the customer's account. The date must be a string in YYYY-MM-DD format. The date must be in the future and between 3 and 15 calendar days from now.|

A payment link is a shareable URL that will take your customers to a hosted payment page. A payment link can be shared and used multiple times.

When a customer opens a payment link it will open a new [checkout session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions) to render the payment page. You can use [checkout session events](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types#event_types-checkout.session.completed) to track payments through payment links.

Related guide: [Payment Links API](https://docs.stripe.com/payment-links)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the payment link's `url` is active. If `false`, customers visiting the URL will be shown a page saying that the link has been deactivated.|
|after_completion|[payment_links_resource_after_completion](#schemapayment_links_resource_after_completion)|true|none|none|
|allow_promotion_codes|boolean|true|none|Whether user redeemable promotion codes are enabled.|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|The ID of the Connect application that created the Payment Link.|
|application_fee_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account.|
|application_fee_percent|number \| null|false|none|This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account.|
|automatic_tax|[payment_links_resource_automatic_tax](#schemapayment_links_resource_automatic_tax)|true|none|none|
|billing_address_collection|string|true|none|Configuration for collecting the customer's billing address. Defaults to `auto`.|
|consent_collection|[payment_links_resource_consent_collection](#schemapayment_links_resource_consent_collection) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration to gather active consent from customers.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|custom_fields|[[payment_links_resource_custom_fields](#schemapayment_links_resource_custom_fields)]|true|none|Collect additional information from your customer using custom fields. Up to 3 fields are supported. You can't set this parameter if `ui_mode` is `elements`.|
|custom_text|[payment_links_resource_custom_text](#schemapayment_links_resource_custom_text)|true|none|none|
|customer_creation|string|true|none|Configuration for Customer creation during checkout.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|inactive_message|string \| null|false|none|The custom message to be displayed to a customer when a payment link is no longer active.|
|invoice_creation|[payment_links_resource_invoice_creation](#schemapayment_links_resource_invoice_creation) \| null|false|none|Configuration for creating invoice for payment mode payment links.|
|line_items|object|false|none|The line items representing what is being sold.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|managed_payments|[payment_pages_checkout_session_managed_payments](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_managed_payments) \| null|false|none|Settings for Managed Payments for this Payment Link and resulting [CheckoutSessions](/api/checkout/sessions/object), [PaymentIntents](/api/payment_intents/object), [Invoices](/api/invoices/object), and [Subscriptions](/api/subscriptions/object).|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name_collection|[payment_links_resource_name_collection](#schemapayment_links_resource_name_collection)|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account on behalf of which to charge. See the [Connect documentation](https://support.stripe.com/questions/sending-invoices-on-behalf-of-connected-accounts) for details.|
|optional_items|[[payment_links_resource_optional_item](#schemapayment_links_resource_optional_item)]|false|none|The optional items presented to the customer at checkout.|
|payment_intent_data|[payment_links_resource_payment_intent_data](#schemapayment_links_resource_payment_intent_data) \| null|false|none|Indicates the parameters to be passed to PaymentIntent creation during checkout.|
|payment_method_collection|string|true|none|Configuration for collecting a payment method during checkout. Defaults to `always`.|

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "maximum": 0,
  "minimum": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Set to true if the quantity can be adjusted to any non-negative integer.|
|maximum|integer \| null|false|none|The maximum quantity of this item the customer can purchase. By default this value is 99.|
|minimum|integer \| null|false|none|The minimum quantity of this item the customer must purchase, if they choose to purchase it. Because this item is optional, the customer will always be able to remove it from their order, even if the `minimum` configured here is greater than 0. By default this value is 0.|

<h2 id="tocS_payment_links_resource_payment_intent_data">payment_links_resource_payment_intent_data</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapayment_links_resource_payment_intent_data"></a>
<a id="schema_payment_links_resource_payment_intent_data"></a>
<a id="tocSpayment_links_resource_payment_intent_data"></a>
<a id="tocspayment_links_resource_payment_intent_data"></a>

```json
{
  "capture_method": "automatic",
  "description": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "setup_future_usage": "off_session",
  "statement_descriptor": "string",
  "statement_descriptor_suffix": "string",
  "transfer_group": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|capture_method|string \| null|false|none|Indicates when the funds will be captured from the customer's account.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that will set metadata on [Payment Intents](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents) generated from this payment link.|
|setup_future_usage|string \| null|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with the payment method collected during checkout.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|For a non-card payment, information about the charge that appears on the customer's statement when this payment succeeds in creating a charge.|
|statement_descriptor_suffix|string \| null|false|none|For a card payment, information about the charge that appears on the customer's statement when this payment succeeds in creating a charge. Concatenated with the account's statement descriptor prefix to form the complete statement descriptor.|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies the resulting payment as part of a group. See the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|capture_method|automatic|
|capture_method|automatic_async|
|capture_method|manual|
|setup_future_usage|off_session|
|setup_future_usage|on_session|

PaymentMethod objects represent your customer's payment instruments.
You can use them with [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents) to collect payments or save them to
Customer objects to store instrument details for future payments.

Related guides: [Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods) and [More Payment Scenarios](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/more-payment-scenarios).

|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.|
|display_brand|string \| null|false|none|The brand to use when displaying the card, this accounts for customer's brand choice on dual-branded cards. Can be `american_express`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners_club`, `discover`, `eftpos_australia`, `interac`, `jcb`, `mastercard`, `union_pay`, `visa`, or `other` and may contain more values in the future.|
|exp_month|integer|true|none|Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.|
|exp_year|integer|true|none|Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|
|funding|string|true|none|Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.|
|generated_from|[payment_method_card_generated_card](#schemapayment_method_card_generated_card) \| null|false|none|Details of the original PaymentMethod that created this object.|
|last4|string|true|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|networks|[networks](#schemanetworks) \| null|false|none|Contains information about card networks that can be used to process the payment.|
|regulated_status|string \| null|false|none|Status of a card based on the card issuer.|
|three_d_secure_usage|[three_d_secure_usage](#schemathree_d_secure_usage) \| null|false|none|Contains details on how this Card may be used for 3D Secure authentication.|
|wallet|[payment_method_card_wallet](#schemapayment_method_card_wallet) \| null|false|none|If this Card is part of a card wallet, this contains the details of the card wallet.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|regulated_status|unregulated|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|brand_product|string \| null|false|none|The [product code](https://stripe.com/docs/card-product-codes) that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.|
|cardholder_name|string \| null|false|none|The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.|
|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.|
|exp_month|integer|true|none|Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.|
|exp_year|integer|true|none|Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|
|funding|string \| null|false|none|Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.|
|issuer|string \| null|false|none|The name of the card's issuing bank.|
|last4|string \| null|false|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|networks|[payment_method_card_present_networks](#schemapayment_method_card_present_networks) \| null|false|none|Contains information about card networks that can be used to process the payment.|
|offline|[payment_method_details_card_present_offline](#schemapayment_method_details_card_present_offline) \| null|false|none|Details about payment methods collected offline.|
|preferred_locales|[string]|false|none|The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.|
|read_method|string \| null|false|none|How card details were read in this transaction.|
|wallet|[payment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_present_common_wallet](#schemapayment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_present_common_wallet)|false|none|none|

PaymentMethodConfigurations control which payment methods are displayed to your customers when you don't explicitly specify payment method types. You can have multiple configurations with different sets of payment methods for different scenarios.

There are two types of PaymentMethodConfigurations. Which is used depends on the [charge type](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/charges):

**Direct** configurations apply to payments created on your account, including Connect destination charges, Connect separate charges and transfers, and payments not involving Connect.

**Child** configurations apply to payments created on your connected accounts using direct charges, and charges with the on_behalf_of parameter.

Child configurations have a `parent` that sets default values and controls which settings connected accounts may override. You can specify a parent ID at payment time, and Stripe will automatically resolve the connected account’s associated child configuration. Parent configurations are [managed in the dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/payment_methods/connected_accounts) and are not available in this API.

Related guides:
- [Payment Method Configurations API](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/payment-method-configurations)
- [Multiple configurations on dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multiple-payment-method-configs)
- [Multiple configurations for your Connect accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/multiple-payment-method-configurations)

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.|

|last4|string \| null|false|none|Last four digits of the bank account number.|
|routing_number|string \| null|false|none|Routing transit number of the bank account.|

|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|

|incremental_authorization|[payment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_details_api_resource_enterprise_features_incremental_authorization_incremental_authorization](#schemapayment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_details_api_resource_enterprise_features_incremental_authorization_incremental_authorization)|false|none|none|
|installments|[payment_method_details_card_installments](#schemapayment_method_details_card_installments) \| null|false|none|Installment details for this payment.<br><br>For more information, see the [installments integration guide](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/installments).|
|last4|string \| null|false|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|mandate|string \| [mandate](#schemamandate) \| null|false|none|ID of the mandate used to make this payment or created by it.|
|multicapture|[payment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_details_api_resource_multicapture](#schemapayment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_details_api_resource_multicapture)|false|none|none|
|network|string \| null|false|none|Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.|
|network_token|[payment_method_details_card_network_token](#schemapayment_method_details_card_network_token) \| null|false|none|If this card has network token credentials, this contains the details of the network token credentials.|
|network_transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.|
|overcapture|[payment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_details_api_resource_enterprise_features_overcapture_overcapture](#schemapayment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_details_api_resource_enterprise_features_overcapture_overcapture)|false|none|none|
|regulated_status|string \| null|false|none|Status of a card based on the card issuer.|
|three_d_secure|[three_d_secure_details_charge](#schemathree_d_secure_details_charge) \| null|false|none|Populated if this transaction used 3D Secure authentication.|
|transaction_link_id|string \| null|false|none|Transaction Link ID (TLID) is a unique identifier for a transaction. This is used by some card networks, such as Mastercard, for transaction linking, in addition to Network Transaction IDs. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.|
|wallet|[payment_method_details_card_wallet](#schemapayment_method_details_card_wallet) \| null|false|none|If this Card is part of a card wallet, this contains the details of the card wallet.|

|network|string \| null|false|none|Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.|
|network_transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.|
|offline|[payment_method_details_card_present_offline](#schemapayment_method_details_card_present_offline) \| null|false|none|Details about payments collected offline.|
|overcapture_supported|boolean|true|none|Defines whether the authorized amount can be over-captured or not|
|preferred_locales|[string]|false|none|The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.|
|read_method|string \| null|false|none|How card details were read in this transaction.|
|reader|string|false|none|ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.|
|receipt|[payment_method_details_card_present_receipt](#schemapayment_method_details_card_present_receipt) \| null|false|none|A collection of fields required to be displayed on receipts. Only required for EMV transactions.|
|wallet|[payment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_present_common_wallet](#schemapayment_flows_private_payment_methods_card_present_common_wallet)|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_type|string|false|none|The type of account being debited or credited|
|application_cryptogram|string \| null|false|none|The Application Cryptogram, a unique value generated by the card to authenticate the transaction with issuers.|
|application_preferred_name|string \| null|false|none|The Application Identifier (AID) on the card used to determine which networks are eligible to process the transaction. Referenced from EMV tag 9F12, data encoded on the card's chip.|
|authorization_code|string \| null|false|none|Identifier for this transaction.|
|authorization_response_code|string \| null|false|none|EMV tag 8A. A code returned by the card issuer.|
|cardholder_verification_method|string \| null|false|none|Describes the method used by the cardholder to verify ownership of the card. One of the following: `approval`, `failure`, `none`, `offline_pin`, `offline_pin_and_signature`, `online_pin`, or `signature`.|
|dedicated_file_name|string \| null|false|none|Similar to the application_preferred_name, identifying the applications (AIDs) available on the card. Referenced from EMV tag 84.|
|terminal_verification_results|string \| null|false|none|A 5-byte string that records the checks and validations that occur between the card and the terminal. These checks determine how the terminal processes the transaction and what risk tolerance is acceptable. Referenced from EMV Tag 95.|
|transaction_status_information|string \| null|false|none|An indication of which steps were completed during the card read process. Referenced from EMV Tag 9B.|

```json
{
```

```json
  "network_transaction_id": "string",

    "string"
  ],
  "read_method": "contact_emv",
  "reader": "string",
  "receipt": {
    "account_type": "checking",
    "application_cryptogram": "string",
    "application_preferred_name": "string",
    "authorization_code": "string",
    "authorization_response_code": "string",
    "cardholder_verification_method": "string",
    "dedicated_file_name": "string",
    "terminal_verification_results": "string",
    "transaction_status_information": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand|string \| null|false|none|Card brand. Can be `interac`, `mastercard` or `visa`.|
|cardholder_name|string \| null|false|none|The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.|
|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.|
|emv_auth_data|string \| null|false|none|Authorization response cryptogram.|
|exp_month|integer|true|none|Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.|
|exp_year|integer|true|none|Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|
|funding|string \| null|false|none|Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.|
|generated_card|string \| null|false|none|ID of a card PaymentMethod generated from the card_present PaymentMethod that may be attached to a Customer for future transactions. Only present if it was possible to generate a card PaymentMethod.|
|issuer|string \| null|false|none|The name of the card's issuing bank.|
|last4|string \| null|false|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|location|string|false|none|ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.|
|network|string \| null|false|none|Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.|
|network_transaction_id|string \| null|false|none|This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.|
|preferred_locales|[string]|false|none|The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.|
|read_method|string \| null|false|none|How card details were read in this transaction.|
|reader|string|false|none|ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.|
|receipt|[payment_method_details_interac_present_receipt](#schemapayment_method_details_interac_present_receipt) \| null|false|none|A collection of fields required to be displayed on receipts. Only required for EMV transactions.|

|read_method|contactless_emv|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_type|string|false|none|The type of account being debited or credited|
|application_cryptogram|string \| null|false|none|The Application Cryptogram, a unique value generated by the card to authenticate the transaction with issuers.|
|application_preferred_name|string \| null|false|none|The Application Identifier (AID) on the card used to determine which networks are eligible to process the transaction. Referenced from EMV tag 9F12, data encoded on the card's chip.|
|authorization_code|string \| null|false|none|Identifier for this transaction.|
|authorization_response_code|string \| null|false|none|EMV tag 8A. A code returned by the card issuer.|
|cardholder_verification_method|string \| null|false|none|Describes the method used by the cardholder to verify ownership of the card. One of the following: `approval`, `failure`, `none`, `offline_pin`, `offline_pin_and_signature`, `online_pin`, or `signature`.|
|dedicated_file_name|string \| null|false|none|Similar to the application_preferred_name, identifying the applications (AIDs) available on the card. Referenced from EMV tag 84.|
|terminal_verification_results|string \| null|false|none|A 5-byte string that records the checks and validations that occur between the card and the terminal. These checks determine how the terminal processes the transaction and what risk tolerance is acceptable. Referenced from EMV Tag 95.|
|transaction_status_information|string \| null|false|none|An indication of which steps were completed during the card read process. Referenced from EMV Tag 9B.|

<h2 id="tocS_payment_method_domain">payment_method_domain</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="schema_payment_method_domain"></a>

<a id="tocspayment_method_domain"></a>

```json
{
  "amazon_pay": {
    "status": "active",
    "status_details": {
      "error_message": "string"
    }
  },
  "apple_pay": {
    "status": "active",
    "status_details": {
      "error_message": "string"
    }
  },
  "created": 0,
  "domain_name": "string",
  "enabled": true,
  "google_pay": {
    "status": "active",
    "status_details": {
      "error_message": "string"
    }
  },
  "id": "string",
  "klarna": {
    "status": "active",
    "status_details": {
      "error_message": "string"
    }
  },
  "link": {
    "status": "active",
    "status_details": {
      "error_message": "string"
    }
  },
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "payment_method_domain",
  "paypal": {
    "status": "active",
    "status_details": {
      "error_message": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

A payment method domain represents a web domain that you have registered with Stripe.
Stripe Elements use registered payment method domains to control where certain payment methods are shown.

Related guide: [Payment method domains](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/pmd-registration).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amazon_pay|[payment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status](#schemapayment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status)|true|none|Indicates the status of a specific payment method on a payment method domain.|
|apple_pay|[payment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status](#schemapayment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status)|true|none|Indicates the status of a specific payment method on a payment method domain.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|domain_name|string|true|none|The domain name that this payment method domain object represents.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether this payment method domain is enabled. If the domain is not enabled, payment methods that require a payment method domain will not appear in Elements.|
|google_pay|[payment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status](#schemapayment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status)|true|none|Indicates the status of a specific payment method on a payment method domain.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|klarna|[payment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status](#schemapayment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status)|true|none|Indicates the status of a specific payment method on a payment method domain.|
|link|[payment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status](#schemapayment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status)|true|none|Indicates the status of a specific payment method on a payment method domain.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|paypal|[payment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status](#schemapayment_method_domain_resource_payment_method_status)|true|none|Indicates the status of a specific payment method on a payment method domain.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|object|payment_method_domain|

<h2 id="tocS_payment_method_interac_present">payment_method_interac_present</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapayment_method_interac_present"></a>

```json
{
  "brand": "string",
  "cardholder_name": "string",
  "country": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "exp_month": 0,
  "exp_year": 0,
  "fingerprint": "string",
  "funding": "string",
  "issuer": "string",
  "last4": "string",
  "networks": {
    "available": [
      "string"
    ],
    "preferred": "string"
  },
  "preferred_locales": [
    "string"
  ],
  "read_method": "contact_emv"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brand|string \| null|false|none|Card brand. Can be `interac`, `mastercard` or `visa`.|
|cardholder_name|string \| null|false|none|The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.|
|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.|
|exp_month|integer|true|none|Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.|
|exp_year|integer|true|none|Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|
|funding|string \| null|false|none|Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.|
|issuer|string \| null|false|none|The name of the card's issuing bank.|
|last4|string \| null|false|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|networks|[payment_method_card_present_networks](#schemapayment_method_card_present_networks) \| null|false|none|Contains information about card networks that can be used to process the payment.|
|preferred_locales|[string]|false|none|The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.|
|read_method|string \| null|false|none|How card details were read in this transaction.|

|description|string \| null|false|none|A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer.|
|end_date|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|End date of the mandate or subscription. If not provided, the mandate will be active until canceled. If provided, end date should be after start date.|
|interval|string|true|none|Specifies payment frequency. One of `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`, or `sporadic`.|
|interval_count|integer \| null|false|none|The number of intervals between payments. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` indicates one payment every three months. |reference|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the mandate or subscription.|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Start date of the mandate or subscription. Start date should not be lesser than yesterday.|
|supported_types|[string]|false|none|Specifies the type of mandates supported. Possible values are `india`.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|setup_future_usage|none|

|confirmation_number|string \| null|false|none|An optional 10 to 11 digit numeric-only string determining the confirmation code at applicable convenience stores.|

For example, if a PaymentIntent is confirmed with Konbini and `expires_after_days` set to 2 on Monday JST, the instructions will expire on Wednesday 23:59:59 JST.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The timestamp at which the Konbini payment instructions will expire. Only one of `expires_after_days` or `expires_at` may be set.|
|product_description|string \| null|false|none|A product descriptor of up to 22 characters, which will appear to customers at the convenience store.|
|setup_future_usage|string|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. A Payment Record is a resource that allows you to represent payments that occur on- or off-Stripe.
For example, you can create a Payment Record to model a payment made on a different payment processor,
in order to mark an Invoice as paid and a Subscription as active. Payment Records consist of one or
more Payment Attempt Records, which represent individual attempts made on a payment network.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount)|true|none|A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency.|
|amount_authorized|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount)|true|none|A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency.|
|amount_canceled|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount)|true|none|A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency.|
|amount_failed|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount)|true|none|A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency.|
|amount_guaranteed|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount)|true|none|A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency.|
|amount_refunded|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount)|true|none|A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency.|
|amount_requested|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_amount)|true|none|A representation of an amount of money, consisting of an amount and a currency.|
|application|string \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect application that created the PaymentRecord.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer_details|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_customer_details](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_customer_details) \| null|false|none|Customer information for this payment.|
|customer_presence|string \| null|false|none|Indicates whether the customer was present in your checkout flow during this payment.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|latest_payment_attempt_record|string \| null|false|none|ID of the latest Payment Attempt Record attached to this Payment Record.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_method_details|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_payment_method_details](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_payment_method_details) \| null|false|none|Information about the Payment Method debited for this payment.|
|processor_details|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_processor_details](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_processor_details)|true|none|Processor information associated with this payment.|
|reported_by|string|true|none|Indicates who reported the payment.|
|shipping_details|[payments_primitives_payment_records_resource_shipping_details](#schemapayments_primitives_payment_records_resource_shipping_details) \| null|false|none|Shipping information for this payment.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|customer_presence|off_session|
|customer_presence|on_session|
|object|payment_record|
|reported_by|self|
|reported_by|stripe|

Learn about the [differences between accounts](/connect/accounts).|

You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.|

|authentication_flow|string \| null|false|none|For authenticated transactions: Indicates how the issuing bank authenticated the customer.|

|exemption_indicator|string \| null|false|none|The exemption requested via 3DS and accepted by the issuer at authentication time.|
|exemption_indicator_applied|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether Stripe requested the value of `exemption_indicator` in the transaction. This will depend on the outcome of Stripe's internal risk assessment.|
|result|string \| null|false|none|Indicates the outcome of 3D Secure authentication.|
|result_reason|string \| null|false|none|Additional information about why 3D Secure succeeded or failed, based on the `result`.|
|version|string \| null|false|none|The version of 3D Secure that was used.|

Custom Payment Methods represent Payment Method types not modeled directly in
the Stripe API. This resource consists of details about the custom payment method
used for this payment attempt.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|display_name|string|true|none|Display name for the custom (user-defined) payment method type used to make this payment.|
|type|string \| null|false|none|The custom payment method type associated with this payment.|

<h2 id="tocS_payout">payout</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapayout"></a>
<a id="schema_payout"></a>
<a id="tocSpayout"></a>
<a id="tocspayout"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "application_fee": "string",
  "application_fee_amount": 0,
  "arrival_date": 0,
  "automatic": true,
  "balance_transaction": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "destination": "string",
  "failure_balance_transaction": "string",
  "failure_code": "string",
  "failure_message": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "method": "string",
  "object": "payout",
  "original_payout": "string",
  "payout_method": "string",
  "reconciliation_status": "completed",
  "reversed_by": "string",
  "source_type": "string",
  "statement_descriptor": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "trace_id": {
    "status": "string",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "type": "bank_account"
}
```

A `Payout` object is created when you receive funds from Stripe, or when you
initiate a payout to either a bank account or debit card of a [connected
Stripe account](/docs/connect/bank-debit-card-payouts). You can retrieve individual payouts,
and list all payouts. Payouts are made on [varying
schedules](/docs/connect/manage-payout-schedule), depending on your country and
industry.

Related guide: [Receiving payouts](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The amount (in cents (or local equivalent)) that transfers to your bank account or debit card.|
|application_fee|string \| [application_fee](#schemaapplication_fee) \| null|false|none|The application fee (if any) for the payout. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/instant-payouts#monetization-and-fees) for details.|
|application_fee_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount of the application fee (if any) requested for the payout. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/instant-payouts#monetization-and-fees) for details.|
|arrival_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Date that you can expect the payout to arrive in the bank. This factors in delays to account for weekends or bank holidays.|
|automatic|boolean|true|none|Returns `true` if the payout is created by an [automated payout schedule](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts#payout-schedule) and `false` if it's [requested manually](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts#manual-payouts).|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this payout on your account balance.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|destination|string \| [bank_account](#schemabank_account) \| [card](#schemacard) \| [deleted_bank_account](#schemadeleted_bank_account) \| [deleted_card](#schemadeleted_card) \| null|false|none|ID of the bank account or card the payout is sent to.|
|failure_balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|If the payout fails or cancels, this is the ID of the balance transaction that reverses the initial balance transaction and returns the funds from the failed payout back in your balance.|
|failure_code|string \| null|false|none|Error code that provides a reason for a payout failure, if available. View our [list of failure codes](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payout_failures).|
|failure_message|string \| null|false|none|Message that provides the reason for a payout failure, if available.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|method|string|true|none|The method used to send this payout, which can be `standard` or `instant`. `instant` is supported for payouts to debit cards and bank accounts in certain countries. Learn more about [bank support for Instant Payouts](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts/instant-payouts-banks).|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|original_payout|string \| [payout](#schemapayout) \| null|false|none|If the payout reverses another, this is the ID of the original payout.|
|payout_method|string \| null|false|none|ID of the v2 FinancialAccount the funds are sent to.|
|reconciliation_status|string|true|none|If `completed`, you can use the [Balance Transactions API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/balance_transactions/list#balance_transaction_list-payout) to list all balance transactions that are paid out in this payout.|
|reversed_by|string \| [payout](#schemapayout) \| null|false|none|If the payout reverses, this is the ID of the payout that reverses this payout.|
|source_type|string|true|none|The source balance this payout came from, which can be one of the following: `card`, `fpx`, or `bank_account`.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Extra information about a payout that displays on the user's bank statement.|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the payout: `paid`, `pending`, `in_transit`, `canceled` or `failed`. A payout is `pending` until it's submitted to the bank, when it becomes `in_transit`. The status changes to `paid` if the transaction succeeds, or to `failed` or `canceled` (within 5 business days). Some payouts that fail might initially show as `paid`, then change to `failed`.|
|trace_id|[payouts_trace_id](#schemapayouts_trace_id) \| null|false|none|A value that generates from the beneficiary's bank that allows users to track payouts with their bank. Banks might call this a "reference number" or something similar.|
|type|string|true|none|Can be `bank_account` or `card`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|payout|
|reconciliation_status|completed|
|reconciliation_status|in_progress|
|reconciliation_status|not_applicable|
|type|bank_account|
|type|card|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|string|true|none|Possible values are `pending`, `supported`, and `unsupported`. When `payout.status` is `pending` or `in_transit`, this will be `pending`. When the payout transitions to `paid`, `failed`, or `canceled`, this status will become `supported` or `unsupported` shortly after in most cases. In some cases, this may appear as `pending` for up to 10 days after `arrival_date` until transitioning to `supported` or `unsupported`.|
|value|string \| null|false|none|The trace ID value if `trace_id.status` is `supported`, otherwise `nil`.|

This is an object representing a person associated with a Stripe account.

A platform can only access a subset of data in a person for an account where [account.controller.requirement_collection](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection) is `stripe`, which includes Standard and Express accounts, after creating an Account Link or Account Session to start Connect onboarding.

See the [Standard onboarding](/connect/standard-accounts) or [Express onboarding](/connect/express-accounts) documentation for information about prefilling information and account onboarding steps. Learn more about [handling identity verification with the API](/connect/handling-api-verification#person-information).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be resolved by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead. Many alternatives can list the same `original_fields_due`, and any of these alternatives can serve as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields again. Re-providing `original_fields_due` also serves as a pathway for attempting to resolve the fields again.|
|currently_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that need to be resolved to keep the person's account enabled. If not resolved by the account's `future_requirements[current_deadline]`, these fields will transition to the main `requirements` hash, and may immediately become `past_due`, but the account may also be given a grace period depending on the account's enablement state prior to transition.|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|true|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|true|none|Fields you must collect when all thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well, and the account's `future_requirements[current_deadline]` becomes set.|
|past_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that haven't been resolved by the account's `requirements.current_deadline`. These fields need to be resolved to enable the person's account. `future_requirements.past_due` is a subset of `requirements.past_due`.|
|pending_verification|[string]|true|none|Fields that are being reviewed, or might become required depending on the results of a review. If the review fails, these fields can move to `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives`. Fields might appear in `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives` and in `pending_verification` if one verification fails but another is still pending.|
