<h2 id="tocS_plan">plan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaplan"></a>
<a id="schema_plan"></a>
<a id="tocSplan"></a>
<a id="tocsplan"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "amount": 0,
  "amount_decimal": "string",
  "billing_scheme": "per_unit",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "interval": "day",
  "interval_count": 0,
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "meter": "string",
  "nickname": "string",
  "object": "plan",
  "product": "string",
  "tiers": [
    {
      "flat_amount": 0,
      "flat_amount_decimal": "string",
      "unit_amount": 0,
      "unit_amount_decimal": "string",
      "up_to": 0
    }
  ],
  "tiers_mode": "graduated",
  "transform_usage": {
    "divide_by": 0,
    "round": "down"
  },
  "trial_period_days": 0,
  "usage_type": "licensed"
}
```

You can now model subscriptions more flexibly using the [Prices API](https://docs.stripe.com/api#prices). It replaces the Plans API and is backwards compatible to simplify your migration.

Plans define the base price, currency, and billing cycle for recurring purchases of products.
[Products](https://docs.stripe.com/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and plans help you track pricing. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by plans. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme.

For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has plans for $10/month, $100/year, €9/month, and €90/year.

Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription) and more about [products and prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/overview).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the plan can be used for new purchases.|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|
|amount_decimal|string(decimal) \| null|false|none|The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|
|billing_scheme|string|true|none|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `amount`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for plans with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for plans with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|interval|string|true|none|The frequency at which a subscription is billed. One of `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`.|
|interval_count|integer|true|none|The number of intervals (specified in the `interval` attribute) between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|meter|string \| null|false|none|The meter tracking the usage of a metered price|
|nickname|string \| null|false|none|A brief description of the plan, hidden from customers.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|product|string \| [product](#schemaproduct) \| [deleted_product](#schemadeleted_product) \| null|false|none|The product whose pricing this plan determines.|
|tiers|[[plan_tier](#schemaplan_tier)]|false|none|Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`.|
|tiers_mode|string \| null|false|none|Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price. In `graduated` tiering, pricing can change as the quantity grows.|
|transform_usage|[transform_usage](#schematransform_usage) \| null|false|none|Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the amount billed. Cannot be combined with `tiers`.|
|trial_period_days|integer \| null|false|none|Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this plan using [`trial_from_plan=true`](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_subscription-trial_from_plan).|
|usage_type|string|true|none|Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`.|

|billing_scheme|tiered|
|interval|day|
|interval|month|
|interval|week|
|interval|year|
|object|plan|
|tiers_mode|graduated|
|tiers_mode|volume|
|usage_type|licensed|
|usage_type|metered|

<h2 id="tocS_portal_subscription_update">portal_subscription_update</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaportal_subscription_update"></a>
<a id="schema_portal_subscription_update"></a>
<a id="tocSportal_subscription_update"></a>
<a id="tocsportal_subscription_update"></a>

```json
{
  "billing_cycle_anchor": "now",
  "default_allowed_updates": [
    "price"
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "products": [
    {
      "adjustable_quantity": {
        "enabled": true,
        "maximum": 0,
        "minimum": 0
      },
      "prices": [
        "string"
      ],
      "product": "string"
    }
  ],
  "proration_behavior": "always_invoice",
  "schedule_at_period_end": {
    "conditions": [
      {
        "type": "decreasing_item_amount"
      }
    ]
  },
  "trial_update_behavior": "continue_trial"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|billing_cycle_anchor|string \| null|false|none|Determines the value to use for the billing cycle anchor on subscription updates. Valid values are `now` or `unchanged`, and the default value is `unchanged`. Setting the value to `now` resets the subscription's billing cycle anchor to the current time (in UTC). For more information, see the billing cycle [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/billing-cycle).|
|default_allowed_updates|[string]|true|none|The types of subscription updates that are supported for items listed in the `products` attribute. When empty, subscriptions are not updateable.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the feature is enabled.|
|products|[[portal_subscription_update_product](#schemaportal_subscription_update_product)]|false|none|The list of up to 10 products that support subscription updates.|
|proration_behavior|string|true|none|Determines how to handle prorations resulting from subscription updates. Valid values are `none`, `create_prorations`, and `always_invoice`. Defaults to a value of `none` if you don't set it during creation.|
|schedule_at_period_end|[portal_resource_schedule_update_at_period_end](#schemaportal_resource_schedule_update_at_period_end)|true|none|none|
|trial_update_behavior|string|true|none|Determines how handle updates to trialing subscriptions. Valid values are `end_trial` and `continue_trial`. Defaults to a value of `end_trial` if you don't set it during creation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|billing_cycle_anchor|now|
|billing_cycle_anchor|unchanged|
|default_allowed_updates|price|
|default_allowed_updates|promotion_code|
|default_allowed_updates|quantity|
|proration_behavior|always_invoice|
|proration_behavior|create_prorations|
|proration_behavior|none|
|trial_update_behavior|continue_trial|
|trial_update_behavior|end_trial|

<h2 id="tocS_price">price</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprice"></a>
<a id="schema_price"></a>
<a id="tocSprice"></a>
<a id="tocsprice"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "billing_scheme": "per_unit",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "currency_options": {
    "property1": {
      "custom_unit_amount": {
        "maximum": 0,
        "minimum": 0,
        "preset": 0
      },
      "tax_behavior": "exclusive",
      "tiers": [
        {
          "flat_amount": 0,
          "flat_amount_decimal": "string",
          "unit_amount": 0,
          "unit_amount_decimal": "string",
          "up_to": 0
        }
      ],
      "unit_amount": 0,
      "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
    },
    "property2": {
      "custom_unit_amount": {
        "maximum": 0,
        "minimum": 0,
        "preset": 0
      },
      "tax_behavior": "exclusive",
      "tiers": [
        {
          "flat_amount": 0,
          "flat_amount_decimal": "string",
          "unit_amount": 0,
          "unit_amount_decimal": "string",
          "up_to": 0
        }
      ],
      "unit_amount": 0,
      "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
    }
  },
  "custom_unit_amount": {
    "maximum": 0,
    "minimum": 0,
    "preset": 0
  },
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "lookup_key": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "nickname": "string",
  "object": "price",
  "product": "string",
  "recurring": {
    "interval": "day",
    "interval_count": 0,
    "meter": "string",
    "usage_type": "licensed"
  },
  "tax_behavior": "exclusive",
  "tiers": [
    {
      "flat_amount": 0,
      "flat_amount_decimal": "string",
      "unit_amount": 0,
      "unit_amount_decimal": "string",
      "up_to": 0
    }
  ],
  "tiers_mode": "graduated",
  "transform_quantity": {
    "divide_by": 0,
    "round": "down"
  },
  "type": "one_time",
  "unit_amount": 0,
  "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
}
```

Prices define the unit cost, currency, and (optional) billing cycle for both recurring and one-time purchases of products.
[Products](https://docs.stripe.com/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and prices help you track payment terms. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by prices. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme.

For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has prices for $10/month, $100/year, and €9 once.

Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription), [create an invoice](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/create), and more about [products and prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/overview).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the price can be used for new purchases.|
|billing_scheme|string|true|none|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `unit_amount` or `unit_amount_decimal`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for prices with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for prices with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|currency_options|object|false|none|Prices defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|custom_unit_amount|[custom_unit_amount](#schemacustom_unit_amount) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration for the amount to be adjusted by the customer during Checkout Sessions and Payment Links.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|lookup_key|string \| null|false|none|A lookup key used to retrieve prices dynamically from a static string. This may be up to 200 characters.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|nickname|string \| null|false|none|A brief description of the price, hidden from customers.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|product|string \| [product](#schemaproduct) \| [deleted_product](#schemadeleted_product)|true|none|The ID of the product this price is associated with.|
|recurring|[recurring](#schemarecurring) \| null|false|none|The recurring components of a price such as `interval` and `usage_type`.|
|tax_behavior|string \| null|false|none|Only required if a [default tax behavior](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/products-prices-tax-categories-tax-behavior#setting-a-default-tax-behavior-(recommended)) was not provided in the Stripe Tax settings. Specifies whether the price is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`. Once specified as either `inclusive` or `exclusive`, it cannot be changed.|
|tiers|[[price_tier](#schemaprice_tier)]|false|none|Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`.|
|tiers_mode|string \| null|false|none|Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price. In `graduated` tiering, pricing can change as the quantity grows.|
|transform_quantity|[transform_quantity](#schematransform_quantity) \| null|false|none|Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the amount billed. Cannot be combined with `tiers`.|
|type|string|true|none|One of `one_time` or `recurring` depending on whether the price is for a one-time purchase or a recurring (subscription) purchase.|
|unit_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|
|unit_amount_decimal|string(decimal) \| null|false|none|The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|billing_scheme|per_unit|
|billing_scheme|tiered|
|object|price|
|tax_behavior|exclusive|
|tax_behavior|inclusive|
|tax_behavior|unspecified|
|tiers_mode|graduated|
|tiers_mode|volume|
|type|one_time|
|type|recurring|

<h2 id="tocS_product">product</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaproduct"></a>
<a id="schema_product"></a>
<a id="tocSproduct"></a>
<a id="tocsproduct"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "created": 0,
  "default_price": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "images": [
    "string"
  ],
  "livemode": true,
  "marketing_features": [
    {
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "object": "product",
  "package_dimensions": {
    "height": 0,
    "length": 0,
    "weight": 0,
    "width": 0
  },
  "shippable": true,
  "statement_descriptor": "string",
  "tax_code": "string",
  "tax_details": {
    "performance_location": "string",
    "tax_code": "string"
  },
  "unit_label": "string",
  "updated": 0,
  "url": "string"
}
```

Products describe the specific goods or services you offer to your customers.
For example, you might offer a Standard and Premium version of your goods or service; each version would be a separate Product.
They can be used in conjunction with [Prices](https://docs.stripe.com/api#prices) to configure pricing in Payment Links, Checkout, and Subscriptions.

Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription),
[share a Payment Link](https://docs.stripe.com/payment-links),
[accept payments with Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment#create-product-prices-upfront),
and more about [Products and Prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/overview)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the product is currently available for purchase.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|default_price|string \| [price](#schemaprice) \| null|false|none|The ID of the [Price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices) object that is the default price for this product.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The product's description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store a long form explanation of the product being sold for your own rendering purposes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|images|[string]|true|none|A list of up to 8 URLs of images for this product, meant to be displayable to the customer.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|marketing_features|[[product_marketing_feature](#schemaproduct_marketing_feature)]|true|none|A list of up to 15 marketing features for this product. These are displayed in [pricing tables](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/pricing-table).|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string|true|none|The product's name, meant to be displayable to the customer.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|package_dimensions|[package_dimensions](#schemapackage_dimensions) \| null|false|none|The dimensions of this product for shipping purposes.|
|shippable|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this product is shipped (i.e., physical goods).|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Extra information about a product which will appear on your customer's credit card statement. In the case that multiple products are billed at once, the first statement descriptor will be used. Only used for subscription payments.|
|tax_code|string \| [tax_code](#schematax_code) \| null|false|none|A [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-categories) ID.|
|tax_details|[tax_product_tax_details_resource_tax_details](#schematax_product_tax_details_resource_tax_details) \| null|false|none|Tax details for this product, including the [tax code](/tax/tax-codes) and an optional performance location.|
|unit_label|string \| null|false|none|A label that represents units of this product. When set, this will be included in customers' receipts, invoices, Checkout, and the customer portal.|
|updated|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|A URL of a publicly-accessible webpage for this product.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|product|

<h2 id="tocS_product_catalog.trial_offer">product_catalog.trial_offer</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaproduct_catalog.trial_offer"></a>
<a id="schema_product_catalog.trial_offer"></a>
<a id="tocSproduct_catalog.trial_offer"></a>
<a id="tocsproduct_catalog.trial_offer"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "duration": {
    "relative": {
      "iterations": 0
    },
    "type": "relative"
  },
  "end_behavior": {
    "transition": {
      "price": "string"
    },
    "type": "transition"
  },
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "nickname": "string",
  "object": "product_catalog.trial_offer",
  "price": "string"
}
```

Trial offers let you define free or paid introductory pricing for a subscription item.
A TrialOffer specifies the price to charge during the trial, how many billing intervals
the trial lasts, and what price the subscription item transitions to when the trial ends.
You attach a TrialOffer to a subscription item
using `items[current_trial][trial_offer]` when creating or updating a subscription.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the trial offer is active. Set to false to archive the trial offer.|
|duration|[product_catalog_impl_endpoints_trial_offer_resource_trial_offer_duration](#schemaproduct_catalog_impl_endpoints_trial_offer_resource_trial_offer_duration)|true|none|none|
|end_behavior|[product_catalog_impl_endpoints_trial_offer_resource_trial_offer_end_behavior](#schemaproduct_catalog_impl_endpoints_trial_offer_resource_trial_offer_end_behavior)|true|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|nickname|string \| null|false|none|A brief description of the trial offer, hidden from customers.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|price|string \| [price](#schemaprice) \| [deleted_price](#schemadeleted_price)|true|none|The price during the trial offer.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|product_catalog.trial_offer|

<h2 id="tocS_product_feature">product_feature</h2>

<a id="schemaproduct_feature"></a>

```json
    "active": true,
    "id": "string",
    "livemode": true,
    "lookup_key": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "object": "entitlements.feature"
  },
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "product_feature"
}
```

A product_feature represents an attachment between a feature and a product.
When a product is purchased that has a feature attached, Stripe will create an entitlement to the feature for the purchasing customer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|entitlement_feature|[entitlements.feature](#schemaentitlements.feature)|true|none|A feature represents a monetizable ability or functionality in your system.<br>Features can be assigned to products, and when those products are purchased, Stripe will create an entitlement to the feature for the purchasing customer.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|product_feature|

<h2 id="tocS_promotion_code">promotion_code</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapromotion_code"></a>
<a id="schema_promotion_code"></a>
<a id="tocSpromotion_code"></a>
<a id="tocspromotion_code"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "code": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "customer": "string",
  "customer_account": "string",
  "expires_at": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "max_redemptions": 0,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "promotion_code",
  "promotion": {
    "coupon": "string",
    "type": "coupon"
  },
  "restrictions": {
    "currency_options": {
      "property1": {
        "minimum_amount": 0
      },
      "property2": {
        "minimum_amount": 0
      }
    },
    "first_time_transaction": true,
    "minimum_amount": 0,
    "minimum_amount_currency": "string"
  },
  "times_redeemed": 0
}
```

A Promotion Code represents a customer-redeemable code for an underlying promotion.
You can create multiple codes for a single promotion.

If you enable promotion codes in your [customer portal configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/customer-management/configure-portal), then customers can redeem a code themselves when updating a subscription in the portal.
Customers can also view the currently active promotion codes and coupons on each of their subscriptions in the portal.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the promotion code is currently active. A promotion code is only active if the coupon is also valid.|
|code|string|true|none|The customer-facing code. Regardless of case, this code must be unique across all active promotion codes for each customer. Valid characters are lower case letters (a-z), upper case letters (A-Z), digits (0-9), and dashes (-).|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The customer who can use this promotion code.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|The account representing the customer who can use this promotion code.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date at which the promotion code can no longer be redeemed.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|max_redemptions|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of times this promotion code can be redeemed.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|promotion|[promotion_codes_resource_promotion](#schemapromotion_codes_resource_promotion)|true|none|none|
|restrictions|[promotion_codes_resource_restrictions](#schemapromotion_codes_resource_restrictions)|true|none|none|
|times_redeemed|integer|true|none|Number of times this promotion code has been used.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|promotion_code|

A Quote is a way to model prices that you'd like to provide to a customer.
Once accepted, it will automatically create an invoice, subscription or subscription schedule.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_subtotal|integer|true|none|Total before any discounts or taxes are applied.|
|amount_total|integer|true|none|Total after discounts and taxes are applied.|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect Application that created the quote.|
|application_fee_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. Only applicable if there are no line items with recurring prices on the quote.|
|application_fee_percent|number \| null|false|none|A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. Only applicable if there are line items with recurring prices on the quote.|
|automatic_tax|[quotes_resource_automatic_tax](#schemaquotes_resource_automatic_tax)|true|none|none|
|collection_method|string|true|none|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay invoices at the end of the subscription cycle or on finalization using the default payment method attached to the subscription or customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`. Defaults to `charge_automatically`.|
|computed|[quotes_resource_computed](#schemaquotes_resource_computed)|true|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The customer who received this quote. A customer is required to finalize the quote. Once specified, you can't change it.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|The account representing the customer who received this quote. A customer or account is required to finalize the quote. Once specified, you can't change it.|
|default_tax_rates|[string \| [tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The tax rates applied to this quote.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|A description that will be displayed on the quote PDF.|
|discounts|[string \| [discount](#schemadiscount)]|true|none|The discounts applied to this quote.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The date on which the quote will be canceled if in `open` or `draft` status. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|footer|string \| null|false|none|A footer that will be displayed on the quote PDF.|
|from_quote|[quotes_resource_from_quote](#schemaquotes_resource_from_quote) \| null|false|none|Details of the quote that was cloned. See the [cloning documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/quotes/clone) for more details.|
|header|string \| null|false|none|A header that will be displayed on the quote PDF.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice) \| [deleted_invoice](#schemadeleted_invoice) \| null|false|none|The invoice that was created from this quote.|
|invoice_settings|[invoice_setting_quote_setting](#schemainvoice_setting_quote_setting)|true|none|none|
|line_items|object|false|none|A list of items the customer is being quoted for.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|number|string \| null|false|none|A unique number that identifies this particular quote. This number is assigned once the quote is [finalized](https://docs.stripe.com/quotes/overview#finalize).|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account on behalf of which to charge. See the [Connect documentation](https://support.stripe.com/questions/sending-invoices-on-behalf-of-connected-accounts) for details.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the quote.|
|status_transitions|[quotes_resource_status_transitions](#schemaquotes_resource_status_transitions)|true|none|none|
|subscription|string \| [subscription](#schemasubscription) \| null|false|none|The subscription that was created or updated from this quote.|
|subscription_data|[quotes_resource_subscription_data_subscription_data](#schemaquotes_resource_subscription_data_subscription_data)|true|none|none|
|subscription_schedule|string \| [subscription_schedule](#schemasubscription_schedule) \| null|false|none|The subscription schedule that was created or updated from this quote.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this quote belongs to.|
|total_details|[quotes_resource_total_details](#schemaquotes_resource_total_details)|true|none|none|
|transfer_data|[quotes_resource_transfer_data](#schemaquotes_resource_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the payments will be attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from each payment will be transferred to for each of the invoices.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|collection_method|charge_automatically|
|collection_method|send_invoice|
|object|quote|
|status|accepted|
|status|canceled|
|status|draft|
|status|open|

<h2 id="tocS_radar.early_fraud_warning">radar.early_fraud_warning</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaradar.early_fraud_warning"></a>
<a id="schema_radar.early_fraud_warning"></a>

```json
{
  "actionable": true,
  "charge": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "fraud_type": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "radar.early_fraud_warning",
  "payment_intent": "string"
}
```

An early fraud warning indicates that the card issuer has notified us that a
charge may be fraudulent.

Related guide: [Early fraud warnings](https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/measuring#early-fraud-warnings)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actionable|boolean|true|none|An EFW is actionable if it has not received a dispute and has not been fully refunded. You may wish to proactively refund a charge that receives an EFW, in order to avoid receiving a dispute later.|
|charge|string \| [charge](#schemacharge)|true|none|ID of the charge this early fraud warning is for, optionally expanded.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|fraud_type|string|true|none|The type of fraud labelled by the issuer. One of `card_never_received`, `fraudulent_card_application`, `made_with_counterfeit_card`, `made_with_lost_card`, `made_with_stolen_card`, `misc`, `unauthorized_use_of_card`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|false|none|ID of the Payment Intent this early fraud warning is for, optionally expanded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|radar.early_fraud_warning|

It includes the Radar risk score from Stripe, payment outcome taken by the merchant or processor, and any post transaction events, such as refunds or disputes. See the [Radar API guide](/radar/multiprocessor) for integration steps.

|customer_details|[insights_resources_payment_evaluation_customer_details](#schemainsights_resources_payment_evaluation_customer_details)|false|none|Customer details attached to this payment evaluation.|
|events|[[insights_resources_payment_evaluation_event](#schemainsights_resources_payment_evaluation_event)]|true|none|Event information associated with the payment evaluation, such as refunds, dispute, early fraud warnings, or user interventions.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|outcome|[insights_resources_payment_evaluation_outcome](#schemainsights_resources_payment_evaluation_outcome) \| null|false|none|Indicates the final outcome for the payment evaluation.|
|payment_details|[insights_resources_payment_evaluation_payment_details](#schemainsights_resources_payment_evaluation_payment_details)|false|none|Payment details attached to this payment evaluation.|
|recommended_action|string|true|none|Recommended action based on the score of the `fraudulent_payment` signal. Possible values are `block`, `continue` and `request_three_d_secure`.|
|signals|[insights_resources_payment_evaluation_signals](#schemainsights_resources_payment_evaluation_signals)|true|none|Collection of signals for this payment evaluation.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|radar.payment_evaluation|
|recommended_action|block|
|recommended_action|continue|

### Properties

|interval_count|integer|true|none|The number of intervals (specified in the `interval` attribute) between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months.|
|meter|string \| null|false|none|The meter tracking the usage of a metered price|
|usage_type|string|true|none|Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`.|

|interval|month|

|interval|year|

Refund objects allow you to refund a previously created charge that isn't
refunded yet. Funds are refunded to the credit or debit card that's
initially charged.

Related guide: [Refunds](https://docs.stripe.com/refunds)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount, in cents (or local equivalent).|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.|
|charge|string \| [charge](#schemacharge) \| null|false|none|ID of the charge that's refunded.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|ID of the customer of this refund.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|ID of the account of this refund.|
|description|string|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. You can use this for displaying to users (available on non-card refunds only).|
|destination_details|[refund_destination_details](#schemarefund_destination_details)|false|none|none|
|failure_balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction)|false|none|After the refund fails, this balance transaction describes the adjustment made on your account balance that reverses the initial balance transaction.|
|failure_reason|string|false|none|Provides the reason for the refund failure. Possible values are: `lost_or_stolen_card`, `expired_or_canceled_card`, `charge_for_pending_refund_disputed`, `insufficient_funds`, `declined`, `merchant_request`, or `unknown`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|instructions_email|string|false|none|For payment methods without native refund support (for example, Konbini, PromptPay), provide an email address for the customer to receive refund instructions.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|next_action|[refund_next_action](#schemarefund_next_action)|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent) \| null|false|none|ID of the PaymentIntent that's refunded.|
|payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the payment method associated with this refund.|
|pending_reason|string|false|none|Provides the reason for why the refund is pending. Possible values are: `processing`, `insufficient_funds`, or `charge_pending`.|
|presentment_details|[payment_flows_payment_intent_presentment_details](#schemapayment_flows_payment_intent_presentment_details)|false|none|none|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for the refund, which is either user-provided (`duplicate`, `fraudulent`, or `requested_by_customer`) or generated by Stripe internally (`expired_uncaptured_charge`).|
|receipt_number|string \| null|false|none|This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this refund.|
|source_transfer_reversal|string \| [transfer_reversal](#schematransfer_reversal) \| null|false|none|The transfer reversal that's associated with the refund. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|Status of the refund. This can be `pending`, `requires_action`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `canceled`. Learn more about [failed refunds](https://docs.stripe.com/refunds#failed-refunds).|
|transfer_reversal|string \| [transfer_reversal](#schematransfer_reversal) \| null|false|none|This refers to the transfer reversal object if the accompanying transfer reverses. This is only applicable if the charge was created using the destination parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|refund|
|pending_reason|charge_pending|
|pending_reason|insufficient_funds|
|pending_reason|processing|
|reason|duplicate|
|reason|expired_uncaptured_charge|
|reason|fraudulent|
|reason|requested_by_customer|

<h2 id="tocS_reporting.report_run">reporting.report_run</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareporting.report_run"></a>
<a id="schema_reporting.report_run"></a>
<a id="tocSreporting.report_run"></a>
<a id="tocsreporting.report_run"></a>

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "error": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "reporting.report_run",
  "parameters": {
    "columns": [
      "string"
    ],
    "connected_account": "string",
    "currency": "string",
    "interval_end": 0,
    "interval_start": 0,
    "payout": "string",
    "reporting_category": "string",
    "timezone": "string"
  },
  "report_type": "string",
  "result": {
    "created": 0,
    "expires_at": 0,
    "filename": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "links": {
      "data": [
        {}
      ],
      "has_more": true,
      "object": "list",
      "url": "string"
    },
    "object": "file",
    "purpose": "account_requirement",
    "size": 0,
    "title": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "url": "string"
  },
  "status": "string",
  "succeeded_at": 0
}
```

The Report Run object represents an instance of a report type generated with
specific run parameters. Once the object is created, Stripe begins processing the report.
When the report has finished running, it will give you a reference to a file
where you can retrieve your results. For an overview, see
[API Access to Reports](https://docs.stripe.com/reporting/statements/api).

Note that certain report types can only be run based on your live-mode data (not test-mode
data), and will error when queried without a [live-mode API key](https://docs.stripe.com/keys#test-live-modes).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|error|string \| null|false|none|If something should go wrong during the run, a message about the failure (populated when<br> `status=failed`).|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|`true` if the report is run on live mode data and `false` if it is run on test mode data.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|parameters|[financial_reporting_finance_report_run_run_parameters](#schemafinancial_reporting_finance_report_run_run_parameters)|true|none|none|
|report_type|string|true|none|The ID of the [report type](https://docs.stripe.com/reports/report-types) to run, such as `"balance.summary.1"`.|
|result|[file](#schemafile) \| null|false|none|The file object representing the result of the report run (populated when<br> `status=succeeded`).|
|status|string|true|none|Status of this report run. This will be `pending` when the run is initially created.<br> When the run finishes, this will be set to `succeeded` and the `result` field will be populated.<br> Rarely, we may encounter an error, at which point this will be set to `failed` and the `error` field will be populated.|
|succeeded_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp at which this run successfully finished (populated when<br> `status=succeeded`). Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|reporting.report_run|

<h2 id="tocS_reporting.report_type">reporting.report_type</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareporting.report_type"></a>
<a id="schema_reporting.report_type"></a>
<a id="tocSreporting.report_type"></a>
<a id="tocsreporting.report_type"></a>

```json
{
  "data_available_end": 0,
  "data_available_start": 0,
  "default_columns": [
    "string"
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "name": "string",
  "object": "reporting.report_type",
  "updated": 0,
  "version": 0
}
```

The Report Type resource corresponds to a particular type of report, such as
the "Activity summary" or "Itemized payouts" reports. These objects are
identified by an ID belonging to a set of enumerated values. See
[API Access to Reports documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/reporting/statements/api)
for those Report Type IDs, along with required and optional parameters.

Note that certain report types can only be run based on your live-mode data (not test-mode
data), and will error when queried without a [live-mode API key](https://docs.stripe.com/keys#test-live-modes).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_available_end|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Most recent time for which this Report Type is available. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|data_available_start|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Earliest time for which this Report Type is available. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|default_columns|[string]|false|none|List of column names that are included by default when this Report Type gets run. (If the Report Type doesn't support the `columns` parameter, this will be null.)|
|id|string|true|none|The [ID of the Report Type](https://docs.stripe.com/reporting/statements/api#available-report-types), such as `balance.summary.1`.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable name of the Report Type|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|updated|integer(unix-time)|true|none|When this Report Type was latest updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|version|integer|true|none|Version of the Report Type. Different versions report with the same ID will have the same purpose, but may take different run parameters or have different result schemas.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|reporting.report_type|

Learn more about [Radar](/radar) and reviewing payments

|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|

Note that this information is an approximation and attempts to locate the nearest population center - it should not be used to determine a specific address.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|open|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the review needs action.|
|opened_reason|string|true|none|The reason the review was opened. One of `rule` or `manual`.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|false|none|The PaymentIntent ID associated with this review, if one exists.|
|reason|string|true|none|The reason the review is currently open or closed. One of `rule`, `manual`, `approved`, `refunded`, `refunded_as_fraud`, `disputed`, `redacted`, `canceled`, `payment_never_settled`, or `acknowledged`.|
|session|[radar_review_resource_session](#schemaradar_review_resource_session) \| null|false|none|Information related to the browsing session of the user who initiated the payment.|

A SetupAttempt describes one attempted confirmation of a SetupIntent,
whether that confirmation is successful or unsuccessful. You can use
SetupAttempts to inspect details of a specific attempt at setting up a
payment method using a SetupIntent.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| null|false|none|The value of [application](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-application) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation.|
|attach_to_self|boolean|false|none|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The value of [customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-customer) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|The value of [customer_account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-customer_account) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation.|
|flow_directions|[string]|false|none|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The value of [on_behalf_of](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-on_behalf_of) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation.|
|payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method)|true|none|ID of the payment method used with this SetupAttempt.|
|payment_method_details|[setup_attempt_payment_method_details](#schemasetup_attempt_payment_method_details)|true|none|none|
|setup_error|[api_errors](#schemaapi_errors) \| null|false|none|The error encountered during this attempt to confirm the SetupIntent, if any.|
|setup_intent|string \| [setup_intent](#schemasetup_intent)|true|none|ID of the SetupIntent that this attempt belongs to.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of this SetupAttempt, one of `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `abandoned`.|
|usage|string|true|none|The value of [usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-usage) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation, one of `off_session` or `on_session`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|flow_directions|inbound|
|flow_directions|outbound|
|object|setup_attempt|

|exp_year|integer \| null|false|none|Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|
|funding|string \| null|false|none|Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.|
|last4|string \| null|false|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|network|string \| null|false|none|Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.|
|three_d_secure|[three_d_secure_details](#schemathree_d_secure_details) \| null|false|none|Populated if this authorization used 3D Secure authentication.|
|wallet|[setup_attempt_payment_method_details_card_wallet](#schemasetup_attempt_payment_method_details_card_wallet) \| null|false|none|If this Card is part of a card wallet, this contains the details of the card wallet.|

A SetupIntent guides you through the process of setting up and saving a customer's payment credentials for future payments.
For example, you can use a SetupIntent to set up and save your customer's card without immediately collecting a payment.
Later, you can use [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intents) to drive the payment flow.

Create a SetupIntent when you're ready to collect your customer's payment credentials.
Don't maintain long-lived, unconfirmed SetupIntents because they might not be valid.
The SetupIntent transitions through multiple [statuses](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses) as it guides
you through the setup process.

Successful SetupIntents result in payment credentials that are optimized for future payments.
For example, cardholders in [certain regions](https://stripe.com/guides/strong-customer-authentication) might need to be run through
[Strong Customer Authentication](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication) during payment method collection
to streamline later [off-session payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/setup-intents).
If you use the SetupIntent with a [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#setup_intent_object-customer),
it automatically attaches the resulting payment method to that Customer after successful setup.
We recommend using SetupIntents or [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) on
PaymentIntents to save payment methods to prevent saving invalid or unoptimized payment methods.

By using SetupIntents, you can reduce friction for your customers, even as regulations change over time.

Related guide: [Setup Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/setup-intents)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_payment_method_types|[string]|false|none|The list of payment method types to allow for this SetupIntent. Stripe will only use methods in this list when determining the payment methods to offer.|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect application that created the SetupIntent.|
|attach_to_self|boolean|false|none|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|automatic_payment_methods|[payment_flows_automatic_payment_methods_setup_intent](#schemapayment_flows_automatic_payment_methods_setup_intent) \| null|false|none|Settings for dynamic payment methods compatible with this Setup Intent|
|cancellation_reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for cancellation of this SetupIntent, one of `abandoned`, `requested_by_customer`, or `duplicate`.|
|client_secret|string \| null|false|none|The client secret of this SetupIntent. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key.<br><br>The client secret can be used to complete payment setup from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the customer. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|ID of the Account this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Account on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Accounts cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|excluded_payment_method_types|[string]|false|none|Payment method types that are excluded from this SetupIntent.|
|flow_directions|[string]|false|none|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|last_setup_error|[api_errors](#schemaapi_errors) \| null|false|none|The error encountered in the previous SetupIntent confirmation.|
|latest_attempt|string \| [setup_attempt](#schemasetup_attempt) \| null|false|none|The most recent SetupAttempt for this SetupIntent.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|managed_payments|[smor_resource_managed_payments](#schemasmor_resource_managed_payments) \| null|false|none|none|
|mandate|string \| [mandate](#schemamandate) \| null|false|none|ID of the multi use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|next_action|[setup_intent_next_action](#schemasetup_intent_next_action) \| null|false|none|If present, this property tells you what actions you need to take in order for your customer to continue payment setup.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) for which the setup is intended.|
|payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the payment method used with this SetupIntent. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then the [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_attempts/object#setup_attempt_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) associated with the `latest_attempt` is attached to the Customer instead.|
|payment_method_configuration_details|[payment_method_config_biz_payment_method_configuration_details](#schemapayment_method_config_biz_payment_method_configuration_details) \| null|false|none|Information about the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) used for this Setup Intent.|
|payment_method_options|[setup_intent_payment_method_options](#schemasetup_intent_payment_method_options) \| null|false|none|Payment method-specific configuration for this SetupIntent.|
|payment_method_types|[string]|true|none|The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this SetupIntent is allowed to set up. A list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).|
|single_use_mandate|string \| [mandate](#schemamandate) \| null|false|none|ID of the single_use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.|
|status|string|true|none|[Status](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses) of this SetupIntent, one of `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`.|
|usage|string|true|none|Indicates how the payment method is intended to be used in the future.<br><br>Use `on_session` if you intend to only reuse the payment method when the customer is in your checkout flow. Use `off_session` if your customer may or may not be in your checkout flow. If not provided, this value defaults to `off_session`.|

```json
    },
```

```json
    "amount": 0,
```

```json
}
```

Shipping rates describe the price of shipping presented to your customers and
applied to a purchase. For more information, see [Charge for shipping](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/during-payment/charge-shipping).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the shipping rate can be used for new purchases. Defaults to `true`.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|delivery_estimate|[shipping_rate_delivery_estimate](#schemashipping_rate_delivery_estimate) \| null|false|none|The estimated range for how long shipping will take, meant to be displayable to the customer. This will appear on CheckoutSessions.|
|display_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the shipping rate, meant to be displayable to the customer. This will appear on CheckoutSessions.|
|fixed_amount|[shipping_rate_fixed_amount](#schemashipping_rate_fixed_amount)|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|tax_behavior|string \| null|false|none|Specifies whether the rate is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`.|
|tax_code|string \| [tax_code](#schematax_code) \| null|false|none|A [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-categories) ID. The Shipping tax code is `txcd_92010001`.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of calculation to use on the shipping rate.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|shipping_rate|
|tax_behavior|exclusive|
|tax_behavior|inclusive|
|tax_behavior|unspecified|

`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They
represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API
just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be
attached to customers.

Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources).
We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods).
This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.

Related guides: [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/customers).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ach_credit_transfer|[source_type_ach_credit_transfer](#schemasource_type_ach_credit_transfer)|false|none|none|
|ach_debit|[source_type_ach_debit](#schemasource_type_ach_debit)|false|none|none|
|acss_debit|[source_type_acss_debit](#schemasource_type_acss_debit)|false|none|none|
|alipay|[source_type_alipay](#schemasource_type_alipay)|false|none|none|
|allow_redisplay|string \| null|false|none|This field indicates whether this payment method can be shown again to its customer in a checkout flow. Stripe products such as Checkout and Elements use this field to determine whether a payment method can be shown as a saved payment method in a checkout flow. The field defaults to “unspecified”.|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|A positive integer in the smallest currency unit (that is, 100 cents for $1.00, or 1 for ¥1, Japanese Yen being a zero-decimal currency) representing the total amount associated with the source. This is the amount for which the source will be chargeable once ready. Required for `single_use` sources.|
|au_becs_debit|[source_type_au_becs_debit](#schemasource_type_au_becs_debit)|false|none|none|
|bancontact|[source_type_bancontact](#schemasource_type_bancontact)|false|none|none|
|card|[source_type_card](#schemasource_type_card)|false|none|none|
|card_present|[source_type_card_present](#schemasource_type_card_present)|false|none|none|
|client_secret|string|true|none|The client secret of the source. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key.|
|code_verification|[source_code_verification_flow](#schemasource_code_verification_flow)|false|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency) \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) associated with the source. This is the currency for which the source will be chargeable once ready. Required for `single_use` sources.|
|customer|string|false|none|The ID of the customer to which this source is attached. This will not be present when the source has not been attached to a customer.|
|eps|[source_type_eps](#schemasource_type_eps)|false|none|none|
|flow|string|true|none|The authentication `flow` of the source. `flow` is one of `redirect`, `receiver`, `code_verification`, `none`.|
|giropay|[source_type_giropay](#schemasource_type_giropay)|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|ideal|[source_type_ideal](#schemasource_type_ideal)|false|none|none|
|klarna|[source_type_klarna](#schemasource_type_klarna)|false|none|none|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|multibanco|[source_type_multibanco](#schemasource_type_multibanco)|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|owner|[source_owner](#schemasource_owner) \| null|false|none|Information about the owner of the payment instrument that may be used or required by particular source types.|
|p24|[source_type_p24](#schemasource_type_p24)|false|none|none|
|receiver|[source_receiver_flow](#schemasource_receiver_flow)|false|none|none|
|redirect|[source_redirect_flow](#schemasource_redirect_flow)|false|none|none|
|sepa_debit|[source_type_sepa_debit](#schemasource_type_sepa_debit)|false|none|none|
|sofort|[source_type_sofort](#schemasource_type_sofort)|false|none|none|
|source_order|[source_order](#schemasource_order)|false|none|none|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Extra information about a source. This will appear on your customer's statement every time you charge the source.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the source, one of `canceled`, `chargeable`, `consumed`, `failed`, or `pending`. Only `chargeable` sources can be used to create a charge.|
|three_d_secure|[source_type_three_d_secure](#schemasource_type_three_d_secure)|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|The `type` of the source. The `type` is a payment method, one of `ach_credit_transfer`, `ach_debit`, `alipay`, `bancontact`, `card`, `card_present`, `eps`, `giropay`, `ideal`, `multibanco`, `klarna`, `p24`, `sepa_debit`, `sofort`, `three_d_secure`, or `wechat`. An additional hash is included on the source with a name matching this value. It contains additional information specific to the [payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/sources) used.|
|usage|string \| null|false|none|Either `reusable` or `single_use`. Whether this source should be reusable or not. Some source types may or may not be reusable by construction, while others may leave the option at creation. If an incompatible value is passed, an error will be returned.|
|wechat|[source_type_wechat](#schemasource_type_wechat)|false|none|none|

Source mandate notifications should be created when a notification related to
a source mandate must be sent to the payer. They will trigger a webhook or
deliver an email to the customer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acss_debit|[source_mandate_notification_acss_debit_data](#schemasource_mandate_notification_acss_debit_data)|false|none|none|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|A positive integer in the smallest currency unit (that is, 100 cents for $1.00, or 1 for ¥1, Japanese Yen being a zero-decimal currency) representing the amount associated with the mandate notification. The amount is expressed in the currency of the underlying source. Required if the notification type is `debit_initiated`.|
|bacs_debit|[source_mandate_notification_bacs_debit_data](#schemasource_mandate_notification_bacs_debit_data)|false|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|reason|string|true|none|The reason of the mandate notification. Valid reasons are `mandate_confirmed` or `debit_initiated`.|
|sepa_debit|[source_mandate_notification_sepa_debit_data](#schemasource_mandate_notification_sepa_debit_data)|false|none|none|
|source|[source](#schemasource)|true|none|`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They<br>represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API<br>just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be<br>attached to customers.<br><br>Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources).<br>We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods).<br>This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.<br><br>Related guides: [Sources API](https://docs.stripe.com/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/customers).|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the mandate notification. Valid statuses are `pending` or `submitted`.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of source this mandate notification is attached to. Should be the source type identifier code for the payment method, such as `three_d_secure`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|source_mandate_notification|

```json
  "refund_attributes_status": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|string \| null|false|none|The address of the receiver source. This is the value that should be communicated to the customer to send their funds to.|
|amount_charged|integer|true|none|The total amount that was moved to your balance. This is almost always equal to the amount charged. In rare cases when customers deposit excess funds and we are unable to refund those, those funds get moved to your balance and show up in amount_charged as well. The amount charged is expressed in the source's currency.|
|amount_received|integer|true|none|The total amount received by the receiver source. `amount_received = amount_returned + amount_charged` should be true for consumed sources unless customers deposit excess funds. The amount received is expressed in the source's currency.|
|amount_returned|integer|true|none|The total amount that was returned to the customer. The amount returned is expressed in the source's currency.|
|refund_attributes_method|string|true|none|Type of refund attribute method, one of `email`, `manual`, or `none`.|
|refund_attributes_status|string|true|none|Type of refund attribute status, one of `missing`, `requested`, or `available`.|

Some payment methods have no required amount that a customer must send.
Customers can be instructed to send any amount, and it can be made up of
multiple transactions. As such, sources can have multiple associated
transactions.
