Subscriptions allow you to charge a customer on a recurring basis.

Related guide: [Creating subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/creating)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect Application that created the subscription.|
|application_fee_percent|number \| null|false|none|A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account.|
|automatic_tax|[subscription_automatic_tax](#schemasubscription_automatic_tax)|true|none|none|
|billing_cycle_anchor|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The reference point that aligns future [billing cycle](https://docs.stripe.com/subscriptions/billing-cycle) dates. It sets the day of week for `week` intervals, the day of month for `month` and `year` intervals, and the month of year for `year` intervals. The timestamp is in UTC format.|
|billing_cycle_anchor_config|[subscriptions_resource_billing_cycle_anchor_config](#schemasubscriptions_resource_billing_cycle_anchor_config) \| null|false|none|The fixed values used to calculate the `billing_cycle_anchor`.|
|billing_mode|[subscriptions_resource_billing_mode](#schemasubscriptions_resource_billing_mode)|true|none|The billing mode of the subscription.|
|billing_schedules|[[subscriptions_resource_billing_schedules](#schemasubscriptions_resource_billing_schedules)]|true|none|Billing schedules for this subscription.|
|billing_thresholds|[subscription_billing_thresholds](#schemasubscription_billing_thresholds) \| null|false|none|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period|
|cancel_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|A date in the future at which the subscription will automatically get canceled|
|cancel_at_period_end|boolean|true|none|Whether this subscription will (if `status=active`) or did (if `status=canceled`) cancel at the end of the current billing period.|
|canceled_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has been canceled, the date of that cancellation. If the subscription was canceled with `cancel_at_period_end`, `canceled_at` will reflect the time of the most recent update request, not the end of the subscription period when the subscription is automatically moved to a canceled state.|
|cancellation_details|[cancellation_details](#schemacancellation_details) \| null|false|none|Details about why this subscription was cancelled|
|collection_method|string|true|none|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay this subscription at the end of the cycle using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer)|true|none|ID of the customer who owns the subscription.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|ID of the account representing the customer who owns the subscription.|
|days_until_due|integer \| null|false|none|Number of days a customer has to pay invoices generated by this subscription. This value will be `null` for subscriptions where `collection_method=charge_automatically`.|
|default_payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment method for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription. This takes precedence over `default_source`. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).|
|default_source|string \| [bank_account](#schemabank_account) \| [card](#schemacard) \| [source](#schemasource) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment source for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription and be in a chargeable state. If `default_payment_method` is also set, `default_payment_method` will take precedence. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).|
|default_tax_rates|[[tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The tax rates that will apply to any subscription item that does not have `tax_rates` set. Invoices created will have their `default_tax_rates` populated from the subscription.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The subscription's description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store an explanation of the subscription for rendering in Stripe surfaces and certain local payment methods UIs.|
|discounts|[string \| [discount](#schemadiscount)]|true|none|The discounts applied to the subscription. Subscription item discounts are applied before subscription discounts. Use `expand[]=discounts` to expand each discount.|
|ended_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has ended, the date the subscription ended.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice_settings|[subscriptions_resource_subscription_invoice_settings](#schemasubscriptions_resource_subscription_invoice_settings)|true|none|none|
|items|object|true|none|List of subscription items, each with an attached price.|
|latest_invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice) \| null|false|none|The most recent invoice this subscription has generated over its lifecycle (for example, when it cycles or is updated).|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|managed_payments|[smor_resource_managed_payments](#schemasmor_resource_managed_payments) \| null|false|none|Settings for Managed Payments for this Subscription and resulting [Invoices](/api/invoices/object) and [PaymentIntents](/api/payment_intents/object).|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|next_pending_invoice_item_invoice|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Specifies the approximate timestamp on which any pending invoice items will be billed according to the schedule provided at `pending_invoice_item_interval`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the charge was made on behalf of for charges associated with this subscription. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/subscriptions#on-behalf-of) for details.|
|pause_collection|[subscriptions_resource_pause_collection](#schemasubscriptions_resource_pause_collection) \| null|false|none|If specified, payment collection for this subscription will be paused. Note that the subscription status will be unchanged and will not be updated to `paused`. Learn more about [pausing collection](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pause-payment).|
|payment_settings|[subscriptions_resource_payment_settings](#schemasubscriptions_resource_payment_settings) \| null|false|none|Payment settings passed on to invoices created by the subscription.|
|pending_invoice_item_interval|[subscription_pending_invoice_item_interval](#schemasubscription_pending_invoice_item_interval) \| null|false|none|Specifies an interval for how often to bill for any pending invoice items. It is analogous to calling [Create an invoice](/api/invoices/create) for the given subscription at the specified interval.|
|pending_setup_intent|string \| [setup_intent](#schemasetup_intent) \| null|false|none|You can use this [SetupIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents) to collect user authentication when creating a subscription without immediate payment or updating a subscription's payment method, allowing you to optimize for off-session payments. Learn more in the [SCA Migration Guide](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/migration/strong-customer-authentication#scenario-2).|
|pending_update|[subscriptions_resource_pending_update](#schemasubscriptions_resource_pending_update) \| null|false|none|If specified, [pending updates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pending-updates) that will be applied to the subscription once the `latest_invoice` has been paid.|
|presentment_details|[subscriptions_resource_subscription_presentment_details](#schemasubscriptions_resource_subscription_presentment_details)|false|none|none|
|schedule|string \| [subscription_schedule](#schemasubscription_schedule) \| null|false|none|The schedule attached to the subscription|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Date when the subscription was first created. The date might differ from the `created` date due to backdating.|
|status|string|true|none|Possible values are `incomplete`, `incomplete_expired`, `trialing`, `active`, `past_due`, `canceled`, `unpaid`, or `paused`. <br><br>For `collection_method=charge_automatically` a subscription moves into `incomplete` if the initial payment attempt fails. A subscription in this status can only have metadata and default_source updated. Once the first invoice is paid, the subscription moves into an `active` status. If the first invoice is not paid within 23 hours, the subscription transitions to `incomplete_expired`. This is a terminal status, the open invoice will be voided and no further invoices will be generated. <br><br>A subscription that is currently in a trial period is `trialing` and moves to `active` when the trial period is over. <br><br>A subscription can only enter a `paused` status [when a trial ends without a payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials/free-trials#create-free-trials-without-payment). A `paused` subscription doesn't generate invoices and can be resumed after your customer adds their payment method. The `paused` status is different from [pausing collection](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pause-payment), which still generates invoices and leaves the subscription's status unchanged. <br><br>If subscription `collection_method=charge_automatically`, it becomes `past_due` when payment is required but cannot be paid (due to failed payment or awaiting additional user actions). Once Stripe has exhausted all payment retry attempts, the subscription will become `canceled` or `unpaid` (depending on your subscriptions settings). <br><br>If subscription `collection_method=send_invoice` it becomes `past_due` when its invoice is not paid by the due date, and `canceled` or `unpaid` if it is still not paid by an additional deadline after that. Note that when a subscription has a status of `unpaid`, no subsequent invoices will be attempted (invoices will be created, but then immediately automatically closed). After receiving updated payment information from a customer, you may choose to reopen and pay their closed invoices.|
|status_details|[subscriptions_resource_status_details_public](#schemasubscriptions_resource_status_details_public)|false|none|Describes changes to the subscription's status.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this subscription belongs to.|
|transfer_data|[subscription_transfer_data](#schemasubscription_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the subscription's payments will be attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from each payment will be transferred to for each of the subscription's invoices.|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has a trial, the end of that trial.|
|trial_settings|[subscriptions_resource_trial_settings_trial_settings](#schemasubscriptions_resource_trial_settings_trial_settings) \| null|false|none|Settings related to subscription trials.|
|trial_start|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has a trial, the beginning of that trial.|

|status|past_due|
|status|paused|
|status|trialing|
|status|unpaid|

<h2 id="tocS_subscription_billing_thresholds">subscription_billing_thresholds</h2>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_gte|integer \| null|false|none|Monetary threshold that triggers the subscription to create an invoice|
|reset_billing_cycle_anchor|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates if the `billing_cycle_anchor` should be reset when a threshold is reached. If true, `billing_cycle_anchor` will be updated to the date/time the threshold was last reached; otherwise, the value will remain unchanged. This value may not be `true` if the subscription contains items with plans that have `aggregate_usage=last_ever`.|

Subscription items allow you to create customer subscriptions with more than
one plan, making it easy to represent complex billing relationships.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|billed_until|integer(unix-time)|false|none|The time period the subscription item has been billed for.|
|billing_thresholds|[subscription_item_billing_thresholds](#schemasubscription_item_billing_thresholds) \| null|false|none|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the related subscription advanced to a new billing period|
|created|integer|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|current_period_end|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The end time of this subscription item's current billing period.|
|current_period_start|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The start time of this subscription item's current billing period.|
|current_trial|[subscriptions_trials_resource_current_trial](#schemasubscriptions_trials_resource_current_trial) \| null|false|none|The current trial that is applied to this subscription item.|
|discounts|[string \| [discount](#schemadiscount)]|true|none|The discounts applied to the subscription item. Subscription item discounts are applied before subscription discounts. Use `expand[]=discounts` to expand each discount.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|price|[price](#schemaprice)|true|none|Prices define the unit cost, currency, and (optional) billing cycle for both recurring and one-time purchases of products.<br>[Products](https://docs.stripe.com/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and prices help you track payment terms. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by prices. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme.<br><br>For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has prices for $10/month, $100/year, and €9 once.<br><br>Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription), [create an invoice](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/create), and more about [products and prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/overview).|
|quantity|integer|false|none|The [quantity](https://docs.stripe.com/subscriptions/quantities) of the plan to which the customer should be subscribed.|
|subscription|string|true|none|The `subscription` this `subscription_item` belongs to.|
|tax_rates|[[tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The tax rates which apply to this `subscription_item`. When set, the `default_tax_rates` on the subscription do not apply to this `subscription_item`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|subscription_item|

A subscription schedule allows you to create and manage the lifecycle of a subscription by predefining expected changes.

Related guide: [Subscription schedules](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect Application that created the schedule.|
|billing_mode|[subscriptions_resource_billing_mode](#schemasubscriptions_resource_billing_mode)|true|none|The billing mode of the subscription.|
|canceled_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the subscription schedule was canceled. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|completed_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the subscription schedule was completed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|current_phase|[subscription_schedule_current_phase](#schemasubscription_schedule_current_phase) \| null|false|none|Object representing the start and end dates for the current phase of the subscription schedule, if it is `active`.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer)|true|none|ID of the customer who owns the subscription schedule.|
|customer_account|string \| null|false|none|ID of the account who owns the subscription schedule.|
|default_settings|[subscription_schedules_resource_default_settings](#schemasubscription_schedules_resource_default_settings)|true|none|none|
|end_behavior|string|true|none|Behavior of the subscription schedule and underlying subscription when it ends. Possible values are `release` or `cancel` with the default being `release`. `release` will end the subscription schedule and keep the underlying subscription running. `cancel` will end the subscription schedule and cancel the underlying subscription.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|pause_schedules|[[subscription_schedules_resource_pause_schedule](#schemasubscription_schedules_resource_pause_schedule)]|false|none|The pause schedules for this subscription schedule.|
|phases|[[subscription_schedule_phase_configuration](#schemasubscription_schedule_phase_configuration)]|true|none|Configuration for the subscription schedule's phases.|
|released_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the subscription schedule was released. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|released_subscription|string \| null|false|none|ID of the subscription once managed by the subscription schedule (if it is released).|
|status|string|true|none|The present status of the subscription schedule. Possible values are `not_started`, `active`, `completed`, `released`, and `canceled`. You can read more about the different states in our [behavior guide](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules).|
|subscription|string \| [subscription](#schemasubscription) \| null|false|none|ID of the subscription managed by the subscription schedule.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this subscription schedule belongs to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|end_behavior|cancel|
|end_behavior|none|
|end_behavior|release|
|end_behavior|renew|
|object|subscription_schedule|
|status|active|
|status|canceled|
|status|completed|
|status|not_started|
|status|released|

A phase describes the plans, coupon, and trialing status of a subscription for a predefined time period.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add_invoice_items|[[subscription_schedule_add_invoice_item](#schemasubscription_schedule_add_invoice_item)]|true|none|A list of prices and quantities that will generate invoice items appended to the next invoice for this phase.|
|application_fee_percent|number \| null|false|none|A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account during this phase of the schedule.|
|automatic_tax|[schedules_phase_automatic_tax](#schemaschedules_phase_automatic_tax)|false|none|none|
|billing_cycle_anchor|string \| null|false|none|Possible values are `phase_start` or `automatic`. If `phase_start` then billing cycle anchor of the subscription is set to the start of the phase when entering the phase. If `automatic` then the billing cycle anchor is automatically modified as needed when entering the phase. For more information, see the billing cycle [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/billing-cycle).|
|billing_thresholds|[subscription_billing_thresholds](#schemasubscription_billing_thresholds) \| null|false|none|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period|
|collection_method|string \| null|false|none|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay the underlying subscription at the end of each billing cycle using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|default_payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment method for the subscription schedule. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription schedule. If not set, invoices will use the default payment method in the customer's invoice settings.|
|default_tax_rates|[[tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The default tax rates to apply to the subscription during this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Subscription description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store an explanation of the subscription for rendering in Stripe surfaces and certain local payment methods UIs.|
|discounts|[[stackable_discount_with_discount_settings_and_discount_end](#schemastackable_discount_with_discount_settings_and_discount_end)]|true|none|The stackable discounts that will be applied to the subscription on this phase. Subscription item discounts are applied before subscription discounts.|
|end_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The end of this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|invoice_settings|[invoice_setting_subscription_schedule_phase_setting](#schemainvoice_setting_subscription_schedule_phase_setting) \| null|false|none|The invoice settings applicable during this phase.|
|items|[[subscription_schedule_configuration_item](#schemasubscription_schedule_configuration_item)]|true|none|Subscription items to configure the subscription to during this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to a phase. Metadata on a schedule's phase will update the underlying subscription's `metadata` when the phase is entered. Updating the underlying subscription's `metadata` directly will not affect the current phase's `metadata`.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the charge was made on behalf of for charges associated with the schedule's subscription. See the Connect documentation for details.|
|proration_behavior|string|true|none|When transitioning phases, controls how prorations are handled (if any). Possible values are `create_prorations`, `none`, and `always_invoice`.|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The start of this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|transfer_data|[subscription_transfer_data](#schemasubscription_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the associated subscription's payments will be attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from each payment will be transferred to for each of the subscription's invoices.|
|trial|boolean|false|none|If set to true the entire phase is counted as a trial and the customer will not be charged for any fees.|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|When the trial ends within the phase.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|billing_cycle_anchor|automatic|
|billing_cycle_anchor|phase_start|
|collection_method|charge_automatically|
|collection_method|send_invoice|
|proration_behavior|always_invoice|
|proration_behavior|create_prorations|
|proration_behavior|none|

Pending Updates store the changes pending from a previous update that will be applied
to the Subscription upon successful payment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|billing_cycle_anchor|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the update is applied, determines the date of the first full invoice, and, for plans with `month` or `year` intervals, the day of the month for subsequent invoices. The timestamp is in UTC format.|
|cancel_at_period_end|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates whether this subscription should cancel at the end of the current period if the update is applied.|
|discount|[discount](#schemadiscount) \| null|false|none|The pending subscription-level discount that will be applied when the pending update is applied.|
|discounts|[string \| [discount](#schemadiscount)]|false|none|The discounts that will be applied to the subscription when the pending update is applied. Use `expand[]=discounts` to expand each discount.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The point after which the changes reflected by this update will be discarded and no longer applied.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|subscription_items|[[subscription_item](#schemasubscription_item)]|false|none|List of subscription items, each with an attached plan, that will be set if the update is applied.|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp representing the end of the trial period the customer will get before being charged for the first time, if the update is applied.|
|trial_from_plan|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates if a plan's `trial_period_days` should be applied to the subscription. Setting `trial_end` per subscription is preferred, and this defaults to `false`. Setting this flag to `true` together with `trial_end` is not allowed. See [Using trial periods on subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials/free-trials) to learn more.|

```json
        "tax_type": "admissions_tax"
      },
      "taxability_reason": "customer_exempt",
      "taxable_amount": 0
    }
  ],
  "tax_date": 0
}
```

A Tax Calculation allows you to calculate the tax to collect from your customer.

Related guide: [Calculate tax in your custom payment flow](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/custom)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_total|integer|true|none|Total amount after taxes in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minor-units).|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| null|false|none|The ID of an existing [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object) used for the resource.|
|customer_details|[tax_product_resource_customer_details](#schematax_product_resource_customer_details)|true|none|none|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp of date at which the tax calculation will expire.|
|id|string \| null|false|none|Unique identifier for the calculation.|
|line_items|object \| null|false|none|The list of items the customer is purchasing.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|ship_from_details|[tax_product_resource_ship_from_details](#schematax_product_resource_ship_from_details) \| null|false|none|The details of the ship from location, such as the address.|
|shipping_cost|[tax_product_resource_tax_calculation_shipping_cost](#schematax_product_resource_tax_calculation_shipping_cost) \| null|false|none|The shipping cost details for the calculation.|
|tax_amount_exclusive|integer|true|none|The amount of tax to be collected on top of the line item prices.|
|tax_amount_inclusive|integer|true|none|The amount of tax already included in the line item prices.|
|tax_breakdown|[[tax_product_resource_tax_breakdown](#schematax_product_resource_tax_breakdown)]|true|none|Breakdown of individual tax amounts that add up to the total.|
|tax_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The calculation uses the tax rules and rates that are in effect at this timestamp. You can use a date up to 31 days in the past or up to 31 days in the future. If you use a future date, Stripe doesn't guarantee that the expected tax rules and rate being used match the actual rules and rate that will be in effect on that date. We deploy tax changes before their effective date, but not within a fixed window.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|tax.calculation|

A Tax Calculation Line Item represents a single item in a tax calculation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The line item amount in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minor-units). If `tax_behavior=inclusive`, then this amount includes taxes. Otherwise, taxes were calculated on top of this amount.|
|amount_tax|integer|true|none|The amount of tax calculated for this line item, in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minor-units).|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|performance_location|string \| null|false|none|Indicates the line item represents a performance where the venue location might determine the tax, not the customer address. Leave empty if the tax code doesn't require a tax location. If you provide this value for tax codes with an `optional` location requirement, it overrides the customer address.|
|product|string \| null|false|none|The ID of an existing [Product](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/object).|
|quantity|integer|true|none|The number of units of the item being purchased. For reversals, this is the quantity reversed.|
|reference|string|true|none|A custom identifier for this line item.|
|tax_behavior|string|true|none|Specifies whether the `amount` includes taxes. If `tax_behavior=inclusive`, then the amount includes taxes.|
|tax_breakdown|[[tax_product_resource_line_item_tax_breakdown](#schematax_product_resource_line_item_tax_breakdown)]|false|none|Detailed account of taxes relevant to this line item.|
|tax_code|string|true|none|The [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-categories) ID used for this resource.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|tax.calculation_line_item|
|tax_behavior|exclusive|
|tax_behavior|inclusive|

A Tax `Registration` lets us know that your business is registered to collect tax on payments within a region, enabling you to [automatically collect tax](https://docs.stripe.com/tax).

Stripe doesn't register on your behalf with the relevant authorities when you create a Tax `Registration` object. For more information on how to register to collect tax, see [our guide](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/registering).

Related guide: [Using the Registrations API](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/registrations-api)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_from|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the registration becomes active. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|country|string|true|none|Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).|
|country_options|[tax_product_registrations_resource_country_options](#schematax_product_registrations_resource_country_options)|true|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If set, the registration stops being active at this time. If not set, the registration will be active indefinitely. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the registration. This field is present for convenience and can be deduced from `active_from` and `expires_at`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|tax.registration|
|status|active|
|status|expired|
|status|scheduled|

A Tax Transaction records the tax collected from or refunded to your customer.

Related guide: [Calculate tax in your custom payment flow](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/custom#tax-transaction)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| null|false|none|The ID of an existing [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object) used for the resource.|
|customer_details|[tax_product_resource_customer_details](#schematax_product_resource_customer_details)|true|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the transaction.|
|line_items|object \| null|false|none|The tax collected or refunded, by line item.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|posted_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The Unix timestamp representing when the tax liability is assumed or reduced.|
|reference|string|true|none|A custom unique identifier, such as 'myOrder_123'.|
|reversal|[tax_product_resource_tax_transaction_resource_reversal](#schematax_product_resource_tax_transaction_resource_reversal) \| null|false|none|If `type=reversal`, contains information about what was reversed.|
|ship_from_details|[tax_product_resource_ship_from_details](#schematax_product_resource_ship_from_details) \| null|false|none|The details of the ship from location, such as the address.|
|shipping_cost|[tax_product_resource_tax_transaction_shipping_cost](#schematax_product_resource_tax_transaction_shipping_cost) \| null|false|none|The shipping cost details for the transaction.|
|tax_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The calculation uses the tax rules and rates that are in effect at this timestamp. You can use a date up to 31 days in the past or up to 31 days in the future. If you use a future date, Stripe doesn't guarantee that the expected tax rules and rate being used match the actual rules and rate that will be in effect on that date. We deploy tax changes before their effective date, but not within a fixed window.|
|type|string|true|none|If `reversal`, this transaction reverses an earlier transaction.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|tax.transaction|
|type|reversal|
|type|transaction|

A Tax Transaction Line Item represents an individual item in a Tax Transaction.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The line item amount in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minor-units). If `tax_behavior=inclusive`, then this amount includes taxes. Otherwise, taxes were calculated on top of this amount.|
|amount_tax|integer|true|none|The amount of tax calculated for this line item, in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minor-units).|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|product|string \| null|false|none|The ID of an existing [Product](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/object).|
|quantity|integer|true|none|The number of units of the item being purchased. For reversals, this is the quantity reversed.|
|reference|string|true|none|A custom identifier for this line item in the transaction.|
|reversal|[tax_product_resource_tax_transaction_line_item_resource_reversal](#schematax_product_resource_tax_transaction_line_item_resource_reversal) \| null|false|none|If `type=reversal`, contains information about what was reversed.|
|tax_behavior|string|true|none|Specifies whether the `amount` includes taxes. If `tax_behavior=inclusive`, then the amount includes taxes.|
|tax_code|string|true|none|The [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-categories) ID used for this resource.|
|type|string|true|none|If `reversal`, this line item reverses an earlier transaction.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|object|tax.transaction_line_item|
|tax_behavior|exclusive|
|tax_behavior|inclusive|
|type|reversal|
|type|transaction|

You can add one or multiple tax IDs to a [customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers) or account.
Customer and account tax IDs get displayed on related invoices and credit notes.

Related guides: [Customer tax identification numbers](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-ids), [Account tax IDs](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/connect#account-tax-ids)

<h2 id="tocS_tax_rate">tax_rate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematax_rate"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,

  "description": "string",
  "display_name": "string",
  "effective_percentage": 0,
  "flat_amount": {

  },

  "jurisdiction_level": "city",

    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },

  "percentage": 0,
  "rate_type": "flat_amount",
  "state": "string",
  "tax_type": "amusement_tax"
}
```

Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax.

Related guide: [Tax rates](/billing/taxes/tax-rates)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Defaults to `true`. When set to `false`, this tax rate cannot be used with new applications or Checkout Sessions, but will still work for subscriptions and invoices that already have it set.|
|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the tax rate for your internal use only. It will not be visible to your customers.|
|display_name|string|true|none|The display name of the tax rates as it will appear to your customer on their receipt email, PDF, and the hosted invoice page.|
|effective_percentage|number \| null|false|none|Actual/effective tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true,<br>this percentage reflects the rate actually used to calculate tax based on the product's taxability<br>and whether the user is registered to collect taxes in the corresponding jurisdiction.|
|flat_amount|[tax_rate_flat_amount](#schematax_rate_flat_amount) \| null|false|none|The amount of the tax rate when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. Tax rates with `rate_type` `percentage` can vary based on the transaction, resulting in this field being `null`. This field exposes the amount and currency of the flat tax rate.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|inclusive|boolean|true|none|This specifies if the tax rate is inclusive or exclusive.|
|jurisdiction|string \| null|false|none|The jurisdiction for the tax rate. You can use this label field for tax reporting purposes. It also appears on your customer’s invoice.|
|jurisdiction_level|string \| null|false|none|The level of the jurisdiction that imposes this tax rate. Will be `null` for manually defined tax rates.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|percentage|number|true|none|Tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage includes the statutory tax rate of non-taxable jurisdictions.|
|rate_type|string \| null|false|none|Indicates the type of tax rate applied to the taxable amount. This value can be `null` when no tax applies to the location. This field is only present for TaxRates created by Stripe Tax.|
|state|string \| null|false|none|[ISO 3166-2 subdivision code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2), without country prefix. For example, "NY" for New York, United States.|
|tax_type|string \| null|false|none|The high-level tax type, such as `vat` or `sales_tax`.|

<h2 id="tocS_tax_rate_flat_amount">tax_rate_flat_amount</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematax_rate_flat_amount"></a>
<a id="schema_tax_rate_flat_amount"></a>
<a id="tocStax_rate_flat_amount"></a>
<a id="tocstax_rate_flat_amount"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "currency": "string"
}
```

The amount of the tax rate when the `rate_type`` is `flat_amount`. Tax rates with `rate_type` `percentage` can vary based on the transaction, resulting in this field being `null`. This field exposes the amount and currency of the flat tax rate.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount of the tax when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. This positive integer represents how much to charge in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase.|

A Reader represents a physical device for accepting payment details.

Related guide: [Connecting to a reader](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/payments/connect-reader)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_reader_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_reader_action) \| null|false|none|The most recent action performed by the reader.|
|device_sw_version|string \| null|false|none|The current software version of the reader.|
|device_type|string|true|none|Device type of the reader.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|ip_address|string \| null|false|none|The local IP address of the reader.|
|label|string|true|none|Custom label given to the reader for easier identification.|
|last_seen_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The last time this reader reported to Stripe backend. Timestamp is measured in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Unlike most other Stripe timestamp fields which use seconds, this field uses milliseconds.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|location|string \| [terminal.location](#schematerminal.location) \| null|false|none|The location identifier of the reader.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|serial_number|string|true|none|Serial number of the reader.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|The networking status of the reader. This value is `null` for mobile readers. We do not recommend using this field in flows that may block taking payments.|

Represents an action performed by the reader

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_error|[api_errors](#schemaapi_errors) \| null|false|none|The reader action failed due to an [API error](https://docs.stripe.com/api/errors). Only present when `status` is `failed` and the underlying failure was an API error. Avoid parsing the `message` field for programmatic logic; use `type` or `code` instead. The `message` field is for display to humans only and may be updated at anytime. Requires [reader version](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-reader-s700-s710#reader-software-version) 2.42 or later. Readers on older versions always return null.|
|collect_inputs|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_collect_inputs_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_collect_inputs_action)|false|none|Represents a reader action to collect customer inputs|
|collect_payment_method|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_collect_payment_method_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_collect_payment_method_action)|false|none|Represents a reader action to collect a payment method|
|confirm_payment_intent|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_confirm_payment_intent_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_confirm_payment_intent_action)|false|none|Represents a reader action to confirm a payment|
|failure_code|string \| null|false|none|Failure code, only set if status is `failed`.|
|failure_message|string \| null|false|none|Detailed failure message, only set if status is `failed`.|
|print_content|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_print_content](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_print_content)|false|none|Represents a reader action to print content|
|process_payment_intent|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_process_payment_intent_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_process_payment_intent_action)|false|none|Represents a reader action to process a payment intent|
|process_setup_intent|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_process_setup_intent_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_process_setup_intent_action)|false|none|Represents a reader action to process a setup intent|
|refund_payment|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_refund_payment_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_refund_payment_action)|false|none|Represents a reader action to refund a payment|
|set_reader_display|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_set_reader_display_action](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_set_reader_display_action)|false|none|Represents a reader action to set the reader display|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the action performed by the reader.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of action performed by the reader.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|failed|
|status|in_progress|
|status|succeeded|

```json
  "amount": 0,
  "charge": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "payment_intent": "string",
  "reason": "duplicate",
  "refund": "string",
  "refund_application_fee": true,
  "refund_payment_config": {
    "enable_customer_cancellation": true
  },
  "reverse_transfer": true
}
```

Represents a reader action to refund a payment

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|false|none|The amount being refunded.|
|charge|string \| [charge](#schemacharge)|false|none|Charge that is being refunded.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|false|none|Payment intent that is being refunded.|
|reason|string|false|none|The reason for the refund.|
|refund|string \| [refund](#schemarefund)|false|none|Unique identifier for the refund object.|
|refund_application_fee|boolean|false|none|Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when refunding this charge. If a full charge refund is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded in an amount proportional to the amount of the charge refunded. An application fee can be refunded only by the application that created the charge.|
|refund_payment_config|[terminal_reader_reader_resource_refund_payment_config](#schematerminal_reader_reader_resource_refund_payment_config)|false|none|Represents a per-transaction override of a reader configuration|
|reverse_transfer|boolean|false|none|Boolean indicating whether the transfer should be reversed when refunding this charge. The transfer will be reversed proportionally to the amount being refunded (either the entire or partial amount). A transfer can be reversed only by the application that created the charge.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|reason|duplicate|
|reason|fraudulent|
|reason|requested_by_customer|

<h2 id="tocS_test_helpers.test_clock">test_helpers.test_clock</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematest_helpers.test_clock"></a>
<a id="schema_test_helpers.test_clock"></a>
<a id="tocStest_helpers.test_clock"></a>
<a id="tocstest_helpers.test_clock"></a>

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "deletes_after": 0,
  "frozen_time": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "name": "string",
  "object": "test_helpers.test_clock",
  "status": "advancing",
  "status_details": {
    "advancing": {
      "target_frozen_time": 0
    }
  }
}
```

A test clock enables deterministic control over objects in testmode. With a test clock, you can create
objects at a frozen time in the past or future, and advance to a specific future time to observe webhooks and state changes. After the clock advances,
you can either validate the current state of your scenario (and test your assumptions), change the current state of your scenario (and test more complex scenarios), or keep advancing forward in time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|deletes_after|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which this clock is scheduled to auto delete.|
|frozen_time|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which all objects belonging to this clock are frozen.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The custom name supplied at creation.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the Test Clock.|
|status_details|[billing_clocks_resource_status_details_status_details](#schemabilling_clocks_resource_status_details_status_details)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|test_helpers.test_clock|
|status|advancing|
|status|internal_failure|
|status|ready|

Related guide: [Standalone 3DS](/payments/3d-secure/standalone-3d-secure)

|challenge_url|string|false|none|The URL for presenting a challenge to your cardholder, present if status is requires_challenge.|
|channel|[three_d_secure_standalone_resource_channel](#schemathree_d_secure_standalone_resource_channel)|true|none|Contains details on the channel used (browser, 3RI) for a standalone 3DS Authentication.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|

|directory_server|string|true|none|The 3DS directory server with which this 3DS Authentication was processed.|
|fingerprinting_url|string|false|none|The URL for performing issuer fingerprinting, present if fingerprinting is supported for the given payment method.|
|flow_preference|[three_d_secure_standalone_resource_flow_preference](#schemathree_d_secure_standalone_resource_flow_preference)|false|none|Contains details of the flow preference used for a standalone 3DS Authentication.|

|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|

```json
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "networks": {
      "preferred": "string"
    },
    "object": "card",
    "regulated_status": "regulated",
    "status": "string",
    "tokenization_method": "string"
  },
  "client_ip": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "token",
  "type": "string",
  "used": true
}
```

Tokenization is the process Stripe uses to collect sensitive card or bank
account details, or personally identifiable information (PII), directly from
your customers in a secure manner. A token representing this information is
returned to your server to use. Use our
[recommended payments integrations](https://docs.stripe.com/payments) to perform this process
on the client-side. This guarantees that no sensitive card data touches your server,
and allows your integration to operate in a PCI-compliant way.

If you can't use client-side tokenization, you can also create tokens using
the API with either your publishable or secret API key. If
your integration uses this method, you're responsible for any PCI compliance
that it might require, and you must keep your secret API key safe. Unlike with
client-side tokenization, your customer's information isn't sent directly to
Stripe, so we can't determine how it's handled or stored.

You can't store or use tokens more than once. To store card or bank account
information for later use, create [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#customers)
objects or [External accounts](/api#external_accounts).
[Radar](https://docs.stripe.com/radar), our integrated solution for automatic fraud protection,
performs best with integrations that use client-side tokenization.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bank_account|[bank_account](#schemabank_account)|false|none|These bank accounts are payment methods on `Customer` objects.<br><br>On the other hand [External Accounts](/api#external_accounts) are transfer<br>destinations on `Account` objects for connected accounts.<br>They can be bank accounts or debit cards as well, and are documented in the links above.<br><br>Related guide: [Bank debits and transfers](/payments/bank-debits-transfers)|
|card|[card](#schemacard)|false|none|You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer<br>later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to<br>transfer to those cards later.<br><br>Related guide: [Card payments with Sources](https://docs.stripe.com/sources/cards)|
|client_ip|string \| null|false|none|IP address of the client that generates the token.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of the token: `account`, `bank_account`, `card`, or `pii`.|
|used|boolean|true|none|Determines if you have already used this token (you can only use tokens once).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|token|

To top up your Stripe balance, you create a top-up object. You can retrieve
individual top-ups, as well as list all top-ups. Top-ups are identified by a
unique, random ID.

Related guide: [Topping up your platform account](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/top-ups)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount transferred.|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this top-up on your account balance. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|expected_availability_date|integer \| null|false|none|Date the funds are expected to arrive in your Stripe account for payouts. This factors in delays like weekends or bank holidays. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.|
|failure_code|string \| null|false|none|Error code explaining reason for top-up failure if available (see [the errors section](/api/errors) for a list of codes).|
|failure_message|string \| null|false|none|Message to user further explaining reason for top-up failure if available.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|initiated_by|string \| null|false|none|Indicates whether the top-up was initiated by Stripe or by the user.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|The ID of a PaymentMethod representing the payment method used for the top-up. A PaymentMethod of type `us_bank_account` can be used.|
|payment_method_options|[topup_resource_payment_method_options](#schematopup_resource_payment_method_options) \| null|false|none|Payment-method-specific configuration for this top-up.|
|source|[source](#schemasource) \| null|false|none|The source field is deprecated. It might not always be present in the API response.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Extra information about a top-up. This will appear on your source's bank statement. It must contain at least one letter.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the top-up is either `canceled`, `failed`, `pending`, `reversed`, or `succeeded`.|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies this top-up as part of a group.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|initiated_by|stripe|
|initiated_by|user|
|object|topup|
|status|canceled|
|status|failed|
|status|pending|
|status|reversed|
|status|succeeded|

A `Transfer` object is created when you move funds between Stripe accounts as
part of Connect.

Before April 6, 2017, transfers also represented movement of funds from a
Stripe account to a card or bank account. This behavior has since been split
out into a [Payout](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payout_object) object, with corresponding payout endpoints. For more
information, read about the
[transfer/payout split](https://docs.stripe.com/transfer-payout-split).

Related guide: [Creating separate charges and transfers](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be transferred.|
|amount_reversed|integer|true|none|Amount in cents (or local equivalent) reversed (can be less than the amount attribute on the transfer if a partial reversal was issued).|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Balance transaction that describes the impact of this transfer on your account balance.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time that this record of the transfer was first created.|
|currency|string(currency)|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|destination|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|ID of the Stripe account the transfer was sent to.|
|destination_payment|string \| [charge](#schemacharge)|false|none|If the destination is a Stripe account, this will be the ID of the payment that the destination account received for the transfer.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|reversals|object|true|none|A list of reversals that have been applied to the transfer.|
|reversed|boolean|true|none|Whether the transfer has been fully reversed. If the transfer is only partially reversed, this attribute will still be false.|
|source_transaction|string \| [charge](#schemacharge) \| null|false|none|ID of the charge that was used to fund the transfer. If null, the transfer was funded from the available balance.|
|source_type|string|false|none|The source balance this transfer came from. One of `card`, `fpx`, or `bank_account`.|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|transfer|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|amount|integer|false|none|The amount transferred to the destination account. This transfer will occur automatically after the payment succeeds. If no amount is specified, by default the entire payment amount is transferred to the destination account.<br> The amount must be less than or equal to the [amount](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object#payment_intent_object-amount), and must be a positive integer<br> representing how much to transfer in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00).|
|description|string|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the transfer. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|destination|string \| [account](#schemaaccount)|true|none|The account (if any) that the payment is attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from the payment are transferred to after payment success.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|payment_data|[payment_data](#schemapayment_data)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_transfer_reversal">transfer_reversal</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfer_reversal"></a>
<a id="schema_transfer_reversal"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "balance_transaction": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "destination_payment_refund": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "transfer_reversal",
  "source_refund": "string",
  "transfer": "string"
}
```

[Stripe Connect](https://docs.stripe.com/connect) platforms can reverse transfers made to a
connected account, either entirely or partially, and can also specify whether
to refund any related application fees. Transfer reversals add to the
platform's balance and subtract from the destination account's balance.

Reversing a transfer that was made for a [destination
charge](/docs/connect/destination-charges) is allowed only up to the amount of
the charge. It is possible to reverse a
[transfer_group](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options)
transfer only if the destination account has enough balance to cover the
reversal.

Related guide: [Reverse transfers](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#reverse-transfers)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount, in cents (or local equivalent).|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delay_days|integer|true|none|The number of days charges for the account will be held before being paid out.|
|interval|string|true|none|How frequently funds will be paid out. One of `manual` (payouts only created via API call), `daily`, `weekly`, or `monthly`.|
|monthly_anchor|integer|false|none|The day of the month funds will be paid out. Only shown if `interval` is monthly. Payouts scheduled between the 29th and 31st of the month are sent on the last day of shorter months.|
|monthly_payout_days|[integer]|false|none|The days of the month funds will be paid out. Only shown if `interval` is monthly. Payouts scheduled between the 29th and 31st of the month are sent on the last day of shorter months.|
|weekly_anchor|string|false|none|The day of the week funds will be paid out, of the style 'monday', 'tuesday', etc. Only shown if `interval` is weekly.|
|weekly_payout_days|[string]|false|none|The days of the week when available funds are paid out, specified as an array, for example, [`monday`, `tuesday`]. Only shown if `interval` is weekly.|

Stripe Treasury for Platforms provides users with a container for money called a FinancialAccount that is separate from their Payments balance.
FinancialAccounts serve as the source and destination of Treasury for Platform’s money movement APIs.

|features|[treasury.financial_account_features](#schematreasury.financial_account_features)|false|none|Encodes whether a FinancialAccount has access to a particular Feature, with a `status` enum and associated `status_details`.<br>Stripe or the platform can control Features via the requested field.|
|financial_addresses|[[treasury_financial_accounts_resource_financial_address](#schematreasury_financial_accounts_resource_financial_address)]|true|none|The set of credentials that resolve to a FinancialAccount.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|

Use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_transfers).

Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|credit_reversal|[treasury.credit_reversal](#schematreasury.credit_reversal)|false|none|You can reverse some [ReceivedCredits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_credits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedCredit leads to the creation of a new object known as a CreditReversal.|
|outbound_payment|[treasury.outbound_payment](#schematreasury.outbound_payment)|false|none|Use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_transfers).<br><br>Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.<br><br>Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundPayment objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments)|
|outbound_transfer|[treasury.outbound_transfer](#schematreasury.outbound_transfer)|false|none|Use [OutboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) to transfer funds from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) to a PaymentMethod belonging to the same entity. To send funds to a different party, use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_payments) instead. You can send funds over ACH rails or through a domestic wire transfer to a user's own external bank account.<br><br>Simulate OutboundTransfer state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_transfers` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.<br><br>Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers)|
|payout|[payout](#schemapayout)|false|none|A `Payout` object is created when you receive funds from Stripe, or when you<br>initiate a payout to either a bank account or debit card of a [connected<br>Stripe account](/docs/connect/bank-debit-card-payouts). You can retrieve individual payouts,<br>and list all payouts. Payouts are made on [varying<br>schedules](/docs/connect/manage-payout-schedule), depending on your country and<br>industry.<br><br>Related guide: [Receiving payouts](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts)|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the source flow that originated the ReceivedCredit.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|credit_reversal|
|type|other|
|type|outbound_payment|
|type|outbound_transfer|
|type|payout|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|credit_reversal|[treasury.credit_reversal](#schematreasury.credit_reversal)|false|none|You can reverse some [ReceivedCredits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_credits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedCredit leads to the creation of a new object known as a CreditReversal.|
|debit_reversal|[treasury.debit_reversal](#schematreasury.debit_reversal)|false|none|You can reverse some [ReceivedDebits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_debits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedDebit leads to the creation of a new object known as a DebitReversal.|
|inbound_transfer|[treasury.inbound_transfer](#schematreasury.inbound_transfer)|false|none|Use [InboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers) to add funds to your [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) via a PaymentMethod that is owned by you. The funds will be transferred via an ACH debit.<br><br>Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using InboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers)|
|issuing_authorization|[issuing.authorization](#schemaissuing.authorization)|false|none|When an [issued card](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing) is used to make a purchase, an Issuing `Authorization`<br>object is created. [Authorizations](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/purchases/authorizations) must be approved for the<br>purchase to be completed successfully.<br><br>Related guide: [Issued card authorizations](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/purchases/authorizations)|
|outbound_payment|[treasury.outbound_payment](#schematreasury.outbound_payment)|false|none|Use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_transfers).<br><br>Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.<br><br>Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundPayment objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments)|
|outbound_transfer|[treasury.outbound_transfer](#schematreasury.outbound_transfer)|false|none|Use [OutboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) to transfer funds from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) to a PaymentMethod belonging to the same entity. To send funds to a different party, use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_payments) instead. You can send funds over ACH rails or through a domestic wire transfer to a user's own external bank account.<br><br>Simulate OutboundTransfer state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_transfers` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.<br><br>Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers)|
|received_credit|[treasury.received_credit](#schematreasury.received_credit)|false|none|ReceivedCredits represent funds sent to a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) (for example, via ACH or wire). These money movements are not initiated from the FinancialAccount.|
|received_debit|[treasury.received_debit](#schematreasury.received_debit)|false|none|ReceivedDebits represent funds pulled from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). These are not initiated from the FinancialAccount.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of the flow that created the Transaction. Set to the same value as `flow_type`.|

<h2 id="tocS_webhook_endpoint">webhook_endpoint</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawebhook_endpoint"></a>
<a id="schema_webhook_endpoint"></a>
<a id="tocSwebhook_endpoint"></a>
<a id="tocswebhook_endpoint"></a>

```json
{
  "api_version": "string",
  "application": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "description": "string",
  "enabled_events": [
    "string"
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "webhook_endpoint",
  "secret": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "url": "string"
}
```

You can configure [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/) via the API to be
notified about events that happen in your Stripe account or connected
accounts.

Most users configure webhooks from [the dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks), which provides a user interface for registering and testing your webhook endpoints.

Related guide: [Setting up webhooks](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/configure)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_version|string \| null|false|none|The API version that events are rendered as for this webhook endpoint. You can't change this value after you create the endpoint.|
|application|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the associated Connect application.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An optional description of what the webhook is used for.|
|enabled_events|[string]|true|none|The list of events to enable for this endpoint. `['*']` indicates that all events are enabled, except those that require explicit selection.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|secret|string|false|none|The endpoint's secret, used to generate [webhook signatures](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/signatures). Only returned at creation.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the webhook. It can be `enabled` or `disabled`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL of the webhook endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|webhook_endpoint|
